News.title: Moment man is confronted after ‘breaking goose’s neck’ in public park – as cops launch probe
News.content:
Next

THIS is the moment a man is confronted after allegedly breaking a goose’s neck in a public park – as cops probe the “attack”.

Shocked bystanders accuse the hooded man of “killing” the bird, which is shown writhing on the ground at Ward End Park in Birmingham.



Disturbing footage circulating across social media shows the man ignoring his accusers as they film him holding a box seemingly filled with bread.

West Midlands Police confirmed officers are probing a report of animal cruelty at the park on October 19.



After showing the animal twitching on the grass, the bystander pans back to the suspect who is seen breaking slices of bread in his hands.

The goose can be heard letting out pained squeals as the bystanders shout at the man, dressed in a Nike hoodie and long black coat, to “stop”.



He continues to look blankly at the camera as he is told “you can’t do this”.

The man filming claims: “He’s feeding ducks and he has just killed one.



“He’s just broken the duck’s neck… This is what he has done to it. The poor animal.

“This guy… you can’t do this. Stop. Stop. Stop.”

A bystander can also be heard saying: “This guy is just unbelievable.”

Speaking on the alleged attack, animal cruelty investigator Joey Alexander said the bird was likely “still conscious” while squirming in the clip.

He told the MailOnline: “There are just shocking and callous parts of this.



“The bird was likely still conscious when it was flailing on the floor.

“I have heard stories like this before of people killing wild animals in parks to take them home and eat them.”

West Midlands Police officers have urged any witnesses to come forward as they probe the alleged attack.

The force said: “We received a report of animal cruelty at Ward End Park in Birmingham on 19 October.

“We are making enquiries to establish the circumstances around what happened.



“Officers are working with partners including the park’s management and the local authority.

“They are looking to speak to anyone who might have seen what happened and might know who was responsible.”

An RSPCA spokesperson said the alleged attack on the goose was “extremely distressing”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They added: “We’d urge anyone with first-hand information about this incident to contact us on 0300 1234 999.

“All wild birds are protected under the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 and it is illegal to deliberately kill, injure or take one, except under licence.”

News.title: Mum pleads guilty to killing her three young children after they were found stabbed to death at home
News.content:
TRIPLE TRAGEDY Mum pleads guilty to killing her three young children after they were found stabbed to death at home







Next

A MUM has pleaded guilty to killing her three young children after they were found stabbed to death at home.

Fares Bash, seven, Joury Bash, three, and nine-month-old Mohammed Bash were discovered dead in Bristol in February 2024.



Their mum Yasmeen Ali, 44, was initially charged with murder but admitted three charges of manslaughter on the grounds of diminished responsibility.

Prosecutors accepted her plea after a court heard she was suffering from an “acute psychosis” at the time.



Ali wept been given an indefinite hospital order in a secure psychiatric facility.

Judge Justice Linden described her as a loving mother, adding: “It is my view you would not have done what you have if you were well.”



Bristol Crown Court heard Ali called 999 after killing her children but was out of breath, speaking in Arabic and told police she was “going to God”.

When officers arrived, they found the children dead and Ali in a “very disturbed state, looking like a zombie” with self-inflicted wounds to her neck.

The house in the Sea Mills area of Bristol was described as “dirty and chaotic” with blood covering the landing.

Ali, who previously worked as a nurse, had been discharged from mental health services just six days before the horror.



Avon and Somerset Police referred itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct over “prior police contact” before the tragedy.

But the police watchdog found no investigation was required.

The court heard two doctors believe the mum was suffering from schizoaffective disorder.



An inquest heard previously how the three children died of knife wounds, with injuries to their chests and necks.

Fares also showed possible signs of asphyxia, Avon Coroner’s Court was told.

It is understood the children’s mum and dad, who are originally from Sudan, moved to the UK around around seven years before the killings.

Dad Alfil Bash described his kids as his “whole world ” in a victim impact statement.

He added: “No words can describe the pain I am going through. Part of me has died.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“My children were innocent human beings. They were precious and deserved long happy lives, to make friends and make their own families one day.

“I’ll spend the rest of my life grieving for my children.”

News.title: Tsunami alert after TWELVE earthquakes off coast of Italy sparking mass evacuations & school closures
News.content:
QUAKE CHAOS Tsunami alert after TWELVE earthquakes off coast of Italy sparking mass evacuations & school closures







Next

A TSUNAMI alert is in place after twelve earthquakes hit off the coast of Italy sparking mass evacuations and school closures.

The largest tremor was recorded as 5.0-magnitude at around 12.20pm in Sicily with the regions of Messina and Palermo being the worst affected.



The shock’s epicenter hit the southern Tyrrhenian Sea northwest of the Aeolian Islands, according to the National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology.

All 11 other quakes were above 3.0-magnitude, officials confirmed.



Schools in the Sicilian capital and across to Messina have been evacuated as a precaution after an orange tsunami warning was issued.

The head of the Sicilian Civil Protection, Salvo Cocina, ordered an immediate state of alert and “ready operations” for the affected municipalities.



A courthouse in Trapani was also evacuated as dozens of worried residents took to the streets.

There have been no reports of damage at the moment.

The first earthquake registered as a 3.3-magnitude at 11.04am in the Aeolian archipelago.

It comes a year after Naples was rocked by its biggest earthquake in four decades.



Homes were resigned to ruins after the devastating 4.4-magnitude tremor rocked the city back in March 2025.

The power supply in parts of Naples were also severally disrupted just after 1am local time when the first quake struck.

One person was left injured in the neighbouring town of Pozzuoli, which was sat close in the quake’s epicentre.

News.title: Boy, 3, shoots himself dead with parent’s gun in car as dad paid for dinner at Burger King drive-thru
News.content:
Next

A THREE-YEAR-OLD boy has died after shooting himself in the face with his parent’s gun while his dad was paying for dinner at a drive-thru.

The horrifying incident unfolded at a Burger King restaurant in Florida on Thursday evening as the family ordered food.



Cops say the youngster’s father was attempting to pay for his meal when his credit card unexpectedly declined.

As he tried to figure out another way to settle the bill, the man – who was reportedly legally permitted to carry a firearm – pulled a loaded Glock handgun from his waistband and set it down inside the vehicle.



The boy, who was playing in the backseat, reached over and grabbed the weapon before squeezing the trigger, according to police.

Emergency services scrambled to the fast-food branch in Bartow, Polk County after a bystander raised the alarm.

The three-year-old was then rushed to hospital, where he was tragically pronounced dead.

Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd said: “At this point in the investigation, we think dad took the gun out. He laid it down. He doesn’t remember where – he is still in a state of shock.

“And while he’s trying to figure out how to pay for dinner with a credit card, the child obviously sees the gun, picks it up and is playing with it, and shoots himself in the face.

“This is a horrible tragedy, and that’s all the indication that we see at this point in time.”



Sheriff Judd confirmed legal action could not be taken for at least seven days, but admitted there was “no appetite” to press ahead with criminal charges.

He added: “[The father] was doing the best he could. The child was in the backseat playing and he had absolutely no clue. At least, according to the initial information. Until he hears the pop.”

The family had moved to central Florida from Connecticut just four months ago, officials said.

The child was reportedly due to celebrate his fourth birthday next week.

The horror shooting comes after a toddler narrowly cheated death after putting a loaded gun into their mouth at a nursery.



The two-year-old managed to rummage through an unzipped bag and pull out the deadly weapon, according to a disturbing report from the Virginia Department of Social Services.

The youngster then shoved the live firearm into their mouth while daycare staff were allegedly glued to their phones.

The horrifying incident unfolded at Thrive Learning Center East in Richmond after daycare operator Martha Evans allegedly brought the loaded weapon into work.

The 66-year-old regularly carried the gun into the nursery in a “fanny bag” which was often left “accessible to children”, the report claimed.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Evans was arrested by cops on October 7 and charged with felony possession of a firearm at a school and misdemeanour reckless handling of a firearm.



She has been released on bond and is scheduled to return to court on December 15, according to court records.

News.title: What should I stockpile? Why the Government is advising Brits to stock up on food and water
News.content:
Next

THE Government has issued a warning for all UK residents who are able to do so to stock up on essentials.

This advice comes in response to recent extreme weather and cyber-attacks, which could potentially leave people without access to food, water and electricity.



Why is the Government advising Brits to stock up on food and water?

British households are being urged to stockpile food, water and emergency supplies in case a national crisis cuts them off from essential services.

The Government’s advice covers preparation for everything from storms to cyber-attacks and power blackouts.



On October 22, Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said: “It’s really important that we ask households and businesses: Are they prepared? Are they ready? Do they know how they would respond in the event of everyday challenges that might manifest themselves?”

“But we’ll also need to take the country a step further and ask them are they prepared for increasingly sophisticated cyber-attacks on our businesses, are they prepared for the eventuality that there may be disruption to essential supply chains caused by hostile state actors or terrorists?



“How would we cope if the payment systems at the local supermarket went down?

“Those are the sorts of everyday challenges and threats we could face, and it’s right that we ask the country to be ready for them and ask everyone to do their bit.”

GOV.UK advice reads: “With storms last winter and the wildfires this summer showing how severe weather events can cause disruption to our everyday lives and impact the services we rely on, from phone signal to water and the internet, launching the campaign brings the UK into line with European peers who all run similar campaigns already.

“The government has worked with other countries to learn from their experience and best practices.



“For example, the advice to be prepared for three days of disruption, which is central to the UK campaign is also used by France, Ireland and the Netherlands.”

What should I stockpile?

According to Government advice, you should stockpile all of the following:

Bottled water : Three litres per person per day for drinking. More would be required for cooking and washing.

: Three litres per person per day for drinking. More would be required for cooking and washing. Food : Three days’ worth of non-perishable food that doesn’t need refrigeration or cooking.

: Three days’ worth of non-perishable food that doesn’t need refrigeration or cooking. Hygiene : Hand sanitiser, wet wipes and toiletries.

: Hand sanitiser, wet wipes and toiletries. Light and warmth : Torch, batteries, blankets, sleeping bags and warm clothing.

: Torch, batteries, blankets, sleeping bags and warm clothing. Communication and information : FM radio (battery or wind-up), charged power bank.

: FM radio (battery or wind-up), charged power bank. Money and documents : Notes, coins and cards, copies of IDs/documents, important phone numbers and information such as medications and doses.

: Notes, coins and cards, copies of IDs/documents, important phone numbers and information such as medications and doses. Medical and health : First aid kit, essential medication and medical supplies.

: First aid kit, essential medication and medical supplies. Baby products : Formula (ready-to-feed formula is best as you may not be able to boil water to make powdered formula safely), nappies and wipes.

: Formula (ready-to-feed formula is best as you may not be able to boil water to make powdered formula safely), nappies and wipes. Pet products: Pet food and bottled water.

Security Minister Dan Jarvis said: “Those who can follow this advice should follow this advice.

“By taking simple steps to be ready for everyday emergencies like severe storms, people can reduce pressure on emergency services, helping them prioritise people who need more support in an emergency.

“This is just the sort of community-focused campaign the UK needs to improve our resilience as a nation.



“It will bring us into line with European counterparts, where advice like this is a normal part of everyday life.”

News.title: At least 1 killed and 3 missing as cargo ship catches fire ‘after being struck by drone’ in Black Sea
News.content:
Next

AT least one person has been killed and three more are missing after a drone struck a cargo ship in the Black Sea.

The vessel became engulfed in flames after the incident, with Romanian rescuers desperately scouring the water for survivors.



Romanian President Nicusor Dan has blamed Russia for the “attack,” which eventually caused the ship to flounder and sink.

The ship’s crew consisted of ten Ukrainians and three Azerbaijanis, and was hit around 15 miles east of the port city of Constanta.



The Ministry of Interior said a fire broke out on a commercial vessel, which “suffered major damage and capsized, with an imminent risk of sinking.”

It added: “Of the 13 people on board, ten were recovered by another commercial vessel in the area, nine alive and one deceased.



“Three others are still missing.”

Authorities did not say what caused the vessel fire, but multiple local media platforms reported it had been struck by a drone.

The naval authority identified the ship as a Comoros-flagged cargo vessel named Khoryv, which the shipping data website MarineTraffic shows departed Turkey on October 21 and was headed for Romania’s Sulina port.

It said: “Rescue teams continue search operations to identify and rescue the other three crew members,” adding that it wasn’t possible to deploy a helicopter due to poor weather conditions and low visibility.



Romanian leader Dan has laid the blame squarely at the Kremlin’s door, saying it was “clearly part of the escalation that Russia is carrying out in the context of the war in Ukraine“.

The incident follows a spate of drone attacks on at least seven cargo vessels off the Black Sea coasts of Nato members Romania and Bulgaria in October, which has raised fears that Russia’s war in Ukraine is spreading.

The recent attacks in the two countries’ exclusive economic zones threaten a global shipping route and have left two people dead, with at least 25 still missing.



On Saturday, Romanian pilots on air policing duties shot down two drones in territorial waters over the Black Sea.

On Thursday, following a meeting of Romania‘s Supreme Council for National Defence, the presidency said that “threats to freedom of navigation and critical infrastructure have increased significantly”.

Romania is looking into “accelerated development of surveillance capabilitiesand effective countermeasures against drones that intrude unauthorised into national airspace and territorial waters”.

Nato said after talks on Black Sea security on Tuesday that it was deploying additional planes, drones and radar systems to the area because of the attacks on ships.

Foreign Minister Dan Neculaescu said Romania was working with Nato allies including Bulgaria and Turkey to “fast-track the additional surveillance capabilities”.



In his Facebook post, Dan said it was “time for Russia to take the peace initiatives put forward by the United States and Europe seriously, to accept the proposals for a ceasefire and to bring the war to an end”.

News.title: Monster who murdered stepdaughter, 19, in her uni halls after developing sexual obsession with her is jailed
News.content:
Next

A MONSTER who murdered his stepdaughter in her uni flat after developing a sexual obsession with her has been jailed.

Carla Georgescu, 19, was discovered dead on what would have been her 20th birthday at the University of Lancashire campus in Preston.



Her stepdad Nathan Owens, 34, had driven 100 miles from the family home to strangle Carla to death after becoming “consumed by jealousy”.

Footage then showed him shopping in Asda with Carla’s mum Janina as she lay slumped against a wardrobe door with injuries to her face and a belt tied around her.



Owens has now jailed for life with a minimum of 25 years after he was convicted of murder.

Sentencing, Mr Justice Jacobs labelled Owens as “despicable” and said he had subjected his victim to a “horrific, brutal attack”.



The judge said: “The last 90 minutes of Carla’s life are too horrendous to think about.

“I am sure that she suffered both mentally and physically during a material part of that 90 minutes.”

Preston Crown Court heard how Owens had become “sexually fixated” with his stepdaughter and made a life-size effigy of her to fulfil his sexual fantasy.

He had also manipulated innocent selfies of Carla into sexual images and had filmed himself having sex with her anime dolls and a stuffed cat she had bought him.



Just days before the horror, Carla had spent the weekend shopping for presents with her mum Janina and watching TV together.

On February 1, Owens drove from the family home in Hartlepool and joined his wife and stepdaughter for a meal at the Kimji Korean restaurant.

Footage showed him and Carla left alone together at one point during the meal.

Following the dinner, Owens and Janina were filmed dropping Carla back off at her accommodation, it was said.



Just three days later, he drove through the night before parking up in his Ford Puma outside Carla’s university residence.

Footage showed him shrouding himself in a blanket before making his way towards Ribble Hall to murder Carla.

The court was told he left 90 minutes later – “shielding” himself with an umbrella and wearing a face-mask and Carla’s trainers, while carrying two bags.

Owens then returned home to Hartlepool where wife Janina said he was his “normal self”.



The mum told the court the couple later went for their regular walk at a nearby beach together.

At the time, Carla’s body remained undiscovered in her student flat.

Janina raised the alarm when her daughter failed to respond to her messages and phone calls.

After Carla was found on what would have been her 20th birthday, two officers went to the family home and told her she had been found hanged.

Janina told the court she was left “shaking” while Owens “started crying”.



He had hugged and comforted her, she said, but at that point he still didn’t reveal he had travelled to see Carla the day before, she revealed.

Janina told jurors it was only when she contacted a hospital mortuary and learned more details about her death that he admitted he had been at the flat.

Owens claimed Carla had wanted him to take incontinence pants to her and help her tidy her room but the prosecution say this was an attempt to “cover his tracks”.



When asked by Mr Lumley if she had any reason to “doubt” Owen, Janina replied she didn’t because “it wasn’t inconsistent with his behaviour” and if Carla had wanted him to come he would have.

A post mortem also revealed Carla had been subjected to two heavy blows to her head, slash marks on her cheek and cuts and bruises to her mouth and nose.

Carla’s hands were covered in blood after she attempted to defend herself and she had sexual injuries, the court heard.

The jury was told sex toys and Owens’ DNA were found at the scene.

Mr Lumley said “some form of grievous sexual activity” had taken place which was “hardly surprising” given Owens’ sexual obsession with her.



Jurors were told the killing was possibly driven by “sexual jealousy” after discovering his stepdaughter was due to meet up with a new lover.

In the months leading up to Carla’s murder, Owens had been collecting photos of her taken without her knowledge.

Owens had also filmed himself having sex with her dolls and toys – including one that was a life-sized “effigy” dressed in Carla’s nightie.

He was also said to have manipulated innocent selfies of Carla into sexual images which he viewed in the week before she died.

“The only possible reason for looking at those images is that Nathan Owens had a wholly improper and dangerously entrenched sexual obsession with his stepdaughter,” Mr Lumley told the court.



He continued: “Her death was the culmination, the end point, of weeks, months and perhaps years of a one-sided sexual obsession.

“And it was the beginning of a complex murder investigation, which led to his door in Hartlepool.

“For it was he who was sexually fixated on Carla and it was he, Nathan Owens, who had killed Carla.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

DI Pete Macdonald, of our Force Major Investigation Team said Owens had a “despicable, perverted sexual obsession with his stepdaughter” that culminated in him killing her.

He added: “No verdict brings Carla back, but I hope that her mum and the rest of her loved ones can feel some sense of justice that the man responsible for taking her future away has been brought to justice.”

News.title: Girl, 13, ‘raped by parents & their friend who threatened her with electric shocks or being forced to eat own eyes’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

SICKENING CRUELTY Girl, 13, ‘raped by parents & their friend who threatened her with electric shocks or being forced to eat own eyes’







Next

A TEENAGE girl was allegedly raped by her parents and their friend who threatened her if she refused.

The girl’s father 45, and mother, 41, are accused of threatening their own daughter, 13, with electric shocks or being forced to “eat her own eyes”.



The couple have been charged with repeatedly raping their daughter and are facing trial in Germany.

Prosecutors allege they encouraged their acquaintance to participate in the abuse.



The Croatian national appears to have gone missing, and is suspected to have fled Germany.

He was brought into the court in handcuffs and leg irons from custody.



He has multiple prior convictions and is currently serving a prison sentence for fraud.

The woman, who has not been detained because she is not believed to pose a flight risk, was already seated in court when he arrived.

Both remained silent throughout the proceedings.

They have not commented so far on the allegations.



Their lawyers have not confirmed whether either of them will testify during the trial.

They face 15 years in prison if convicted.

Their acquaitance had spent six months in prison ahead of trial before the regional court released him because there was “no urgent suspicion of a crime“.

By the time a higher court overturned this decision it was already too late and he had disappeared.

An international arrest warrant has been issued for him.



The allegations were first reported to police when the girl confided in an adult.

Her parents have been charged with rape, sexual abuse of a person entrusted to their care and aggravated sexual abuse of a child.

The girl now lives in a children’s home and is expected to testify in court.

A verdict is expected on November 17.

News.title: Pharmacist warning on the effect vaping is really having on your voice
News.content:
Pharmacist warning on the effect vaping is really having on your voice

It comes after Selena Gomez admitted vaping had changed her voice

View 3 Images Vaping has some hidden health effects (Image: Witthaya Prasongsin via Getty Images)

A pharmacist has warned that vaping could affect people's voices, after singer and actress Selena Gomez revealed she believes heavy nicotine use has changed hers. Hanna Yusuf, a prescribing pharmacist at Chemist4U, says vape aerosol can irritate delicate tissues around the vocal cords, potentially contributing to dryness, coughing and a hoarse voice.

‌



‌



Gomez, 34, spoke about her experience in an Instagram story this week, saying she had vaped nicotine heavily and believed it had altered her voice. "Nicotine is so hard to quit, and I think I just wanted to say, if you're going through it, or if you're even trying to vape, it's just not worth it," she said.

‌



"It's so stupid, and it has changed my voice. I stopped, and I just hope we can keep it up. It's really hard. But I know if you are going through something, you can get through it, too."

‌



View 3 Images Selena Gomez has spoken out about her vaping habits (Image: Variety via Getty Images)

Her comments have prompted renewed interest in the possible effects of vaping on vocal health. Gomez previously discussed her voice during an Instagram Live in December 2025, saying her throat sometimes swelled internally, while the BBC has noted that lupus can also affect the voice box.

‌



Yusuf said: "Vaping can negatively affect your voice, vocal cords, and overall vocal health." She explained that aerosol produced when an e-cigarette heats liquid contains tiny particles that can irritate and dry out tissues around the vocal folds.

The NHS lists coughing, dry mouth and throat, mouth and throat irritation, and shortness of breath among possible side effects of vaping. These symptoms may affect vocal comfort, while repeated coughing and prolonged speaking or singing can put additional strain on the voice.

‌



View 3 Images Millions of Brits vape in the UK (Image: Getty Images)

Yusuf added: “"Studies suggest that vaping may contribute to inflammation and dryness affecting the vocal folds and surrounding airway tissues." However, research into the specific long-term effects of vaping on the voice remains limited, so it is important not to assume every change in someone's voice is caused by vaping.

Article continues below

People can help protect their voices by staying hydrated, avoiding inhaled irritants and resting their voice when it feels strained. Yusuf recommends seeking medical advice if voice changes persist, with NHS guidance advising people to see their GP if they have a hoarse voice lasting more than three weeks.

Vaping is considered less harmful than smoking, according to the NHS, and nicotine vapes can help some adults quit cigarettes. However, they are not risk-free, and people who vape to stop smoking can ask a stop smoking service or healthcare professional for support if they want to quit vaping too.

News.title: Police officer raped by Met cop David Carrick calls for Scotland Yard chief to resign
News.content:
Police officer raped by Met cop David Carrick calls for Scotland Yard chief to resign

Officer Linda Williams has called the way she was treated by the Met throughout her legal claim "devastating" and says it nearly drove her to suicide

View 4 Images Linda Williams was attacked by Carrick in 2004 (Image: Black Letter Communications/Press Association)

A police officer raped by David Carrick has called for Metropolitan Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley to resign after receiving a six-figure settlement from the force.

‌



Linda Williams, 60, who has bravely waived her right to anonymity, was attacked by serial rapist and former officer Carrick in 2004. Carrick, 51, who previously served as an armed officer in the Met, is one of the country's worst ever sex offenders and is currently serving 37 life sentences after attacking more than a dozen women.

Ms Williams has called the way she was treated by the Met throughout her legal claim "devastating" and says it nearly drove her to suicide. Her case against the Met has now been settled for an undisclosed six-figure sum without the force admitting liability.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 4 Images Linda feels let down by the Met (Image: Black Letter Communications/Press Association)

She said: "The whole process has taken me right back to how I felt when I was raped by Carrick, controlled, abused and powerless. If I was raped tomorrow, I wouldn't report it. Both the criminal justice process and the civil process have been so traumatic.

‌



"I say that as someone who was once a sexual offences officer, supporting victims myself. Despite that experience and my understanding of the system, I still wouldn't report it because of the complete lack of empathy and support I have experienced from the police.

"At no point did I feel they sincerely acknowledged that I had been through a horrific sexual attack and that the trauma of that had deeply scarred me, or their role in it all.

‌



"They used the fact that I just got on with my life as best I could after the rape against me. I was an exemplary officer and continued to perform well at work, and they relied on that to suggest I had shown no signs of psychological trauma. As far as I am concerned, it is Mark Rowley, the Commissioner, saying these terrible things as he was the defendant in the case."

View 4 Images In 2022 and 2023, Carrick pleaded guilty to 71 sexual offences, including 48 rapes against 12 other women over 17 years (Image: Hertfordshire Police/PA)

‌



Ms Williams, from Hertfordshire, alleged it was "the Met's fault" that she could not report the rape in 2004, and that "little had changed" in the culture since then.

She said the force was "like an episode of Life On Mars" and that she would have been "the officer who alleged I had been raped by a fellow officer," adding: "I wouldn't have had the back up of my colleagues in dangerous situations and ultimately, I doubt anything would have been done about Carrick."

‌



She reported the attack in 2021, and said she has had no relationships since the attack 22 years ago. "After the attack, I couldn't face the thought of being with a man or even having somebody in my home," she said.

"That makes for a lonely Christmas and no holidays. It's my choice but the reason behind it wasn't my choice. That's down to the attack. Carrick stole the future that I wanted."

‌



Following her lengthy legal dispute, Ms Williams now wants to see changes to the support systems in the Met, including a unit overseen by victims. But she told how she's spoken to officers trying to set up similar systems who have met resistance from the force.

View 4 Images Linda received a six-figure settlement from the Met (Image: PA)

‌



She said: "Mark Rowley will say they are doing everything they can to stop violence against women and girls, I disagree. The Met need to set up a unit overseen by victims like me who understand what it is like to be raped. For this to happen Rowley needs to go and we need a new commissioner."

Sophie Bullimore, a solicitor from Penningtons Manches Cooper who represented Ms Williams, said: "My client is an extremely impressive woman, who has shown incredible strength since the assault and throughout this process; however her life has been forever changed and more than 20 years after the attack, the impact on her mental health and daily living is still stark."

‌



She added that the "time it has taken" to reach a settlement has resulted in Ms Williams taking long-term sickness from the police and has asked that the Met "review" how they deal with cases like this in future.

In 2022 and 2023, Carrick pleaded guilty to 71 sexual offences, including 48 rapes against 12 other women over 17 years. In November last year, he was convicted of molesting a 12-year-old child in the late 1980s and repeatedly raping and abusing a female ex-partner.

‌



A Met Police spokesperson said: "David Carrick was responsible for the most appalling offences and as we have said previously, we are truly sorry for the harm and suffering he caused his victims. He should never have been a police officer. Serious flaws in the way we approached such investigations at the time meant we did not spot his pattern of abusive behaviour.

"As a result, we missed opportunities to pursue him through the misconduct process. We deeply regret this. We recognise the unique and additional impact on DC Linda Williams, whose exposure to Carrick came as a result of her being a Met officer. Her continued commitment to public service, in spite of the trauma she experienced, is commendable.

"Throughout subsequent legal proceedings, the Met has tried to reduce further distress and re-traumatisation to DC Williams' welfare and has aimed to deal with her claims as quickly and compassionately as possible. The Commissioner has previously met with DC Williams in person as well as spoken to her via email on multiple occasions.

"He has repeatedly acknowledged that she has shown courage in speaking out about her experience in an effort to drive forward necessary change and in now waiving her anonymity to continue to do so. He has contacted DC Williams to ask whether she would be willing to meet again and further discuss these issues in person."

News.title: Andy Burnham defends emergency kit list and gives verdict on stockpiling wine
News.content:
Andy Burnham defends emergency kit list and gives verdict on stockpiling wine

Andy Burnham said unexpected weather events are becoming 'more and more common' as he faced questions about the emergency kit list Brits are encouraged to make sure they stockpile

View 2 Images Andy Burnham defended the government's kit list and gave his verdict on including wine (Image: Getty Images)

Andy Burnham has defended urging families to stockpile emergency kits at home - warning unexpected events are becoming "more and more common".

‌



‌



The Prime Minister said the UK faces a winter of greater flooding ahead of a summit to learn from the summer's wildfires. The government has issued a list of items people should have ready in the event of an emergency - including water, tinned food and battery-powered radios.

‌



Mr Burnham also suggested people should be allowed a glass of wine to get them through a crisis after Angela Rayner previously joked a bottle of Sauvignon Blanc would be in her survival kit.

‌



Military planes to fight wildfires and survival campaign launched - see kit list READ MORE :

John Healey told to extend free breakfasts to SEND children in secondary school at Budget READ MORE :

Asked about the Housing Secretary's comment, he said: "I'm not sure that that's the top of the list in terms of the advice that we're giving to the public.

"You need to have a clear head when it comes to a challenging situation. So some tins of food, some bottled water, I think maybe. But I'm sure people are allowed a glass or two as well to get them through a difficult situation."

‌



Last month Ms Rayner told Times Radio her emergency kit would include mascara, concealer, a bottle of Sauvignon Blanc, baked beans and a tin of custard.

Advice issued on Thursday said Britons should make sure they have three days of water, non-perishable food and items like torches and radios to get through an emergency.

‌



View 2 Images Mr Burnham made a jokey reply to a quip by Angela Rayner about her emergency kit (Image: Temilade Adelaja/Press Association)

Mr Burnham said: "We're having the conversation with people about being better prepared because we're living in a world where unexpected events seem to be becoming more and more common."

‌



It comes as parts of the country were battered by Storm Austen, with thousands of homes left without power and flights having to be cancelled. Further amber weather warnings for wind have been issued by the Met Office over the weekend.

The PM said: "Obviously, weather events, and we're in a situation today where the UK is facing storms and obviously, we feel for the people without power in Cornwall right now. It is just having those supplies in the house to get you through those moments. So we are having that conversation about resilience.

‌



"That's why we're holding this summit today, it's why we're putting the guidance out to the public. We potentially are facing a winter of greater flooding, so it's about recognising all of those risks and taking action."

Earlier Treasury minister James Murray admitted he has not followed the guidance on stockpiling supplies. The paymaster general told BBC Breakfast that he had a stockpile of coffee, adding: "If you look at, say, Ireland or other countries in Europe like France and Netherlands, they've had this system for quite a long time, the idea of having a bit of stuff at home to protect yourselves in case something goes wrong.

‌



"So it's quite normal in other countries. I think it's a bit more interesting here because we haven't really talked about it as a country in recent years."

Asked what he had stockpiled, he said: "I've got quite a lot of coffee in my house... it's for individual people to take choices. I'm not going to say: `Here's a Government shopping list.'" He added: "I'm not going to pretend I've followed all that advice myself yet."

‌



Ministers are ramping up plans to prepare for extreme weather in the UK. On Thursday the government announced military planes and helicopters will be equipped to fight wildfires after Britain faced a summer of extreme heat.

Meanwhile, Security Minister Dan Jarvis has launched a public awareness campaign to ensure families can prepare for everyday services being disrupted by extreme weather or other events like cyberattacks.

Article continues below

The "Be Ready" campaign urges Brits to keep a small supply at home, including non-perishable food and bottled water, and to sign up to the Priority Services Register, a service that helps gas, water, and electricity companies identify customers that may need extra support in an emergency.

News.title: Try this trick to give the kid's a good night's sleep in a hotel this half term
News.content:
Try this trick to give the kid's a good night's sleep in a hotel this half term

The Sleep Charity and Premier Inn share expert tips to help children sleep easily in unfamiliar environments this half term, keeping their bedtime routines smooth while away from home.

View 4 Images Heading to a hotel this half term? Try these tricks to get little ones to sleep (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

It can be tricky to get your little ones off to sleep when they’re away from home. Staying over in a new environment is exciting, but it’s also a change from their nightly routine, and that can make it difficult for them to drift off. So, we decided to ask the experts!

‌



‌



Here, The Sleep Charity - in partnership with Premier Inn - have given some top bedtime tips to help kids nod off in no time, wherever they are. As a charity that works extensively with families, they know the importance of a great night’s sleep.

‌



Favourite teddy: Kids will always want something familiar in a new environment, so be sure to pack their favourite toy or blanket to help them feel comfortable and at home.

‌



View 4 Images Pack their favourite toy to make them feel at home - the smell will help too (Image: Catherine Falls Commercial via Getty Images)

Bedtime routine: Although you won’t be able to do everything like you would at home, try to include an element of your usual routine, such as reading a bedtime story.

Colouring in: Fine motor skill activities help kids relax, so take advantage of the colouring packs in hotel restaurants like to get a head-start on bedtime!

‌



No TV: Screens interfere with the production of melatonin, a hormone that makes us sleepy. Switching off the TV an hour before bedtime can really help little ones nod off.

View 4 Images A bath can make little ones feel at home and also relax them before bed (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Bath time: A warm bath 30 minutes before bedtime can be very effective in helping kids wind down and getting them off to sleep.

Repetition: Staying away from home is exciting for kids, so you’ll need to be clear and firm with them when it’s time for bed. Try a calming phrase like ‘It’s night-time, go to sleep’ and repeat it.

‌



Dim the lights: Switch off a few lights and make use of the Premier Inn blackout curtains to help with that all-important melatonin production.

View 4 Images It pays to plan your mealtimes around little ones - and check out Premier Inn's kids-eat-free deals over half term (Image: Premier Inn)

‌



Mealtimes: Plan your dinner time! Try not to eat so early that the kids are hungry by bedtime or so late that they’re uncomfortably full.

Avoid stimulants: Caffeine and sugar play havoc with sleep so in the evenings, try to steer little ones away from sugary desserts and opt for fruit and water instead.

‌

Little ones can enjoy delicious and nutritious dishes like our 10-Veg Tomato Pasta and Oven Baked Poppin’ Chicken – and sweet treats like a Fresh Fruit Salad, Pancakes and more.

News.title: Poland closes airports and 'air defence system activated' as Russia launches attack
News.content:
Poland closes airports and 'air defence system activated' as Russia launches attack

The airports in Lublin and Rzeszów have suspended flights this afternoon 'due to military activity' in eastern Poland

View Image This September 19, 2025 Hand Out image released by the Swedish Airforce shows a Russian MIG-31 fighter jet flying above the Baltic sea after violating Estonian air space. Three Russian MiG-31 fighters violated Estonian airspace over the Gulf of Finland on Friday, Estonia said, triggering complaints of a dangerous new provocation from the EU and NATO. Sweden and Finland scrambled rapid reaction aircraft, a spokesman for the Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe (SHAPE) told reporters. (Photo by Forsvarsmakten / HANDOUT / AFP) / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE - MANDATORY CREDIT "AFP PHOTO / SOURCE / BYLINE" - HANDOUT - NO MARKETING NO ADVERTISING CAMPAIGNS - DISTRIBUTED AS A SERVICE TO CLIENTS (Photo by FORSVARSMAKTEN/HANDOUT/AFP via Getty Images) (Image: FORSVARSMAKTEN/HANDOUT/AFP via Getty Images)

Two airports have been closed in eastern Poland and the country's air defence system as Russia launches yet more strikes on Ukraine.

‌



‌



The airports in Lublin and Rzeszów have temporarily suspended flights this afternoon "due to military activity". A statement from the Polish armed forces released at 12pm local time (11am BST) says the fresh Russian attack has been carried out in western Ukraine using airborne assault assets.

‌



As a result, Poland has activated its "necessary forces and resources" of the air defence system. However, the command said the measures are precautionary and aim to ensure the protection of Polish airspace.

‌



The situation is being monitored. The statement reads: "Attention. In connection with further strikes by the Russian Federation on targets in the western part of Ukraine, carried out using airborne assault assets, the necessary forces and resources of the air defence system have been activated through the Air Operations Center – Air Component Command.

"The actions are of a preventive nature and are aimed at securing and protecting Polish airspace, especially in areas adjacent to the threatened zones. The Operational Command of the Armed Forces monitors the current situation, and subordinate forces and resources remain ready to respond."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Poland's air navigation services agency added: "Due to military activity, the airports in Lublin and Rzeszów have temporarily suspended flight operations." Similar action was taken on Monday, when the two airports were closed and military aviation operated across Polish airspace.

Article continues below

That followed Russian strikes on targets in the western part of Ukraine, conducted using unmanned aerial vehicles.

News.title: 'Middle East tension is soaring in the run-up to Netanyahu's fight for his political life'
News.content:
The Israeli army is bracing to close the West Bank after a terror flare-up at a checkpoint as the country prepares for the polls.

It marks a genuine security threat to Israel, the main concern for Israelis facing arguably the most important elections in the country’s history.

Conspiracy theories abound about Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu needing a major incident to improve his chances of political survival. Israel’s wiliest political figure, he is nevertheless clinging to power and faces an extremely close election day Tuesday October 27.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



View 5 Images Leader of Irael's Yashar opposition Gadi Eisenkot (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Current polling puts Netanyahu in a close fight with Gadi Eisenkot, a former head of the Israel Defense Forces, to become prime minister.

Many are tired of Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving Prime Minister, who has served for 18 years across three separate periods and has shunted the country to the right.

The polls come amid escalating violence across the region following the October 7 Hamas attacks launched from Gaza. The West Bank is seething under the pressure of more than 600,000 amid the horror of violent attacks on Palestinians.

‌



View 5 Images Israeli soldier at scene of checkpoint attack (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Britain at risk of more terror attacks as US-Iran war set to explode again READ MORE :

Saudi pledged massive revenge attack after Houthis hit airports READ MORE :

This morning the Israeli Defence Force shot dead two attackers at a Hebron security stop. As many as five Israeli soldiers were wounded but this will not be the first time the West Bank will have been closed.

Dominating the polling is security since Netanyahu’s challengers are hugely critical of security failures that led to October 7. Almost 1,200 people were killed and 251 others taken back to Gaza in the deadliest attack Israel had suffered since independence in 1948 and which triggered an horrific outbreak of violence in Gaza, Lebanon and beyond.

It started conflicts with Hamas, Hezbollah, pro-Iran militia in Iraq, the Yemeni Houthis, an explosion of violence in the West Bank and missile exchanges with Iran. You only have to look into the eyes of young Palestinian men in the West Bank at the funerals of their friends to witness the fury.

‌



View 5 Images Israeli troops set up position in West Bank (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The same goes for the faces of exhausted troops of the IDF and the refugees who spent many months sheltering in hotels as their homes in northern Israel came under attack.

Or the faces of shattered children forced to grow up in the hellscape of Gaza amid the bombs and bullets. Israeli liberals have been hardened by the horror of October 7.

It sparked war in Gaza which has killed at least 70,000 Palestinians and more than 1,150 Israeli soldiers. Netanyahu paints himself as "Mr Security", pointing to victories in Israel's wars since 2023.

‌



But there have been the catastrophic intelligence failures of October 7, followed by accusations Netanyahu ignored warnings about Hamas.

There then followed some of the most incredible victories, not least the Mossad “pager plot” which killed many Hezbollah operatives and badly wounded many more.

Like everything in Israel it is beyond complex. Ultra-Orthodox Jewish men have been exempt from service, but since war broke out this has become an increasingly divisive. Judicial reform has also featured heavily.

Netanyahu's government wants reforms to the judicial system, which led to mass protests before 7 October and which threaten democracy. The cost of living is another key issue.

‌



View 5 Images Shooting scene in Hebron, West Bank (Image: Mosab Shawer/JNA via ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

Netanyahu faces stiff opposition and election day is unlikely to unveil a conclusive winner. There are 38 different parties contesting the election — although most will not get enough votes to secure a spot in the 120-seat parliament, the Knesset.

Polling suggests Yashar may be the largest party with between 20 and 23 seats. Netanyahu’s party Likud would run second on roughly 19 to 21 seats.

But that does not mean victory as Israel will get a coalition and the election is just the start of weeks of immensely complex coalition negotiations.

‌



Netanyahu’s main opposition Yashar, meaning ‘straight’ or ‘honest’ is expected to win 23 Knesset seats out of 120, slightly ahead of Netanyahu's Likud.

Yashar is led by by former IDF Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, But Netanyahu could win if Likud and its coalition partners amount to more seats, arriving at 52 and Yashar and its “change Bloc” coalition may win 51, just for example.

Neither would have the 61-seat majority needed, unless it secures support from smaller parties. So Netanyahu’s future rests on his ability first to win a higher number of seats and then to negotiate a coalition as it does for Eisenkot’s “change Bloc.”

News.title: UK house prices: Data uncovers massive £1 million rift between most and least affordable areas
News.content:
UK house prices: Data uncovers massive £1 million rift between most and least affordable areas

Property prices in the UK now far outstrip average wages, but the rate differs wildly across the country - with homes in the most affordable an average of £1 million cheaper

View 5 Images Brits are facing an affordability crisis as house prices surge across the UK (Image: In Pictures via Getty Images)

New data has uncovered a massive seven-figure rift between house prices in the most and least affordable parts of the country.

‌



‌



House prices in the UK are nearly seven times the earnings of the average Brit, with the latest figures from the Office of National Statistics (ONS) showing the average home is worth £273,000 in 2026. The average is up 0.9 percent on last year, although house price growth appears to be slowing, the the rate of increase down from 1.2% in July, 1.5% in June, 3.1% in May and 4.2% in April.

‌



While wage growth has meant that, in some cases, Brits are able to pay more than they might once have, people are still looking for areas with the most affordable properties.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 5 Images Scotland is the most affordable part of the country (Image: Getty Images/Westend61)

Average annual earnings for full-time workers in the UK are currently at £40,911 before tax, an increase of 4.5 percent compared to 2025.

‌



That increase means house prices are now, on average, 6.7-times higher than earnings - the lowest ratio since 2015. In August last year, house prices were 6.9-times higher than wages. In 2024 they were 7.1-times higher, in 2023 they were 7.5-times higher, and in 2022 they were 8.0-times higher.

House prices haven't been four times higher than average earnings for more than 20 years, becoming five-times earnings back in 2002 - a rate to which the country has not returned since.

‌



That said, however, there are still areas across the country where rates are below this highly sought-after rate, and where prospective home buyers will get more for their money.

‌



The UK's most affordable areas

Inverclyde, a naturally stunning part of Renfrewshire in Scotland, is the most affordable part of the country to buy a home. The area boasted average house prices of £115,000 in the year to August, lower than anywhere else in the country and well more than £1 million under the least affordable part of the country.

Inverclyde's average house prices work out to around three times the local average earnings of £37,819 a year, making the ratio the lowest in terms of house-price-to-earnings in the country.

‌



Aberdeen is the next most affordable place to buy, with average house prices there working out at 3.1-times average earnings in the area. In West Dunbartonshire the ratio is 3.3-times, in North Ayrshire it’s also 3.3-times, and in East Ayrshire it’s 3.5-times.

Meanwhile, Burnley is the most affordable place to buy a home in England. Average house prices in the area were £137,000 in the year to August. That works out as 3.7-times the local average earnings of £36,821.

‌



View 5 Images Average earnings are several times lower than the average house prices (Image: In Pictures via Getty Images)

The full list of most affordable areas is as follows:

‌



Inverclyde: 3.0 City of Aberdeen: 3.1 North Ayrshire: 3.3 West Dunbartonshire: 3.3 East Ayrshire: 3.5 Renfrewshire: 3.7 Burnley: 3.7 South Ayrshire: 3.8 Hartlepool: 3.8 North Lanarkshire: 3.9 City of Dundee: 3.9 Na h-Eileanan Siar: 3.9 Hyndburn: 3.9 Cumberland: 4.0 Blaenau Gwent: 4.0 Middlesbrough: 4.0 County Durham: 4.0 Darlington: 4.1 Blackpool: 4.1 City of Kingston upon Hull: 4.1

The cheapest places to buy a home are as follows:

‌



Inverclyde: £115,000 West Dunbartonshire: £132,000 City of Aberdeen: £134,000 Burnley: £137,000 Hartlepool: £137,000 City of Kingston upon Hull: £137,000 East Ayrshire: £138,000 Blackpool: £138,000 North Ayrshire: £141,000 County Durham: £141,000

View 5 Images The least affordable part of the country continues to be London (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The UK's least affordable areas

London continues to outpace every part of the country in terms of home affordability, despite residents receiving the largest average pay packets.

While average house prices have fallen by 13.8 percent over the last 12 months, Kensington and Chelsea remains the most expensive of the lot. Homes still hit seven figures over the same period, with average prices of £1.2 million apiece in the historically affluent area.

‌



Average earners took home £58,502 a year, so any locals hoping to buy a home would have to take out a mortgage worth 20.6-times their salary.

The ratio is the highest house-price-to-income in the country. Second to Kensington and Chelsea is Richmond upon Thames, where the ratio is 14.5. That’s followed by Camden at 13.8, the City of Westminster at 13.4 and Hammersmith and Fulham at 13.3.

‌



The Surrey borough of Elmbridge has the highest ratio outside of the capital. Average homes in the area cost £736,000 in the year to August. That’s 12.7-times more than the average earnings of £57,962 a year.

Another Surrey area, Mole Valley, had the next highest ratio outside of London with homes costing 12.6-times the local salary. Trafford was the least affordable place to buy in the North of England. Average house prices in the borough were £394,000 in the year to August.

‌



The lack of affordability, even while prices are far lower than London, is due to local earnings of £46,055 a year, which are 8.6 times lower than the average house price.

View 5 Images Few places were able to compete against London for the least affordable part of the country (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



The full list of least affordable areas is as follows:

Kensington and Chelsea: 20.6 Richmond upon Thames: 14.5 Camden: 13.8 City of Westminster: 13.4 Hammersmith and Fulham: 13.3 Ealing: 12.9 Elmbridge: 12.7 Haringey: 12.7 Merton: 12.7 Mole Valley: 12.6 Hounslow: 12.5 Three Rivers: 12.3 Brent: 12.3 Hertsmere: 12.2 Islington: 12.0 Hackney: 12.0 Barnet: 12.0 Wandsworth: 11.9 Kingston upon Thames: 11.7 Waverley: 11.5

News.title: Meghan says she was informed about 'disturbing allegations' against her father in 2018
News.content:
The Duchess of Sussex has said she was informed about "disturbing allegations" about her estranged father in 2018.

In a statement, Meghan said a letter containing allegations against Thomas Markle was sent to the Metropolitan Police that year and subsequently shared with her.

Her comments come after reports that images of child sexual abuse allegedly belonging to her father had been found at his former home in the Philippines.

Thomas Markle, who is 82 and based in the US, denies possessing any such images.

Commenting after the allegations, first reported by The Sun newspaper, external, the duchess said: "I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."

She said that when she received the letter outlining allegations against her father, she was "given assurance that these were being investigated".

She added she hoped it could be understood why she had kept her distance from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".

This was "to protect them", Meghan said, adding that she had "trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families".

She described the allegations as "more sickening than one could ever imagine" and said her "sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children".

Meghan's half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr, alleged to The Sun that he had found child abuse images at his father's home in the Philippines and reported to the police.

The Undersecretary for the Philippines Department of Justice, Nicholas Ty, told the BBC that "the matter is currently being investigated" by an anti-human trafficking and child sexual exploitation task force in Cebu.

Philippines Interior Minister Jonvic Remulla separately told the BBC that national police had secured Thomas Markle Snr's computer to conduct a comprehensive digital forensic examination.

Investigators are currently analysing the data to determine the full scope and extent of his alleged criminal activities, with the minister saying it would take one week to get the forensic results.

The BBC has contacted Thomas Markle Snr and the Metropolitan Police for comment.

The allegations about Meghan's estranged father cast a new light on their complicated family relationships.

The statement from the Duchess of Sussex says the sharing of information about her father happened in 2018 - the year in which she married Prince Harry.

It is understood that Meghan first learnt about the allegations against her father after the wedding.

The claims add a fresh dimension to the questions about why Prince Harry and their children did not ever seem to have met Meghan's father - and why relations seemed to be so strained.

With such question marks over her estranged father - and he has denied any wrongdoing - it also raises the issue of whether that played a part in the Sussexes' hurried return to the UK in late summer.

The Sussexes' spokesman has not responded to questions about whether that was a factor in their decision to leave the US, where her father was living.

The pair and their two children returned to the UK in August after six years in the US.

They moved there after stepping back as senior royals in January 2020, meaning they no longer perform official royal duties or receive public funds.

Meghan is the only child of Thomas Markle's marriage to her mother, Doria Ragland, but he has two other children - Samantha and Thomas Markle Jr - from an earlier marriage.

The relationship between Meghan and her father, a former TV lighting director, broke down in the run-up to her wedding in 2018.

At the time, Thomas Markle was found to have colluded with photographers, accepting payment to stage photographs of him preparing for the wedding.

The resultant fall-out saw him pull out of his daughter's wedding, citing health problems. Meghan was instead walked down the aisle by King Charles III - then Prince of Wales.

In 2025, Thomas Markle moved to the Philippines after a series of strokes.

He is reportedly now living in a rehabilitation centre in Florida, where he is learning to walk again, after having a leg amputated during surgery in December 2025.

Meghan sent a letter to her estranged father while he was in hospital in the Philippines after the procedure.

News.title: Burnham suggests stocking up on tinned food and bottled water
News.content:
The prime minister has advised people to stock up on tinned food and bottled water in order to be prepared for emergencies.

With storms battering the UK, and in the wake of online disruption caused by a major security flaw, Andy Burnham said "unexpected events seem to be becoming more and more common".

The government has drawn up recommendations for households to have three days' worth of bottled water and tinned food to deal with a crisis such as a war, an online attack or a natural disaster.

Defending government advice to stockpile essentials, he suggested people should also allow themselves some wine to get them through a difficult situation.

At Labour's conference last month, Housing Secretary Angela Rayner joked that her emergency box, external would include a bottle of Sauvignon Blanc wine.

She said she'd include: "Mascara, concealer, I don't know, a bottle of Sauvignon Blanc, a tin of baked beans because you've gotta have some baked beans, and I like a good tin of custard as well so I think that'll keep me going for a while."

Asked whether he agreed with her, Burnham told BBC Radio 5 Live's Matt Chorley: "Well, I'm not sure a bottle of wine is your best first port of call if you're in a slightly crisis situation, but it probably helps when you've done the hard work, but I'll stick to the basics I think.

"I do like my beans, so I have plenty of those in the cupboard and soup.

"I think those are the kind of things that I would recommend people to have as well as well as Twiglets, I'm not sure I can get by without, for too long without those."

Last month, the National Audit Office (NAO) warned Britain's food supply chain is at risk given the growing threat of cyber-attacks and the climate crisis and said the Department for Food, the Environment and Rural Affairs (Defra) had not done enough in recent years to improve supply chain resilience.

The chief executive of the Cold Chain Federation, which represents firms transporting temperature-controlled foods, also told the BBC the UK is being targeted by Russian cyber-hackers who "know that there are pinch points in the food supply system".

Speaking at a wildfire resilience summit in Liverpool, Burnham denied the government had failed to properly prepare, saying: "No, we're having the conversation with people about being better prepared because we're living in a world where unexpected events seem to be becoming more and more common.

"Obviously, weather events, and we're in a situation today where the UK is facing storms and obviously, we feel for the people without power in Cornwall right now.

"It is just having those supplies in the house to get you through those moments. So we are having that conversation about resilience."

News.title: Detective raped by colleague says Met handling of case 'like being raped again'
News.content:
A Metropolitan Police detective, who was raped by a fellow officer, has told the BBC that Scotland Yard's handling of her case was "like being raped all over again".

Det Con Linda Williams was attacked in 2004 by PC David Carrick - a serial abuser jailed for life in 2023 for sexual offences against her and 11 other women.

Linda has post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) because of the attack and sought damages from the Met for failing to protect her from Carrick. The lengthy civil case left her feeling suicidal, she says.

The "worst thing", she says, was when lawyers acting for the Met commissioner challenged the severity of her PTSD on the basis that she had been raped only once.

The Met has told the BBC it "tried to reduce further distress and re-traumatisation to DC Williams' welfare and has aimed to deal with her claims as quickly and compassionately as possible".

"We recognise the unique and additional impact on DC Linda Williams, whose exposure to Carrick came as a result of her being a Met officer," the force added. "Her continued commitment to public service, in spite of the trauma she experienced, is commendable."

Linda, who has waived her legal right to anonymity to speak to the BBC, has settled her civil case and the Met has now paid her compensation without acceptance of liability.

In an unprecedented move for a serving officer, she is now calling publicly for Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley to resign. She believes he has failed to change police culture as promised and she still does not trust her own force to handle cases like hers.

When he took on the most important job in UK policing in 2022, Sir Mark pledged to change the Met. At the time, the force was viewed as being in crisis - following Sarah Everard's murder by a serving officer and other scandals including officers sharing photos of murdered sisters Bibaa Henry and Nicole Smallman.
