News.title: Final James Bond screen tests to take place this weekend, reports say
News.content:
Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O'Connor are among the actors thought to be taking part in final auditions to play James Bond, according to reports.

Screen tests are said to be taking place this weekend, possibly as early as Friday, according to the Hollywood Reporter, external, with between three and five actors understood to have reached the last stages of the process.

The finalists are said to be taking part in auditions with three components - stunts, camera presence and dialogue.

Deadline reported the screen tests, external had been due take place in early October, but had been delayed by scheduling conflicts, while Variety said Turner and Lowden, external "appear to be in the mix" to replace Daniel Craig.

British actors Aaron Taylor-Johnson and James Norton were previously connected to the role, while Irish actor Paul Mescal's name had also been thrown into the mix.

Other actors now appear to be in the frame, but reports on the current casting situation vary.

Variety suggested Slow Horses star Lowden may now be edging ahead, while Masters of the Air star Turner was speculated about earlier this year, with some fans suggesting his wife Dua Lipa could sing the Bond theme song.

Sources told Deadline that at least four final screen test offers have been made, and while unconfirmed, "three of the four expected to test are Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O'Connor".

O'Connor is best known for playing Prince Charles in The Crown, and for starring in 2025's Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery, with Craig.

Jack O'Connell had been thought to be in the mix, but sources said this may no longer be the case, while Euphoria and Wuthering Heights Star Jacob Elordi is not thought to be testing.

Other stars who were previously linked with the role include The King's Man star Harris Dickinson, along with SAS: Rogue Heroes' Jack Barton.

Deadline said: "Even with the tests wrapping next week, there is no timeline for when a final decision will be made."

News.title: Earnings limit of up to £140K for first-time buyers loan scheme
News.content:
Households will need to earn less than Â£110,000 to qualify for the government's new loan scheme for first-time buyers, or Â£140,000 for homes bought in London.

As first reported by The Times, external, the earnings limits are expected to be confirmed at the Budget next week.

The Your First Home scheme will offer government-backed equity loans worth 20% of new-build properties in England bought from participating developers.

The loans, which will also be subject to an initial interest-free period, are designed to help people buy a home with deposits as low as 2.5%.

Previous schemes to help first-time buyers did not restrict eligibility by income but faced criticism for stoking house prices by allowing relatively wealthy households to borrow more.

Unveiling the Your First Home Scheme at last month's Labour conference, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said it would focus on those who "really need support".

Details of the changes, including salary caps, are due to be confirmed at next week's Budget.

The Times reported that ministers had initially decided to set the earnings limits at Â£90,000 for homes outside outside London and Â£110,000 in the capital, before concluding this would deny access to too many middle-earning couples, such as teachers and nurses.

The government has also argued that the scheme will help to boost housebuilding, after ministers conceded they are set to miss a target to build 1.5 million homes in England by the next election.

News.title: Hispanic voters helped bring Trump to power - in Texas, the tide may be turning
News.content:
Texas accounted for roughly one-third of all ICE arrests nationwide in July 2026 - a larger share than any other state - according to government figures obtained by the Deportation Data Project.

"They said we're gonna seek out, capture, detain and deport the worst of the worst," Snipes said in his sermon. "Well, we're here on the border and the cartel is the worst-of-the-worst. So we thought, well, that's a good thing.

"But it turned out, you can hear almost every day, some poor guy going to work and they stop him and detain him and start a big fight."

After the service, two members of the congregation stopped to chat. "We're educators, and we have a lot of students that are having to go back because their parents are getting deported," one said.

"The cruelty that we're seeing - I think that's turning the tide, at least I hope so," their friend added.

Turning the tide politically is what Democrats are hoping they can do in Texas in the midterm elections on 3 November. But that will not be easy.

This stretch of the Rio Grande was once one of the busiest crossing points on the US-Mexico border. Under former President Joe Biden, hundreds of thousands of migrants came through here, with more than two and a half million apprehensions recorded in a single year.

Trump promised to stop these illegal crossings during his 2024 election campaign, and in large parts he has delivered.

Border crossings are now at their lowest level in decades. And it was that promise which in part drove Trump's astonishingly high level of support in the state, taking around 55% of Hispanic votes in Texas alone - a record for a Republican presidential candidate.

Javier Villalobos is the Republican Mayor of McAllen, one of the biggest cities in the Rio Grande Valley. He expects Republicans will find it tough this time around, but credits the Trump administration with stemming the border problem.

"I remember I put out a videoâ¦ thanking the administration for immediately securing the border. That was great," he said. "And I think generally most people are okay with the deportation of criminals, violent people, or people that really are not productive at all."

But if you start deporting people that are productive and law-abiding, that is where the problem is, he added.

News.title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial
News.content:
Shares in the drugmakers MSD (known as Merck in the US) and Moderna have surged since both companies first hinted at the success of the vaccine in the summer.

But investors sold off stock on Thursday after financial analysts said the results were not quite as strong as those seen in an earlier, much smaller trial.

Both companies said they were now "engaging with authorities" suggesting they could file for approval from medicine regulators as soon as next year.

Widespread NHS use will also depend on cost, given that each individual patient will need to have their tumour genetically analysed and a personalised vaccine made for them.

The trial will continue so that the patients involved can be monitored â both to see if the cancer returns over time and to assess whether the drug ultimately helps them live longer.

Professor Alan Melcher from the Institute of Cancer Research in London, who wasn't involved in the research, described the results as "very impressive".

"It is an important proof of principle for the field, although we shouldn't get ahead of the evidence," he said.

"We can't assume from one melanoma trial that the same approach will work across all cancers, and longer follow-up will be important to understand the effect on overall survival."

The full trial results are due to be presented at the European Society of Medical Oncology (ESMO) cancer conference in Madrid on Saturday.

They have yet to be published in a peer-reviewed medical journal, where they can be scrutinised by independent experts.

News.title: Lights will stay on this winter, grid operator says after concerns
News.content:
The lights will stay on this winter, the body in charge of Britain's electricity network has said after concerns were raised by some of its engineers.

The National Energy System Operator (NESO) said the country's electricity system was prepared and "resilient to the challenges it may face" during the colder months.

However, its winter outlook report comes after an independent investigation found engineers had "high levels of stress and concern" about their ability to ensure adequate supply due to differences between renewable and gas-fired power generation.

NESO said supplies were expected to remain secure throughout the winter, though warned there could be "tight days".

It added that such days would result in it deploying notices to power producers that additional electricity generation may be needed. It said such an announcement was not a warning of power cuts and was routine.

"While we never take resilience for granted, households and businesses can be confident that Great Britain's electricity system remains secure, reliable and among the most resilient in the world," said Deborah Petterson, director of whole energy system resilience at NESO.

In a separate report, National Gas, a private company that owns and runs the country's gas network, and is separate from NESO, said it expected to have sufficient supply to meet demand this winter, but forecast gas for power generation to increase at peak demand due to the "intermittent" nature of renewables.

News.title: Give more people weight-loss jabs on the NHS, say MPs
News.content:
Hundreds of thousands more people should be given access to the weight-loss injection Mounjaro on the NHS in England, a cross-party group of MPs says.

The Health Committee said the current plan for 220,000 people to have this jab for free on prescription in 2028 was a "woefully small number" and "unambitious".

This represents only around 6% of eligible people and is a key reason why more than a million have been paying privately for weight-loss injections, including Mounjaro and Wegovy.

The committee says a two-tier system is emerging in which only the wealthy can get good access to the medication that curbs appetite.

News.title: Man, 61, in court charged with murder of 'stabbed' woman who died after crash
News.content:
A 61-year-old man has appeared in court charged with the murder of a woman who suffered "stab wounds" and died following a crash.

Eleanor Barnfield, 47, died in hospital after police were called to a crash on Coity Road in Bridgend on Monday, where they found she had "puncture wounds unrelated to the collision". The BBC understands they were sustained in a stabbing.

Clifford Foster was arrested on Tuesday at the Ger-y-Nant retirement housing complex, close to where the crash happened, where he lived and Eleanor worked.

Speaking only to confirm his name, age and address, Foster appeared at Newport Magistrates' Court on Friday, wearing a grey tracksuit and using a crutch to support himself.

News.title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says
News.content:
Private companies buying up care homes for older people in England could undermine the government's plan to create a universal care service, the regulator says.

The Care Quality Commission's annual report, external highlights how a rising share of the care home market is owned by large firms - the five biggest increased their share by 26% in the last two years, driven by interest from US property investors, and now own one in seven homes.

While there can be benefits, there are concerns the trend can lead to higher prices and a reduction in quality.

The regulator said rapid changes to the market, including the fragmentation of home help into more smaller services, needed monitoring and clearer planning.

The CQC said the changes to at-home care, which covers support to help people wash and dress, could create inefficiencies - nearly a third of these services are providing care to four or fewer people.

In contrast, there are few smaller care homes judged important for providing specialist and personalised care.

Small care homes have always represented a tiny proportion of the care home market, but over the last 14 years the numbers have fallen significantly, particularly those that combine care with nursing support, which are down by a quarter.

News.title: Prepare for supply chain disruption from cyber or climate emergencies, Streeting warns
News.content:
Members of the public and businesses need to think more about how they would cope with natural disasters, cyber-attacks or state-sponsored terrorism, the defence secretary has said.

Wes Streeting warned people needed to be more aware of emerging risks facing the UK and make plans to deal with them.

He added that the government was launching a "national resilience conversation" to raise awareness, including advice for households like stocking up on food, bottled water and first aid supplies.

Streeting also said that cyber incidents - like the recently discovered critical security flaw in the programming language which powers much of the internet - will happen "more and more".

Streeting told BBC One's Question Time that the UK is facing a greater threat to the country, "than we have certainly for most, if not all, of my lifetime".

Speaking to an audience at the UK Gun Hall Plant in Telford earlier on Thursday, where it was announced production of tank gun barrels would return to the UK, he spoke of "everyday challenges" facing households.

He pointed to wildfires burning this summer and the flooding that is expected this winter.

Streeting said the public need to be prepared for "increasingly sophisticated cyber-attacks" on businesses, or supply chain disruption caused by "hostile state actors or terrorists".

The defence secretary referenced the critical security flaw in the PHP programming language which has left organisations around the world scrambling to update their systems.

In the UK, 32 government services were offline while the potential cyber-security issues were addressed.

"It's not just from foreign states engaged in espionage or sabotage; it's also organised criminals," Streeting told Question Time.

"In this world of AI that we live in... it does also present threats if people are innovating and pushing against conventional [cyber] defences."

News.title: Mum sentenced for killing her three children
News.content:
A mother who admitted killing her three children has been sentenced to an indefinite hospital order in a secure psychiatric facility.

The bodies of Fares Bash, seven, Joury Bash, three, and nine-month-old Mohammed Bash were discovered on Blaise Walk in Sea Mills, Bristol, on 18 February 2024.

Appearing at Bristol Crown Court earlier, Yasmeen Ali, 44, admitted three charges of manslaughter on the grounds of diminished responsibility, as her defence said she was suffering from an "acute psychosis".

She wept as details of the fatal injuries were read out, and Judge Justice Linden - describing her as a loving mother - said: "It is my view you would not have done what you have if you were well."

Ali, speaking through an interpreter, appeared in court wearing a purple coat and a black head scarf.

Only six people were allowed into the courtroom to minimise the impact on her mental health.

News.title: Monk on Caldey Island gave naked photos of himself to visitors
News.content:
She said she was stunned but did not say anything to Keet because she thought he would deny it and she might be asked to leave the island.

Natalie said: "I think the worst thing it did, if I'm completely honest, it took away my whole spiritual belief in Catholicism."

But Keet claimed she turned "wickedly against him" after he rejected her attempts to seduce him.

It is also claimed Keet made several unwelcome sexual advances towards an employee of the abbey.

Allegedly, he touched her breasts and bottom, commented on her body and referred to her genitals, despite being asked not to.

Other allegations included making sexualised comments while showing nude photos of himself and pictures of naked women.

It is claimed Keet was confronted at the time but said UK law did not apply to him as he was a Dutch citizen, that he could do as he liked as he was on a private island and allegedly, he called the employee "too sensitive".

He is also accused of saying the woman was lucky to receive sexual attention from him and "women welcomed male attention".

It is also claimed the monk told her she would lose her job if she complained.

Keet said the allegations were false and quoted The Bible in his statement to the podcast: "To all who are pure themselves, everything is pure; but to those who have been corrupted and lack faith, nothing can be pure [Letter to Titus 1,15]."

He said the employee had made up the allegations in the hope the monastery would pay her money and that she was paid to "keep quiet".

"If it was not so sad, it would be laughable, how she could make up so many allegations spread out over three years, in which we had co-operated so pleasantly together. Very sad," he added.

News.title: Ed Sheeran’s former band Beoga say singer’s Macklemore decision will ‘follow him around’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Beoga, Ed Sheeran’s former band who quit his tour after Macklemore was dropped for making pro-Palestinian remarks on stage, have claimed that the singer’s decision will “follow him around”.

The Irish band were among the acts to withdraw from the US leg of Sheeran’s Loop tour in September in support of the “Thrift Shop” rapper and people of Palestine.

Returning to stage after the scandal, Sheeran tearfully said that his friends and family had “abandoned” him after “one of the worst weeks of my life”.

Speaking in their first major interview, Beoga members Eamon Murray and Niamh Dunne told The Irish Times that they hadn’t “fallen out” with Sheeran, but that it was important to “hold your friends accountable… whether it’s Ed Sheeran or your mad neighbour”.

open image in gallery Irish trad band Beoga, who played on stage with Sheeran ( Getty )

Bodhrán player Murray theorised that Sheeran will have had “counsel coming from 100 places”, and that his stance would go on to haunt him.

“People will remember that’s the position we took and they’ll remember that Ed took that position. That will follow him around. He will have to wrestle with that,” he said.

“My position has been to Ed and anybody, you can say whatever you want; if you don’t take action, it doesn’t matter. You can make 100 statements. But if you don’t cancel the shows, it doesn’t matter what you say if you don’t do anything... We should all be able to freely and openly stand up and say ‘Free Palestine’. We support a free Palestine.”

Announcing their decision to withdraw from the tour in the days that followed, Beoga wrote on Instagram that “to play in venues that silence anyone advocating for a Free Palestine is not an option for us”.

“The decision to stand up for free speech and the right to speak about Palestine was a very easy decision for us as a band to make,” Dunne said. “The professional and financial stakes are very real.”

Murray echoed: “A friend of mine said, when we knew we were going to be put in an awkward position, ‘Courage can’t see around a corner.’

open image in gallery Sheeran ( AFP/Getty )

“In terms of the material cost to us all, nobody thought about that at the time. It’s since then that you think about it and go, ‘Okay, right.’ But you’d torture yourself if you thought about all the things that were going to come.”

The Independent has contacted Sheeran’s representatives for comment.

Things kicked off in September after “Same Love” musician Macklemore announced that he had been dropped as the support act for the remainder of Sheeran’s US tour dates.

Macklemore claimed that the singer told him that Robert Kraft — the CEO of Kraft Group who owns Gillette Stadium — had personally called to say that he would not be allowed to perform at the venue.

Sheeran responded with his own lengthy public statement saying that he would not be drawn into a public debate about the Gaza war and that the decision to remove Macklemore was “the promoter’s decision”.

Following this, Irish acts Beoga and Aaron Rowe, the Danish band Lukas Graham, and Billie Eilish’s brother Finneas all individually announced on Instagram that they were withdrawing from the tour.

On stage in Philadelphia, Sheeran told his fans: “I’ve had to take and make difficult decisions, and I am making mistakes. I’m so, so sorry. I don’t want to disappoint fans. I want my music and shows to be about unity, not division; about humanity, not politics.”

He continued: “But this is a humanitarian issue. I cannot hide how I feel about it anymore. What happened in Israel, and at the music festival on October 7th was horrific and compounded centuries of Jewish pain. What is happening in Gaza is catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate.

“My heart has been broken by the scale of devastation and loss of civilian loss and loss of children’s lives. And the systemic injustice we’re seeing unfolding the West Bank cannot be overlooked.”

News.title: What are the accusations against Meghan Markle’s father Thomas?
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

For free real time breaking news alerts sent straight to your inbox sign up to our breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

The Duchess of Sussex’s estranged father Thomas Markle Snr is accused of possessing child sex abuse images.

Meghan Markle’s half-brother, Thomas Markle Jnr, alleged that he found images belonging to her father at his former home in the Philippines, The Sun reported.

In an interview with the Daily Mail, Mr Markle Snr denied possessing child sex images, calling the accusations “sick lies”.

The Sun reports that Mr Markle Jnr told police he discovered “hundreds, if not thousands” of the images at his father’s home in Cebu.

open image in gallery Meghan and her father have not spoken since 2018 ( Instagram )

According to the newspaper, Mr Markle Snr is alleged to have left the images in storage boxes when he moved out of the property earlier this year.

Mr Markle Jnr said he submitted a statement to police in the Philippines and told The Sun: “When I found this material I was horrified and I had no option but to report my dad.

“I have supported, cared for him and helped him for years – but that stops now. I won’t speak to my father ever again unless I’m called to give evidence against him.”

The newspaper reports that Mr Markle Jnr was searching for a phone for his girlfriend’s father in boxes of his own father’s belongings, which led him to discover the images and videos.

In July, he reported them to the FBI Hotline, the United States’ National Centre for Exploited and Missing Children and state police in Pennsylvania, where his father was living.

Mr Markle Jnr also retrieved the four large cardboard boxes from storage and an IT expert helped him access three computer hard drives, revealing further images, The Sun reports.

Court papers filed in Cebu have begun police inquiry, the newspaper says.

open image in gallery Mr Markle has denied the allegations ( Instagram )

Authorities in the UK had previously told the Duchess that allegations made about her father in a 2018 letter sent to Scotland Yard and subsequently shared with her by police were being investigated, it is understood.

In 2025, Mr Markle Snr moved to the Philippines for a new life after suffering a series of strokes.

Then, in December of that year he had his leg amputated during life-saving surgery.

He is reportedly now living in a rehab centre in Florida, where he is learning to walk again.

The Duchess has been estranged from her former TV lighting director father since the weeks before her wedding in 2018, after he staged and sold photographs to the paparazzi.

Meghan said in a statement: “I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed.

“In 2018, a letter was sent to the Metropolitan Police and Royalty and Specialist Protection. That letter was subsequently shared with me.

“It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated.

“I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them.

“I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families.

“Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children.”

In response to the accusations, Mr Markle Snr said: “I'm shocked, I'm hurt and I'm very upset that my son is making these accusations against me. I could never do what I'm being accused of. It's the worst thing anyone could accuse me of.

“This is bulls****. It's just a bunch of lies. It's sick. I have no idea why Tom is trying to destroy me with these lies.”

News.title: Next Man United manager: Who could replace Michael Carrick?
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Michael Carrick is running out of time to save his job at Manchester United, with the club poised to ramp up the search for a fourth permanent manager in three years since minority owners Ineos took over football operations.

Carrick – who impressed during his interim spell in charge last season – has come under huge pressure following United’s worst start to a season in 40 years and the dismal 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

While the problems United face run far deeper than the head coach – as highlighted by defender Lisandro Martinez after the defeat to Atletico Madrid earlier this month – Carrick’s appears to be on the brink following criticism of his tactics by the United captain Bruno Fernandes.

While he is set to remain in charge for Sunday’s home game against Bournemouth, the club have already discussed potential replacements should Carrick follow the departures of Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim under the Ineos leadership.

But who could United turn to as they seek to salvage their campaign?

Eddie Howe

The Englishman is available after his shock decision to leave Newcastle United in the summer. Howe told the club he needed a break from management but the chance to take charge at Old Trafford, three months later, would surely be too good to turn down if an offer arrives. The 48-year-old remains highly regarded in English football after taking over a Newcastle side in the relegation zone and leading them to the club’s highest Premier League finish in two decades, as well as their first domestic silverware in 70 years. Howe twice took Newcastle into the Champions League playing an energetic, high-intensity style of football that would be popular at Old Trafford. He is currently the favourite with the bookies.

open image in gallery Howe led Newcastle to the Carabao Cup in 2025 before leaving at the end of the following season ( Getty )

Fabian Hurzeler

Brighton have been the surprise package in the Premier League this season and the 33-year-old Hurzeler has drawn praise for turning the Seagulls into a side capable of competing with the country’s biggest clubs. Brighton’s 3-0 victory over champions Arsenal earlier this season was a masterclass in modern coaching while Hurzeler’s side also knocked United out of the Carabao Cup with a brilliant 3-2 win at Old Trafford. The Independent’s Chief Football Writer Miguel Delaney has reported that Hurzeler is admired at Old Trafford but Brighton would demand significant compensation for the highly-rated German and United may not have the cash. At Brighton, Hurzeler has also enjoyed an environment where the club have made all the right decisions off the pitch. At United, he would arguably be walking into the opposite.

The Brighton boss said on Friday: “I’m fully focused on my job here. I’ve got no time to think about these rumours because we play every three days. I have a lot of respect for Michael Carrick and the job he has done at Manchester United the last season. He's a great human being, a great personality, and I really respect him. There's nothing more to say about that. I’m really privileged to be here. I’m part of a journey [at Brighton] and I still have this feeling when I go to bed that we are not finished with our journey... “We have built this [together] over the years. We’ve had good periods, we’ve had bad periods. To build these connections you need time. You don’t take these things for granted. It’s a people business. Making a people business out of this pressure business is something I don’t take for granted and something I won’t throw away that fast.”

open image in gallery Fabian Hurzeler led Brighton to a brilliant win at Old Trafford earlier this season ( Getty )

Julian Nagelsmann

The former wunderkind of German coaching was reportedly on United’s radar when they sacked Ruben Amorim at the start of the year, but as an option for the summer following the World Cup. Well, that was a bit of a disaster for the former Bayern Munich and RB Leipzig coach, as Germany were knocked out in the last-32 by Paraguay. Nagelsmann, 39, would naturally be interested in managing United and the club’s director of recruitment, Christopher Vivell, previously worked with him at Red Bull.

open image in gallery Julian Nagelsmann has been considered by United in the past and is available ( Getty )

Unai Emery

The Spaniard has done a superb job at Aston Villa by securing Champions League qualification and ending the club’s trophy drought with victory in the Europa League. But Aston Villa will be even more determined to keep Emery given the club are only in the early stages of their rebuild under him, having completely overhauled the spine of their team over the summer. As it is, Emery enjoys complete control over his project at Villa Park, a reality he is unlikely to find at Old Trafford, while he appears enthused by the challenge of constructing a second competitive team in the Premier League. With Emery, who is under contract until 2029, United would also need to pay Villa compensation, and that may place him above their budget.

open image in gallery Unai Emery appears enthused by the challenge of building ‘Villa 2.0’ ( Getty )

Antonio Conte

The appeal of the combustible Italian only has grown while United have been accused of becoming too passive and pedestrian on the pitch. Conte is one of the most demanding coaches in the game and would instantly bring a level of intensity and urgency that has been lacking this season, while his CV – with Serie A titles at Juventus, Inter Milan and Napoli and a Premier League crown with Chelsea – commands respect. Conte also brought an immediate improvement when he took charge of a floundering Tottenham five years ago and led them back into the Champions League, which now has to be United’s biggest concern. So the 57-year-old offers impact, but then what? Conte has a sharp tongue and is not afraid to criticise his bosses if he feels they are failing to support him. His exit from Tottenham in March 2023 followed a stunning evisceration of the club in a now legendary press conference at Southampton. United would be playing with fire but options of Conte’s calibre are few and far between.

In a statement on Friday, Conte distanced himself from the Manchester United job while branding reports that he is in “advanced negotiations” with any club as “speculation”. He said: “Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management. It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right. I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my ‘strong personality’. These reports are unfounded, as there is currently no concrete basis for such assessments.”

open image in gallery United could be playing with fire if they turn to Conte ( AFP/Getty )

Cesc Fabregas

The former Arsenal, Barcelona and Chelsea midfielder is developing a reputation as Europe’s brightest young coach – as his brilliant Como side demonstrated by thrashing United in the Champions League on Wednesday night. The Spaniard appears committed to his project in northern Italy, though, and also has a financial incentive to continue leading Como in their debut Champions League campaign due to owning a stake in the Serie A club. The 39-year-old’s own stock is also rising and the lure of returning to one of his former clubs in the future, such as Barcelona, could result in Fabregas taking a patient and considered approach to his next move.

open image in gallery Cesc Fabregas helped Como into the Champions League for the first time in their history after just two years in the job ( Reuters )

Another interim

Well, we’ve been here before. Before Michael Carrick stepped into the breach in January it was Under-18s manager Darren Fletcher, who oversaw the draw with Burnley and FA Cup third-round defeat to Brighton. Before him, Ruud van Nistelrooy held the reins between Erik ten Hag’s dismissal and Amorim’s appointment and before that, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer experienced the same cycle of boom-and-bust that Carrick has gone through over the past 10 months. In short, there’s no shortage of former United players who are available to remind an underperforming dressing room of the importance of the badge and the meaning of the shirt. It could be time for Fletcher to give Sir Alex another call.

News.title: The show-stopping fashion is the most exciting thing about this season of Celebrity Traitors
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Watching the round table showdowns during the current season of The Celebrity Traitors, it seems like our star players’ goals are threefold. Root out the Traitors. Argue back if you’re wrongly under suspicion. And if you can’t manage the first two? Make sure you’re wearing something unforgettable.

Ever since the show launched on the BBC in 2022, presenter Claudia Winkleman’s tartan goth style – a high camp array of kilts, chunky knits, leather gloves worthy of a Bond villain and ruffled Victoriana blouses – has become a source of feverish fashion worship. The pieces that she wears, whether they be from a high street brand or a little-known independent designer, have a habit of selling out almost as soon as they appear on screen.

But this time around, Winkleman has some serious sartorial competition. This autumn’s cohort of famous faces might be floundering a little as they try to work out who can be trusted in the castle, and who is just a very good liar – but they are certainly having plenty of fun with fashion at the same time.

Undoubtedly top of the style pecking order is Love Island host turned Traitor extraordinaire Maya Jama, who set the tone in the first episode when she rocked up wearing a £2,570 hi-shine khaki trench coat from Saint Laurent, looking like some sort of cartoonishly chic detective inspector from a schlocky sci-fi movie.

The fact that she was immediately anointed as a Traitor by Winkleman might have caused a less confident fashionista to try and fly under the radar in unremarkable outfits. Instead, Jama has taken the opposite approach. On day two, she wore a shaggy sheepskin bolero jacket with almost comically exaggerated shoulders in a mustardy yellow hue. The vibe? If Big Bird spent a year studying at Central St Martins.

open image in gallery Jama kicked things off with a high-end trench from Saint Laurent ( BBC/Studio Lambert/Euan Cherry )

Jama’s power jacket, the work of London design house Agro Studio, encapsulates the perfect Traitors style formula – go all-out on the top half, because that’s what viewers will see when you’re sat at the roundtable. This is, of course, the most keenly watched, most intensely dramatic part of each episode, so it makes sense to dress the part and lean into the show’s theatricality.

open image in gallery Jama’s fuzzy bolero is one of this series’ most talked-about looks ( BBC/Studio Lambert/Euan Cherry )

Following the same cues is former Little Mix star Leigh-Anne Pinnock, who has been offering up her own colourful take on lady of the manor style, playing with typically Traitors-esque plaids and chequered fabrics but making them her own with bold shapes and eye-catching colours.

Her first castle outfit was a vintage Dolce & Gabbana checked jacket and skirt co-ord (sourcing pieces from the archives shows just how seriously this year’s celebs are taking the show’s fashion contest), while her sunshine yellow tweedy jacket in a cropped trench-like style from Paul Costelloe helped brighten up an early roundtable.

open image in gallery Pinnock brightened things up in sunshine yellow tweed ( CREDIT LINE:BBC/Studio Lambert/Euan Cherry )

Pinnock has also thrown in a few more affordable labels too, like when she wore a raincoat from Instagram favourite Damson Madder. On Thursday night’s show, though, her penchant for a slightly out-there fashion choice might have subconsciously influenced her fellow players to distrust her. “The gloves don’t help,” comedian Joanne McNally quipped of the singer’s elbow length red gloves (“proper Cruella deVil vibes!”) during a debrief with Pinnock and Romesh Ranganathan after the round table. It’s The Traitors after all – more tenuous stuff has certainly been seized upon as proof of nefarious nighttime goings-on.

McNally, meanwhile, prefers a statement shirt and tie for her roundtable appearances, experimenting with oversized collars and unexpected textures, like her shiny lilac-on-lilac ensemble in episode three. Opting for a more lowkey but still stylish look is 70-year-old Jerry Hall, who has gone full Highland heroine with a dash of Americana, alternating extremely cosy knits and tartan scarves with fringed jackets nodding to her Texan roots.

Also worthy of note? Joe Lycett’s characteristically out-there get-ups, which included a refreshingly bonkers polka dot blazers and shorts combo, paired with fuzzy lilac lapels and matching socks, a chequerboard anorak and what appeared to be a cow print shell suit. Ranganathan’s looks, meanwhile, are considerably more pared back in comparison; he’s very much flying the flag for the fashion conscious every-bloke in his patterned jackets (again, putting the focus on the upper half for those breakfast and roundtable moments).

open image in gallery Joe Lycett, left, dons a checked jacket and Jerry Hall, centre, opts for Highland chic ( CREDIT LINE:BBC/Studio Lambert/Euan Cherry )

This fashion smorgasbord doesn’t just happen by magic, of course. The show has a dedicated cast stylist, Catherine Moran, whose job is to make sure that the players’ looks work together on screen, and that each star has a distinct visual identity.

Before filming starts, Moran recently revealed to The Telegraph, the celebs receive a “wardrobe guide” featuring a few mood boards and some pointers on colour, “which looks great on screen”. This cheat sheet also has tips on “practical elements such as how many outfits they need, activewear for missions and other bits and bobs they may not have thought of”.

She’ll then talk to the stars about what they want to wear; some of them will work with stylists, others will choose their own clothes, and some “want some help from me to put it together”, she told The Telegraph. Then when filming is in process, she will “coordinate the cast together each day, ensuring that we have a good selection of colours throughout, and everyone looks and feels different”.

The process is similar for the civilian version of the show (albeit presumably without the input of personal stylists). And although the main competition hasn’t quite had as many big style moments as the celebrity spin-off, there have been a few Traitors and Faithfuls who deserve honourable mentions, like jumpsuit-loving Stephen and bold knitwear aficionado Jade from season four earlier this year.

Of course, not all the players are jostling to make a fashion statement. There’s been plenty of sensible outdoor gear from the likes of James Acaster and Ross Kemp, who are flying the flag for the Mountain Warehouse man (although Kemp probably ensured all of his anoraks and puffa coats were SAS-approved beforehand – that is a guy who takes preparation seriously).

With just a handful of episodes left before the finale, we’re now reaching the point in the competition where we’re having to bid farewell to some of our snazziest on-screen dressers – and bemoaning the Traitors’ murdering and the Faithfuls’ blundering voting strategies for depriving us of more great outfits. Their game plans might not have been flawless, but this celebrity cohort has certainly proven that the castle can be a catwalk.

News.title: Marathon world champion Peres Jepchirchir suspended after positive EPO test
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Reigning marathon world champion Peres Jepchirchir has been suspended by the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) after testing positive for EPO.

The 33-year-old returned an adverse analytical finding for the performance-enhancing drug in an out-of-competition sample taken in Kenya before her victory at the Sydney Marathon this August.

The AIU announced it had provisionally suspended Jepchirchir in a statement released on Friday, just a day after Ethiopia’s former Tokyo Marathon winner Ruti Aga was given a six-year ban for a positive test for methylprednisolone and tampering with the investigation.

The timing of Jepchirchir’s positive test, before her victory in Sydney, means the result is at risk of being struck from her record.

The Kenyan’s case could follow the pattern set by her compatriot, 2019 marathon world champion Ruth Chepng’etich. Chepng’etich was banned for three years from April 2025 after she tested positive for and admitted using the banned substance hydrochlorothiazide, a diuretic commonly used to mask the use of performance-enhancing drugs.

All of her results, titles, appearance and prize money from the date of her positive test in March 2025 were forfeited but her achievements and records from before the date of her positive test still stand, including her marathon world record, set in Chicago in 2024.

She was granted a one-year reduction from the automatic four-year ban after accepting the sanction within 20 days.

Jepchirchir is a four-time World Marathon Major winner and claimed Olympic gold in the marathon at Tokyo 2020, and is currently fifth in the world rankings.

She won the world marathon title for the first time in Tokyo last September, adding to her two individual half-marathon world titles, and is both a former world record holder in the half-marathon and a former women’s-only world record holder in the marathon, set when she won in London in 2024.

She withdrew from this year’s London Marathon due to a stress fracture sustained after finishing second in the Valencia marathon last December, making her return to top-level competition in Sydney. She dominated the event, finishing in 2:18:31, over three minutes clear of second-placed ‌compatriot Irine Cheptai.

More follows

News.title: Who is supporting Gianni Infantino and how many votes will secure re-election as Fifa president?
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Gianni Infantino is facing a battle to cling onto his Fifa presidency heading into next year’s election after his botched bid to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors resulted in a significant loss in support.

England and Wales have been among the football associations to join European governing body Uefa in leading the charge for Infantino’s removal from power, formally withdrawing their endorsement of the Swiss-Italian for re-election in March 2027.

But as the dust has settled on his privatisation ploy, Infantino’s bid for a third term has strengthened. His allies have surfaced, with the likes of Mexico and Argentina joining Caf, the African football governing body, in reaffirming support for the under-fire president, and now the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has reversed its position and backed Infantino with AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa underlining that there is “a true understanding between us”.

Infantino needs 106 votes from the 211 member associations to be re-elected as president. Here is every country and confederation to have expressed their opposition or support for Infantino:

Who has formally withdrawn its support for Infantino?

Uefa (55 members) 🇪🇺

Uefa, the governing body for Europe, has staunchly opposed Infantino’s leadership. They threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions before Infantino’s eventual climbdown but has continued to assert that his position is untenable, even taking legal action against the Swiss-Italian.

The body points to how there have not been “assurances” that attempts like the privatisation of the World Cup “to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again”.

More recently, Uefa general secretary Theodore Theodoridis has written to his Fifa counterpart Mattias Grafstrom setting out a series of questions on behalf of European members of the Fifa Council, demanding documents covering a series of Infantino controversies. Fifa has until 2 November to answer these questions.

Concacaf (41 members) 🌎

Concacaf, the Confederation for North America and the Caribbean, came out in opposition of Infantino after being left stunned at the lack of consultation during the Fifa sell-off plan, which they went on to reject.

After the plan was aborted, the confederation said: “This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour. A comprehensive reckoning with this presidency is imperative.”

Concacaf president Victor Montagliani was initially seen as a front-runner to challenge Infantino in next March’s election but he now looks set to pursue another term as Concacaf chief.

open image in gallery Concacaf president Victor Montagliani ( Getty )

England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿

The English FA are one of many European member associations to send a letter to Fifa withdrawing its support for Infantino’s re-election in 2027.

Infantino’s apology letter that was sent around on Wednesday night changed nothing for the FA, who was “deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance” surrounding his sell-off scheme.

open image in gallery FA chief executive Mark Bullingham (left) next to Gianni Infantino ( PA )

Wales 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿

The Football Association of Wales were one of the first to send its letter withdrawing support for Infantino.

“The ‌recent failures in good governance, processes, ‌leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgment ​have led us to a position ‌where Mr Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to ‌remain at the helm of world football,” a statement read. “Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.”

Scotland 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿

The SFA’s chief executive Ian Maxwell told the BBC that the governing body’s position has “been clear” since Uefa’s collective statement.

“We have aligned ourselves with the Uefa position and 55 nations are stronger than one voice.

“Their statement since then has talked about a lack of confidence in the Fifa leadership and the Scottish FA agree completely with that decision.

“The SFA will not be voting for Gianni Infantino come the re-election in early 2027.”

Republic of Ireland 🇮🇪

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) has followed in withdrawing its support for Infantino while backing Uefa’s stance.

"Following an FAI board meeting, the decision was taken to rescind the letter of support that the Association supplied earlier this year," it confirmed. "It has since written to Fifa to explain its reasoning. The Association is grateful for the support that Fifa provides to Irish football, but recent events have raised significant concerns regarding governance, transparency and the lack of meaningful consultation.”

Italy 🇮🇹

The Italian Football Federation (FIGC) took a few weeks to take official action but it has now withdrawn its support for Infantino's candidacy in the next Fifa presidential election scheduled.

"This decision is intended to clearly and transparently express the FIGC's position - in full agreement with Uefa and its president Aleksander Ceferin - regarding the recent initiatives promoted by the FIFA president concerning the governance and development of international competitions," FIGC said in a statement.

Finland 🇫🇮

Finland kickstarted this process, with it being revealed that the Scandinavian member association was the first to send a letter officially withdrawing support for Infantino.

Serbia 🇷🇸

The Football Association of Serbia then sent a similar letter to Fifa.

“We would like to remind you that we provided our support to Mr Infantino in writing on 25 May of this year, but after carefully considering the events that have seriously damaged the image and reputation of both Fifa and its president in the past period, this is the only logical and rational course of action,” a statement read.

Sweden 🇸🇪

Sweden’s federation (SvFF) followed suit: "At an extraordinary board meeting on Monday, SvFF has chosen not to support Fifa President Gianni Infantino ​in the upcoming re-election.

"This is after a long-term assessment of the development within Fifa and the organization's leadership. The decision is based on recurring shortcomings in governance, transparency and management, which means that trust in Gianni Infantino's leadership no longer exists."

open image in gallery Infantino has officially lost the endorsement of numerous Uefa nations ( PA )

Croatia 🇭🇷

As did the Croatian Football Federation (HNS): "The Croatian Football Federation has informed Fifa of its decision to withdraw the support previously expressed for Mr Gianni Infantino's candidature for another term as Fifa president.

"This decision followed a thorough reassessment within the federation in light of recent developments surrounding the Fifa World Cup 2026 and discussions within our governing bodies. We consider our position to be clearly communicated to Fifa and have no further comment to add at this time."

Albania 🇦🇱

The Albanian Football Federation also took the same stance, aligning with Uefa.

“The Albanian Football Association has sent an official letter to Fifa Secretary General Mattias Grafström, informing him that it has withdrawn its support for Mr Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for another four-year term as Fifa President,” the statement confirmed.

Greece 🇬🇷

The Greek Football Association has backed Uefa’s push for a change in Fifa’s leadership, similarly withdrawing support to underscore a united European front in opposition to Infantino.

"The Greek FA (EPO) has taken a clear position against a candidacy of Gianni Infantino," EPO presdient Makis Gagatsis told reporters. "We saw things happen at the World Cup that are not acceptable to football public opinion. Then... came a programme to sell World Cup rights and we are clearly against it, so we withdrew our support of the Fifa president."

Germany 🇩🇪

The German federation (DFB) already opted against endorsing Infantino earlier in the year so has not had to send a letter withdrawing support to take an opposing stance.

“The DFB has not signed a letter of support for the re-election of Gianni Infantino," the governing body stated in July. "Further steps will be discussed in the DFB presidential board."

Former Germany national team director Oliver Bierhoff further reiterated the nation’s loss of trust in Infantino: "We have to take care of football. It is already commercial but it is a property for all of football. The world views may be different but in the last weeks and months a lot happened so that we have no trust any more that it will be going in the right direction."

Denmark 🇩🇰

Denmark are in a similar position to Germany, having not endorsed Infantino’s re-election bid prior to the scheme’s reveal.

There is also a precedent for their opposition to Infantino, with federation president Jesper Moller not supporting his re-election efforts back in 2022: “There is only one candidate ... but Denmark will not be supporting the current president.”

Norway 🇳🇴

The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) have been one of the most vocal bodies to call for Infantino’s resignation, and while they have not yet officially sent a letter to withdraw their support in him, such action is expected in the coming days.

NFF president Lise Klaveness told the Guardian: “We decided that there is no trust in Infantino now. We have been worried consistently and there has been one more step in worrying direction every year, every part of the year. The trust is now gone for us, there is no way back for Infantino.

“We’re left in a very polarised cooperation globally and, I would say, chaos. So we will ask him to resign immediately so that the global football community can look ahead and cooperate going into the future.”

open image in gallery Lise Klaveness has called on Infantino to resign ( Reuters )

Netherlands 🇳🇱

The Royal Dutch Football Association (KNVB) is also yet to officially withdraw its support but is among the many to have confirmed it has lost confidence in Infantino’s leadership.

“The way this process has unfolded has resulted in a fundamental loss of confidence in the leadership of Fifa President Gianni Infantino. The KNVB no longer has confidence in his leadership,” a statement read.

Romania 🇷🇴

The Romanian Football Federation (FRF) were among the countries to resolutely reject the sell-off proposal, calling it “a dangerous initiative to turn football into a private asset.

As a result, the FRF will withold support for Infantino’s re-election for the time being, with a statement reading: “FRF is suspending the discussion regarding the support of Fifa President Gianni Infantino for a new term, until further clarifications.”

Northern Ireland ☘️

The Northern Irish football association (IFA) has expressed “concerns” over Infantino’s leadership but has not officially withdrawn its support yet, unlike neighbours Ireland.

"We take our responsibilities as a member association of both Uefa and Fifa seriously," said an IFA spokesperson. "We support the current Uefa position on the matter and will continue to engage constructively on issues relating to football governance. We are of course aware of the recent developments and wider concerns within the football community. We are considering these matters carefully and will continue to engage through the appropriate governance structures and channels.”

Jordan 🇯🇴

Jordan are so far the only non-Uefa member association to publicly oppose Infantino after federation president Prince Ali bin Hussein levelled accusations of blackmail against Fifa.

Prince Ali alleged the organisation offered assistance with the kingdom's issues in exchange for his endorsement, following Infantino's withdrawal from a World Cup stake sale proposal. Among the problems cited was the association's eight-month wait for prize money, due since December for reaching the Arab Cup final in Qatar.

After taking to X to reveal the outstanding payments, the Jordan Football Association received the prize money two days later - but Prince Ali has not changed his stance over not endorsing Infantino: “It does not change my clear position concerning the leadership of Fifa: my FA and I will not endorse president Infantino, nor will we vote for him.”

New Zealand 🇳🇿

New Zealand have broken rank with Oceania’s confederation by withdrawing their support for Infantino.

"After careful consideration, NZF has formed the view that decisions and actions within Fifa have contributed to a breakdown in trust and increased division within international football, and that an independent review is required to restore confidence and trust,” a statement read.

Who is supporting Infantino?

Confederation of African Football (54 members) 🌍

Caf, the governing body for African football, was the first confederation to unanimously back Infantino.

“We are committed to continue working together with Fifa, its member associations, other football confederations and stakeholders to safeguard and adhere to governance, due process, and transparency global best practises and to contribute to the development and growth of football worldwide,” Caf president Patrice Motsepe said.

Motsepe later added that the position of embattled president Infantino can only be decided by Fifa elections.

Asian Football Confederation (47 members) 🌏

The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has endorsed Infantino an apparent turnaround in its stance from two months ago when it criticised the head of football’s world governing body for a breach of trust.

AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, speaking at the body’s extraordinary congress meeting in Tokyo on Friday, embraced Infantino with a large hug in front of the membership as he delivered his endorsement.

“We affirm our full commitment to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a new mandate as the Fifa president.” Sheikh Salman said. “You’ve visited a lot of countries in Asia. I’ve spoken to a lot of members within this continent. I know your feeling and I think your commitment is clear as well.”

Argentina 🇦🇷

Argentina became the first member from South America to voice its support for Infantino, on the same day that confederation Conmebol - which had thus far only expressed support of Infantino - expressed concern over Fifa’s procedures.

"Of our highest consideration, on behalf of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), and its Executive Committee, we address you, dear President, and through your worthy intermediary the Fifa board, to express our support for the management carried out during the last 10 years, which had as its main axes the development of football throughout the world and institutional solidity based on a clear governance model, stable and transparent,” a statement read.

open image in gallery Argentina president Javier Milei (left) behind Infantino at the "Board of Peace" hosted by US president Donald Trump ( AFP/Getty )

Paraguay 🇵🇾

Paraguay has also followed suit as Infantino’s Conmebol support base begins to surface.

Their federation published a letter of support addressed to Infantino, writing that it "reaffirms its commitment to continue working alongside Fifa”.

Mexico 🇲🇽

Mexico joined Argentina from the Americas, breaking rank from the United States, Canada and the rest of Concacaf that had condemned Infantino’s plan and aligned itself against his leadership.

The Mexican Football Federation (FMF) stated: "The FMF will neither recognise nor approve any process convened outside of that institutional framework, and it joins the call made... by President Infantino to collectively continue developing football for the benefit of the 211 member associations."

Grenada 🇬🇩

Grenada’s federation (GFA) has also broken away from the Concacaf block and reaffirmed its support for Infantino.

“The GFA reaffirms its support for Fifa President Gianni Infantino and expresses its sincere appreciation for his continued support for football development in Grenada and across the Caribbean over his period of service in office and for the years to come,” a statement read.

Saint Kitts and Nevis 🇰🇳

Like Grenada, the Saint Kitts and Nevis Football Association (SKNFA) has welcomed Infantino’s decision to scrap the plan, called for respect of Fifa’s institutional processes and backed the president to continue.

It said: “The SKNFA concluded by reaffirming its support for Infantino’s leadership and vision, and said it looks forward to supporting him as he completes his current constitutional mandate and continues efforts to advance football development across Fifa’s 211 Member Associations.”

Qatar 🇶🇦

Qatar was the first football association to publicly back Infantino, even though they later welcomed the decision to scrap the plan.

"While the proposal had merit, we applaud the wisdom behind prioritising unity among member associations. The Qatar Football Association fully supports President Infantino's efforts to continue growing and strengthening the game globally,” a statement read.

open image in gallery Qatar's FA has backed Infantino to continue as president ( Getty Images )

Sri Lanka 🇱🇰

Like Qatar, Sri Lanka welcomed the decision to scrap the investment plan and has since reaffirmed its support for Infantino.

"One of President Infantino's defining leadership qualities has always been his willingness to listen to the views and concerns of Member Associations. This decision is a clear reflection of his inclusive leadership style, built on dialogue, mutual respect, and a genuine commitment to serving the global football community," its statement read.

Kuwait 🇰🇼

Like others, Kuwait welcomed the decision to halt the plans but Sheikh Ahmed Yusuf Al-Sabah, the president of the Kuwait Football Association, affirmed his support for Infantino.

A statement read: “He concluded by affirming the Kuwait Football Association's confidence in the leadership of Fifa President Gianni Infantino, and its support for efforts aimed at developing the game and enhancing its opportunities for growth in a way that serves all national associations and achieves the shared interests of global football.”

Lebanon 🇱🇧

Lebanon, who granted Infantino citizenship last year, have backed the Swiss-Italian, with FA president Hashim Haidar all but echoing the same sentiments as Kuwait.

“Haidar reaffirms the Lebanese Football Association’s support for Fifa President Gianni Infantino and his confidence in the decisions he makes in the best interests of global football, as well as in his efforts and initiatives aimed at developing the game,” he said, while also asserting that Infantino’s proposal “could be re-examined ... in a away that serves the greater good of the sport and preserves its unity”.

Indonesia 🇮🇩

The president of the Indonesian FA supported Infantino’s sell-off plan and has now backed him for another term.

Hailing Fifa as a “strategic partner that is truly present” in its football development, Erick Thohir said: “This is proof of President Infantino’s vision that football development must not be centered on a single region; it must proceed worldwide.”

Philippines 🇵🇭

Philippines have also backed Infantino and backed for co-operation among confederations.

"We stand behind President Gianni Infantino's leadership, and trust that continued dialogue among all confederations and member associations will keep the global game moving forward together,” the Philippines confirmed.

Mongolia 🇲🇳

Joining the Philippines, the Mongolian Football Federation has put out a statement in support of Infantino.

Bhutan 🇧🇹

The Bhutan Football Federation has published a letter that extends its “sincere appreciation” to Infantino for scrapping the plans, hailing him for demonstrating “true leadership” by “prioritising consensus over commerce”.

“We stand united with Fifa and President Infantino in their ongoing efforts to serve the global football community,” wrote federation president Dasho Ugen Tsechup.

Morocco 🇲🇦

The location of Infantino’s crisis meeting on Wednesday, Morocco have stuck by the Swiss-Italian as one of his most loyal allies.

“What has been achieved in recent years through Fifa’s development programmes, particularly in Africa, represents an important accomplishment that must be preserved, to the benefit of all member associations,” said the Royal Moroccan Football Federation’s president Fouzi Lekjaa.

open image in gallery Infantino held his crisis meeting in Rabat, Morocco ( AP )

Egypt 🇪🇬

Similar to their north African counterpart, Egypt have maintained their endorsement of Infantino.

"The Egyptian Football Association reiterates its full trust in President Gianni Infantino's leadership and its continuous support for any initiatives that benefit Fifa member associations and the future of world football,” a statement read.

Mauritania 🇲🇷

Ahmed Yahya, the country's representative on the Fifa Council, was one of a number of African football leaders to say he was backing Infantino early on, pledging his support before Caf took its stance.

Niger 🇳🇪

Same as above, with Hamidou Djibrilla from Niger coming out quickly in support of Infantino.

Sudan 🇸🇩

Sudan’s federation joined five other Arab nations - Qatar, Lebanon, Morocco, Egypt and Mauritania - in writing a joint statement backing Infantino.

"Recognising the important role of Arab football in bringing people together and strengthening co-operation among football associations across the Arab world, we ... express our full support for Mr Gianni Infantino, president of Fifa, and reaffirm our confidence in his leadership and continued commitment to the development of football worldwide," the statement read.

"We deeply appreciate Mr Infantino’s sustained efforts to advance football globally, expand opportunities across all regions and strengthen the game’s role in bringing people and communities together. We look forward to continuing our close cooperation with him towards a stronger and more prosperous future for world ‌football, expanding opportunities and further enhancing Arab football’s contribution to ​the global game."

DR Congo 🇨🇩

DR Congo's federation (Fecofa) president Veron Mosengo-Omba, who was only elected in May, spoke out in “full support”. of Infantino. The two studied at university in Switzerland together.

Fecofa said it had "greatly benefited" from Fifa's programmes, citing investment in development and infrastructure.

Nigeria 🇳🇬

The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has largely aligned itself towards a supportive stance for Infantino's leadership, with former NFF president and deputy chairman of Fifa's Men's National Teams Competitions Committee, Amaju Pinnick, backing his initial sell-off plan.

Comoros 🇰🇲

The president of the Comoros Football Federation, Said Ali Athouman, also backed Infantino’s scheme due to the financial benefits to smaller nations.

"Our problem is how to obtain money,” he said. “Right now, we have no sponsors. So how do we compete? The richest nations can train players, have infrastructure and equipment, and it's no coincidence that they then achieve results. Most European countries don't have ​these problems.”

open image in gallery A number of African nations have fallen in line with the stance of Caf president Patrice Motsepe ( Getty )

Malawi 🇲🇼

Fleetwood Haiya, Malawi's football chief, echoed the same concerns in his support for Infantino.

He told BBC Sport: "Our government is not able to make sure that they have medical supplies in hospitals and at the same time to look at football. Malawi needs money."

Uganda 🇺🇬

The Ugandan federation are said to have echoed Malawi’s sentiments, with football officials from the federation telling BBC Sport that Fifa investment has transformed their game both on and off the pitch.

Gambia 🇬🇲

Lamin Kaba Bajo told BBC Sport that his federation not just stood by Infantino, but would do "everything within our means" to get him re-elected.

"That's my personal opinion as president of the federation, and a good number of African memberships also stand on that line. He is here to stay,” he said.

Djibouti 🇩🇯

The Djiboutian Football Federation has similarly welcomed the decision to withdraw the sell-off proposal, with president Souleiman Hassan Waberi saying the climbdown “demonstrates a firm commitment to preserving the unity, solidarity and cohesion that define the football family”.

He said in a statement: “I reaffirm my full support for Fifa President Mr Gianni Infantino and for all initiatives aimed at promoting the sustainable, transparent and inclusive development of football around the world.”

South Africa 🇿🇦

While not an official statement from the federation, South Africa’s Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture of South Africa, Gayton McKenzie, posted on X saying that Infantino had been "very good to African football".

"Africa should be cautious in joining the public lynching of Infantino,” he warned. “He has been very good to African football. We can debate his ideas but let's not forget who has been a friend to us. Many of those calling for his head want the old status quo back too."

Who is yet to take a stance?

The Oceania Football Confederation (OFC), with its 11 member associations, stopped short from pulling its support for Infantino in their statement after welcoming the scrapping of the sell-off plan, very much staying on the fence as it called for a “review”.

A statement read: "The OFC recognises the progress achieved over the last decade in advancing football development in Oceania under Fifa's leadership and encourages Fifa to use the review as an opportunity to identify and implement any changes that may be necessary."

Meanwhile, South American body Comnebol, with its 10 member associations, expressed “concern about the repeated unilateral actions taken” and welcomed the decision to withdraw the plans, affirming it will “not support any action” that “ignores or deviates” from the “democratic procedures that represent the 211 Fifa member associations”.

However, as a long-time ally of Infantino, it did endorse him to get elected for a third term earlier in the summer, with Conmebol eager for his 64-team World Cup plans to go through for the 2030 edition. They have not explicitly confirmed this stance since the scandal, though.

State of play

As things stand, Infantino has 105 member associations backing him for re-election, while 95 members are outwardly confirmed to be opposing him. This is taking into account the endorsements of confederations, which are being considered as a blanket vote from all members under that governing body unless a member has broken rank.

For example, Jordan’s opposition to Infantino means he is not included in the other 47 AFC member associations supporting Infantino, per the confederation’s endorsement, while the likes of Mexico, Grenada, and St Kitts and Nevis are all separate from the other 38 Concacaf members in opposition.

This suggests that Infantino is teetering on securing re-election, theoretically needing just one more vote. However, each nation has a vote for itself and some could go against their confederation’s stance to turn the tide against the Swiss-Italian come March’s election.

News.title: UFC star Arman Tsarukyan brawls with Conor McGregor ally over Khamzat Chimaev insult
News.content:
