UFC star Arman Tsarukyan brawled with Dillon Danis on Thursday, ahead of Friday’s wrestling match between the pair.

Tsarukyan, the UFC’s No 2 lightweight contender, will wrestle Danis at a Real American Freestyle (RAF) event in Las Vegas, one day after a press conference to promote the card.

And at that press conference, Danis sported a T-shirt showing a mock-up photo of Tsarukyan’s friend Khamzat Chimaev without a beard, along with the words: “Khamzat is my b***h.”

When Danis – a former jiu-jitsu training partner of Conor McGregor – explained as much, Tsarukyan lurched along the desk and appeared to throw a right hand at Danis.

Security stepped in to hold back both men as a mass brawl broke out, with Chimaev, a former UFC middleweight champion, later getting involved.

Chimaev pinned Danis in an RAF wrestling match in June, leading to another brawl. After Thursday’s press conference, Chimaev told Red Corner MMA: “I’m gonna be close there [on Friday night]. If something happens, we’re ready.”

Former UFC welterweight champion Robbie Lawler, who will wrestle Chimaev on Friday, reacted to Thursday’s chaos by telling MMA Fighting: “It is what it is. It’s just... I’m here to wrestle and compete. I’m just keeping my life simple, and I’m not trying to get involved in any of that nonsense.

open image in gallery Arman Tsarukyan (left) knocked out Mauricio Ruffy in stunning fashion at UFC 331 in September ( Getty )

“It’s just... You want to put your best foot forward, and a lot of kids are watching this, guys who are excited about wrestling. It’s not always about the show, and it’s not about the eyes; it’s about freaking having this sport be built and taking it to another level. And I just think we need to do a better job as competitors.”

Tsarukyan vs Danis will headline RAF 14 at the Fontainebleau hotel in Vegas, with Chimaev vs Lawler serving as the co-main event.

News.title: Tokyo Marathon winner handed six-year doping ban for submitting fake prescription
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

One of the world’s top marathon runners has been given a six-year ban from the sport after submitting a fake prescription to attempt to explain a positive drug test.

Ruti Aga, who won the Tokyo Marathon in 2019, returned a positive test for the banned substance methylprednisolone, a steroid which is used to reduce pain, after winning a half-marathon in China in March.

The Ethiopian claimed she had been prescribed the drug to treat a knee injury which she had been suffering from since April 2025.

But an investigation into her test by the Ethiopian Anti-Doping Authority revealed that the prescription she submitted came from a medical clinic which did not actually exist, and was issued to her by a family member who had “no medical registration with the relevant authority”.

Aga was charged with violating three anti-doping regulations but did not respond to the charges before the deadline, which could potentially have taken a year off her suspension if she admitted the breaches. The ban was therefore issued without a hearing.

The Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) said on Thursday that it had banned Aga for two years for the positive test and a further four years, to be served consecutively, for “tampering” with the investigation.

Aga attempted “to mislead the investigation by providing false information in an interview” in April and produced a “forged/manipulated document” in May, according to the AIU’s press release on the case.

The 32-year-old was ranked 11th in the world at the time of testing positive and as well as claiming the Tokyo title in 2019 had four top-three finishes at World Marathon Majors.

The AIU’s chief executive, Brett Clothier, said: “Protecting clean competition takes resources, but this case sends a clear message: attempts to cheat will be exposed”.

News.title: Europe’s record-breaking summer heat estimated to have killed 50,000 people
News.content:
More than 50,000 people are estimated to have died across Europe as a result of this summer’s record-breaking heatwaves, according to research.

In the UK alone, researchers estimate there were 4,354 excess deaths this summer.

The number of excess deaths across Europe is double the number recorded in 2025 and it is also far higher than the previous record of 29,000 deaths. This was recorded in 2022 when the continent also endured exceptionally high temperatures, with the mercury hitting 40 degrees celsius for the first time in the UK.

According to the Met Office the UK saw its hottest ever summer this year with five widespread heatwaves and 40 days where the temperature was above 30 degrees celsius. Mainland Europe experienced its third hottest summer, with temperatures particularly high in the south and west.

Researchers from Imperial College, London and the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) looked at 854 urban areas in 30 countries across Europe. Using temperature records and modelling based on the relationship between heat and mortality they estimated the number of heat-related deaths that occurred between June and August.

They said findings from previous years’ excess heat mortality modelling matched official figures released later by national health authorities.

Because the study only looked at urban areas – making up 40 per cent of the population of the countries studied – researchers believe the number of deaths is likely to be an underestimate.

According to the study, published in Nature Health, southern and western Europe were hardest hit. Italy experienced the highest number of excess deaths (13,303), followed by France (7,268), Spain (6,824), Germany (6,340) then the UK.

There were an estimated 22,000 deaths among those aged 85 and over but researchers pointed out that an estimated 6,000 people under the age of 65 are also likely to have died as a result of the heat.

Around a third of the deaths took place in late June, when average temperatures across Europe were more than 5°C above what would be expected during this time of year. Researchers say in early summer people were less likely to have acclimatised to the sweltering weather. This period was marked by both extremely high humidity and unusually high night-time temperatures, making it difficult for people to cool down.

Researchers also estimated that more than two thirds of the total excess deaths were attributable to climate change. Across the continent as a whole Europe was an average 2.9°C higher than would have been expected. However, in some places temperatures were as much as 12°C higher.

Dr Clair Barnes, extreme weather and climate change researcher at Imperial College, said extreme heat was having a severe impact on public health.

“It is yet another reminder both of the imperative of rolling out targeted interventions to protect those who are most vulnerable to this increasingly extreme heat, and of the growing need to rapidly transition away from fossil fuels to slow the pace of change and limit future warming.”

Dr Pierre Masselot, assistant professor of statistics and epidemiology at LSHTM and one of the study’s authors, said “climate change is everybody’s problem”.

“It is not just hot regions that are suffering any more with some parts of Western and Northern Europe experiencing extreme heat and historically high health burden. And the whole population is affected, as shown by the significant death toll among younger age groups.

“It is becoming increasingly clear our cities are poorly adapted to rising heat, and it is critical we improve our efforts towards adaptation. This means cooling the cities through more green spaces and less pollution, and providing health care for affected populations.”

News.title: Bournemouth thrash Milan to seal greatest win in club’s history
News.content:
Milan could not even point to being down to 10 men for the last hour as mitigation; long before, Bournemouth had treated the Rossoneri with contempt. When Ruben Amorim’s side trudged off, soaked and silenced, they had not mustered a single shot on target.

Few nights have better encapsulated the Premier League’s power. Bournemouth have never finished higher than last season’s sixth in the top flight of English football; AC Milan have won seven European Cups. But the Premier League’s financial clout is such that, each season, the bottom club earns more than the champions of Serie A.

The Premier League’s shared riches, allied to years of astute recruitment and management, have underpinned the Bournemouth’s ascent. Even Andoni Iraola’s departure has not stalled the progress at the Vitality Stadium; Marco Rose has relished the new European adventure.

Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz had already been toppled in Bournemouth’s first two European games. Now, Bournemouth have won their first three matches in Europe. Despite middling Premier League form, Rose’s ambitions will extend far beyond securing a berth in the knockout stages of the Europa League. On this evidence, Bournemouth are legitimate contenders to win the competition, and earn a berth in next season’s Champions League.

“It’s a special night for the club,” Ryan Christie, Bournemouth captain, said. “It’s mega – in terms of the story of the club, it’s ridiculous.”

Evanilson, perhaps, was Bournemouth’s standout player against AC Milan, combining intricate linkup play with a constant threat in front of goal. Centre-back Antonio Silva, controlling play from deep while marauding forward, also possessed a calmness that any of Milan’s beleaguered team lacked.

His side’s fate swiftly sealed, Amorim did not bother to summon Luka Modric or Christian Pulisic. Bournemouth’s own bench showed the depth that the club now possesses. Rayan showed off his trickery and directness; Adli – a substitute for substitute Alex Toth, who suffered a hamstring injury – then ensured that Bournemouth secured the margin of victory that their dominance deserved.

News.title: Harry Brook hits historic double century – but England still lose to Sri Lanka
News.content:
Good morning and welcome to the fourth match of the autumn tri-series in Pakistan. After two wins for the hosts, the two touring sides face each other for the first time in Rawalpindi, the last match here before the circus leaves for Lahore. England and Sri Lanka played each other only last month in this format, England winning at Chester-le-Street and the Oval by a distance, those victories sandwiching a narrow defeat at Headingley where, if you remember, Harry Brook’s side were cruising until Jos Buttler ripped his left hamstring. He did eventually come back out to bat on one leg as his rattled team-mates flapped and fell to Asitha Fernando, Dilshan Madushanka and Eshan Malinga.

On Tuesday against Pakistan, England again were flying with both ball and bat but they let the middle-order rebuild, losing control of the rate. Their two most experienced white-ball bowlers, Adil Rashid, who looked rusty after breaking his hand in August, and Sam Curran, who missed the end of August and all of September following groin surgery, went for 6.87 and eight runs an over respectively. Then, after a promising opening partnership, Ben Duckett top-edged a pull, Tom Banton flicked straight to midwicket and Will Jacks later fell in identical fashion when well-set to marshal the chase. Arafat Minhas ended up with six for 40, bowling Harry Brook with a beauty, and there will be more trial by spin today.

Although there was some talk of England failing in end-of-days Bazball fashion, it most reminded me of the teething troubles of Eoin Morgan’s side in 2015 and 2016 when they were experimenting with players, viz this Rose Bowl collapse. We have to acknowledge that Joe Root, the best player of spin, was undone by one that kept low from Naseem Shah and both Brook and Jordan Cox lost their wickets to very good deliveries from Arafat, a bowler, on a feast day. Dunith Welllalage will return to try to replicate his line of attack today but he is a bowler that England know well. He has had his days against them but they have also given him some tap in the past.

News.title: Health authorities race to investigate first human death linked to Shamonda virus
News.content:
A French man has become the first person to contract Shamonda virus, a disease previously only found in animals and spread through midges.

The patient, who had a weakened immune system, has since died, according to the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC).

Shamonda virus was first identified in Nigeria in the 1960s and has this year been detected in farm animals all across Europe.

It was confirmed to have spread to the British Isles in September, after being found in a cattle herd on the island of Jersey. There have also been cases in Ireland.

The French patient, who was immunocompromised, died earlier this month while infected with the virus, but it is unclear if the infection contributed to his death, the ECDC said in a statement.

Investigations into whether the virus caused or contributed to the patient’s death and how the infection was acquired are ongoing.

Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the director of the World Health Organization (WHO) said in a statement on X that he was “in contact with French authorities, who are collecting information to better understand the source of infection.”

He added the patient was “immunocompromised, which made them more vulnerable to infection and severe disease.”

There was “no health risk to the general public identified at this time”, the French health and agriculture ministries said in a joint statement.

Dr Ben Brennan, Group Leader and Senior Lecturer, MRC-University of Glasgow Centre for Virus Research, University of Glasgow, said: “This is an important scientific finding, as it is the first reported human infection with Shamonda virus [..] at present, there is no evidence that Shamonda virus causes widespread human disease, although further investigation is needed to understand its ability to infect people.”

In animals, Shamonda virus attacks the central nervous system and can lead to severe inflammation and haemorrhage. It can also lead to miscarriages.

Affected horses have been reported to exhibit seizures, lethargy, fever, muscle twitching, and difficulty walking.

Authorities are also still trying to ascertain whether the man himself was infected by a biting midge – the route of transmission between animals – or if he could have been infected by close contact with livestock.

It is thought he was infected in eastern France, where the virus had been circulating in midges and animals earlier in the year.

“Despite decades of circulation of the Shamonda virus in Africa and Asia, no human cases had been documented until now. This is therefore an exceptional case occurring in a severely immunocompromised patient,” French health authorities said in a statement.

The UK Plant and Health Agency said some of the neurological signs of the disease in horses resemble West Nile fever, human cases of which reached a record high on mainland Europe this year.

News.title: What happens when you get malaria during pregnancy?
News.content:
Huge strides have been made in recent years in combating malaria but one group is more at risk than ever before: pregnant women.

They are uniquely vulnerable to the disease and because sub-Saharan Africa shoulders the burden of global cases the continent’s rapidly growing population means far more women are exposed today than at the turn of the millennium.

According to a recent study, 52 million pregnant women in Africa face the threat of malaria each year, up from 37 million in 2000.

And the toll is heavy: malaria in pregnancy kills at least 10,000 mothers and 210,000 infants every year.

Malaria in pregnancy is uniquely dangerous, and the disease acts very differently to how it does in someone who is not pregnant.

“Pregnant women are one of the most vulnerable groups to malaria, it can lead to severe anaemia, immune suppression, and in the worst cases, mortality,” Lottie Renwick, global campaign director at Malaria No More UK told The Telegraph.

Malaria parasites infect and feed on red blood cells, dividing and multiplying in the bloodstream. This makes them easily detectable through a simple blood test, which allows life-saving treatment to be administered quickly.

But in pregnancy, the parasites are notoriously evasive.

Instead of floating in the bloodstream, they colonise in the placenta – the organ that feeds and sustains the baby.

News.title: Harry Kane proves there is only one Ballon d’Or winner
News.content:
After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

News.title: Aston Villa 2.0 are making mockery of the early-season doom merchants

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are currently level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

He said: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”

What a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Just a week after their biggest European win, the 6-0 destruction of Fenerbahce, expectations were understandably high. Before kick-off a huge tifo was unfurled in the Holte End with the words: “We’ve conquered before. We’re prepared for more.”

Sports.title: Antonio Conte breaks silence on Man Utd job links with long statement amid pressure on Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Next

ANTONIO CONTE has dismissed speculation over his future amid links to the Manchester United job and says he will “take time” before deciding on his next role.

The fiery Italian has been tipped to succeed under-fire Michael Carrick at Old Trafford amid United’s rotten run of results.

United were thrashed 4-1 by Como in the Champions League this week, extending their winless streak to seven games.



Carrick hasn’t picked up a win since beating Ipswich 5-2 in August and could come serious pressure ahead of crucial games against Bournemouth and Chelsea.



Former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Conte has emerged as a standout contender to take over at United should they decide to axe Carrick.

But the Premier League and five-time Serie A winner shot down rumours he could take over a club in the near future following his exit from Napoli in June.

Conte said: “Following recent media reports in Italy and abroad, I feel it is appropriate to clarify my position.



“My name has been linked with numerous clubs, but there are currently no negotiations at an advanced stage.

“Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management.

“It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right.

“I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my ‘strong personality’.



“These reports are unfounded, as there is currently no concrete basis for such assessments.

“Should a concrete opportunity arise, that will be the time to hold discussions with the club concerned and jointly consider the terms of a potential agreement, with due regard for both parties’ needs and the qualities and approach that define my work as manager.

“Until then, any assumptions about my demands and my professional future remain speculation and cannot be treated as fact.”

Sports.title: Man Utd make decision on Bruno Fernandes punishment after bombshell Carrick criticism
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED will not punish Bruno Fernandes or strip him of the captaincy following his explosive criticism of Michael Carrick.

The Red Devils have decided their skipper will keep the armband despite disappointment inside Old Trafford over his post-match comments following Wednesday’s humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como.



Fernandes openly questioned United’s tactical approach in Italy, taking issue with the coaching staff’s decision not to press Como man-to-man.

Carrick hit back afterwards by insisting: “If you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.”



But United chiefs are understood to feel Fernandes was expressing understandable anger in the immediate aftermath of one of the club’s worst European nights.

United legend Gary Pallister admitted Fernandes’ performance and demeanour against Como were difficult to watch.

Speaking exclusively to Paddy Power, he said: “His body language didn’t look great in the game – he was throwing his hands up in the air.”

Pallister added: “It’s the last thing Michael Carrick needs, his captain coming out and questioning things.

And the former United centre-back believes Fernandes’ comments have only created another unwanted headache.

The 61-year-old said: “Bruno saying what he said doesn’t do anybody any favours – himself, the club, the players or the manager. It leaves the club putting out fires again.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Pallister also dismissed the idea that former Chelsea boss Antonio Conte would provide an easy solution if United did decide to replace Carrick.

He said: “Conte is high maintenance and would probably play a back five, and we’ve already been down that route with Ruben Amorim.

United are winless in seven games in all competitions and currently sit 13th in the Premier League and 21st in the Champions League standings.

But while Carrick’s position is increasingly uncertain, Fernandes has received the club’s backing to continue as captain – with no punishment coming his way over his extraordinary Como interview.

Sports.title: Bournemouth assets top charts in Gameweek 7 ahead of favourable fixture run
Sports.content:
Next

FOR fans of a certain age, Bournemouth 3 Milan 0 is a scoreline that takes some time to compute.

The Cherries made light work of the Italian giants in the Europa League on Thursday, aided Mike Maignan’s moment of madness, leaving Dream Team managers much to ponder ahead of the Gameweek 8 deadline.

Evanilson (£3.8m) outperformed all other forwards in Gameweek 7 with a hefty 22-point haul.



The Brazilian assisted his side’s opening goal against Sunderland and then doubled the lead in the second half with a moment of magic as he rounded Robin Roefs (£2.8m) with a composed step-over.



When all was said and done, he took the Black Cats for 14 points.

Against Milan, he notched another eight points via a fantasy assist that occurred when his headed effort was deflected wide by Koni de Winter’s hand, resulting in a penalty converted by Justin Kluivert (£3.7m).

Evanilson also made three tackles, created a big chance and registered a shot on target as the hosts outclassed Ruben Amorim’s men at the Vitality Stadium.



Bournemouth’s No9 leads the way for assists in his position with five in all competitions.

Add in three goals (across the last three Gameweeks) and it’s no wonder he’s up to third in the rankings among strikers with 69 points to his name — Nicolas Jackson (£4m), Charalampos Kostoulas (£3.1m) and Joao Pedro (£5.8m) are among those overtaken this past week.

Evanilson also ranks first in his position for tackles and big chances created, evidence of an impressive all-round game.

His current ownership of 4.1% suddenly looks scandalously low.



Evanilson was not the only Bournemouth player to come out on top in their position in Gameweek 7.

James Hill (£3.1m) topped the defensive charts with a 19-point return.

Marco Rose’s men kept clean sheets in both fixtures but the 24-year-old edged out team-mates Adrien Truffert (£3.3m) and Antonio Silva (£3.4m) by making six tackles, picking up a bonus point, and registering a shot on target.

Bournemouth’s only clean sheet in their first eight games came against Lincoln in the Carabao Cup but since they were thrashed 5-1 by Chelsea at the start of Gameweek 6, they’ve shut out Sturm Graz, Sunderland and Milan in consecutive fixtures.



If Hill and company have turned a corner then it’s well timed.

Bournemouth’s upcoming fixtures appear relatively favourable and Europa League commitments ensure plenty of point-scoring opportunities.

And we haven’t even discussed midfield, where Marcus Tavernier (£3.3m) has racked up 71 points at an average of 6.5 per game.



The 27-year-old has scored five goals, a tally bettered by only Rayan Cherki (£5.4m) among midfielders, and ranks sixth in his position after a 19-point haul in Gameweek 7.

Tavernier is the most popular Bournemouth asset but even his ownership of 6.2% is modest.

But three wins from three in the Europa League and some favourable match-ups to come means Hill, Tavernier and Evanilson all deserve sincere consideration.

Sports.title: European giants snub SHOWERS after Champions League clash over fears of deadly bacteria in stadium water
Sports.content:
Next

BORUSSIA DORTMUND stars refused to shower at the stadium after their Champions League clash over fears of potentially deadly bacteria in the water system.

The German giants instead raced back to their team hotel to wash off after securing a narrow 2-1 victory over Azerbaijani champions FK Sabah on Tuesday night.



That decision was reportedly driven by concerns over Legionella bacteria, which can grow in water systems when water is left unused for long periods.

The bacteria can cause Legionnaires’ disease – a potentially serious lung infection when contaminated water droplets are inhaled.



Legionella can multiply in certain water systems, particularly where water is stagnant or not used regularly.

Borussia Dortmund‘s players were instructed not to use the stadium showers, with head coach Niko Kovac revealing the squad had also avoided them following training the previous day.

The Croatian boss said: “We didn’t shower after training yesterday either, and now we’re heading straight back to the hotel. We were told not to shower here.”

The players, including two-goal hero Serhou Guirassy, were seen leaving the Olympic Stadium in Baku in their training gear and heading straight onto the team bus.

The swift exit raised eyebrows, particularly given the stadium was completed in 2015 and hosted matches during Euro 2020.

But Dortmund sporting director Ole Book offered a more diplomatic explanation when asked about the decision.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He said: “I think the showers at the hotel were a bit more inviting. So we’re making sure the players get there quickly.

“More inviting — you can probably use your imagination a little.

He then described the stadium’s facilities as “not quite so nice.”



Dortmund, who won the Champions League in 1997, were finalists just two years ago when they lost 2-0 to Real Madrid at Wembley.

Kovac’s side have started this season well, currently second in the Bundesliga – behind Bayern Munich on goal difference.

Dortmund face Eintracht Frankfurt at home tomorrow before travelling to the Allianz Arena next weekend for a mouthwatering showdown with Bayern.

Sports.title: Eddie Howe's passionate dressing room speech about Man Utd resurfaces as he's eyed for job
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe's passionate dressing room speech about Man Utd resurfaces as he's eyed for job

Manchester United are reportedly weighing up Eddie Howe as a potential replacement for Michael Carrick, with the ex-Newcastle boss having previously stung the Red Devils

View Image Eddie Howe gave an inspired speech as Newcastle boss before guiding the team to victory over Manchester United (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Eddie Howe isn't exactly famed for his displays of emotion, but he let it all out as he inspired Newcastle to victory over Manchester United in 2023. Howe has a record of beating United and is now being touted as a potential replacement for Michael Carrick.

‌



‌



After five years in the north-east, Howe parted ways with the Magpies and was replaced by Matthias Jaissle over the summer. However, he could be in line for a Premier League comeback in the event United get rid of the struggling Carrick.

‌



Howe, 48, has won just eight of his 21 meetings with United, though six of those wins came over the course of his last eight encounters as Newcastle boss. The Magpies lost the EFL Cup final to United in February 2023 before the teams reconvened several months later, when Howe used Erik ten Hag's own words against him to inspire his troops to victory.

‌



"My final message today: I'm going to do something I rarely do," said Howe in a clip from Amazon Prime Video's 'We Are Newcastle United' docuseries. "But I felt upon hearing the comments, I needed to relay it to you. So comments from their [United's] manager.

"'They have the lowest ball-in-play time in the league and are quite successful at slowing the game down. It's an annoying team to play against, so we have to find a way to play against them. So it's up to us that we get the speed in the game and we are also dependent on the refereeing as well'.

Man Utd chiefs SPLIT on Michael Carrick replacement as player row spills into boardroom READ MORE :

‌



"Why am I telling you that? If they want a quick game coming here, let's f*****g give it to them. Let's blow them away with our running, let's be intense in every action that we do, let's make it a quick game. Let's go."

Newcastle went on to beat United 2-0 that day. Late goals from Joe Willock and Callum Wilson proved the difference, which also started a streak of three consecutive Newcastle wins in their head-to-head rivalry.

‌



Warning: Explicit language

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Howe holds a reputation as being mild-mannered in his approach and rarely letting his emotions get the better of him on the touchline. United incumbent Carrick might be described as similarly soft-tempered, not that it has granted much fortune at Old Trafford of late.

A 4-1 demolition at the hands of Como in the Champions League on Tuesday has stretched United's winless run to seven games. That's sparked more intense talk of Carrick being replaced in the near future, with Howe among the available candidates to take the job.

‌



While it's hardly reaching the levels of Sir Alex Ferguson's infamous hairdryer treatment, Howe's speech showed a certain knack for knowing what to say and how to say it. On the other hand, one might argue Newcastle were simply the better team during that period.

A change of leader looks all but inevitable for United if the current malaise in results persists. And some fans may find it comforting to see Howe in a more impassioned light amid rumours he's in the running to take over if that's the case.

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim reminded of Man Utd misery after cock-up in AC Milan's defeat at Bournemouth
Sports.content:
Ruben Amorim reminded of Man Utd misery after cock-up in AC Milan's defeat at Bournemouth

Former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim endured a nightmare return to English football on Thursday night as his AC Milan side were beaten at Bournemouth

View 2 Images Amorim endured a chastening return to English football (Image: UEFA via Getty Images)

Ruben Amorim was given a stark reminder of his difficult time in charge of Manchester United when he returned to English football on Thursday night.

‌



‌



Amorim is now manager of European giants AC Milan who travelled to Bournemouth in the Europa League. But it was more misery for Amorim on British shores as the San Siro juggernauts slipped to a humbling 3-0 defeat.

‌



And Portuguese boss Amorim had an embarrassing moment of his own in the first half.

‌



After Milan goalkeeper Mike Maignan was sent off for a double-handed push into the face of Cherries star Tyler Adams, Amorim inexplicably tried to replace him without substituting an outfield player.

Make sure you don't miss the best football coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Marcus Tavernier scored from the spot to put Bournemouth 2-0 up after Justin Kluivert had already given the hosts the lead. Amine Adli curled in a free-kick in the second half to round off the scoring.

And Bournemouth fans were quick to remind Amorim of his previous results against the Cherries as the game drew to a close, chanting: "Ruben Amorim, it's happened again!"

‌



Amorim took on Bournemouth twice as United boss, failing to win on each occasion. The Red Devils were beaten 3-0 at Old Trafford in December 2024, before playing out a wind 4-4 draw at the same venue 12 months later.

Amorim has had an up-and-down start to life in the San Siro dugout, sitting fourth in Serie A but 24th in the Europa League standings.

‌



He has stuck by his much-derided three-at-the-back system which ultimately saw his downfall at United. Despite being steadfast in his belief, Amorim hinted earlier this season he would be willing to adapt.

View 2 Images Amorim was sacked by Manchester United in January (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

‌



"I change all the time, we need to start with a base, we have two months of work," he said following a 2-0 defeat by Benfica.

"We lost tonight, but we will find the solutions to adapt to these games, because we need to create an idea, but we also need to win, so of course we can adapt."

‌



Amorim was sacked in January after a turbulent 14-month tenure with United sixth in the table following a £250million summer outlay on signings.

He was replaced by Michael Carrick who led United back to the Champions League, but is now under huge pressure himself having won just two of 11 games in all competitions so far this season.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta told to make risky change as he delivers Bukayo Saka update
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta told to make risky change as he delivers Bukayo Saka update

Mikel Arteta has been told to make a significant change to his Arsenal starting XI

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta has been advised to change his formation (Image: Getty )

Arsenal return to Premier League action this Saturday afternoon when they face Everton at home. The Gunners will be hoping to secure all three points as they look to close the gap on league leaders Manchester City.

‌



‌



Mikel Arteta’s side are coming off the back of a tough 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest last weekend, having made hard work of their recent league encounters. That was followed by an impressive display away at Bayern Munich in the Champions League in midweek, where the English and German champions had to settle for a point apiece.

‌



But, despite coming away from the game with plenty of positives, Arteta had to deal with a fresh injury blow and a new dilemma regarding how to get the best out of Viktor Gyokeres, who set up Declan Rice’s late equaliser after coming on as a substitute.

‌



Now, Mirror Football brings you two of the latest stories involving the north London club.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Mikel Arteta provides worrying Bukayo Saka update after Arsenal star forced off READ MORE :

Arsenal leave it late vs Bayern Munich but Mikel Arteta dealt huge injury blow READ MORE :

Arteta told to make change

Former Arsenal midfielder Anders Limpar has suggested that Arteta should change his formation if he wants to get the best out of Gyokeres. The Spaniard usually deploys a single striker in a 4-3-3 or 4-2-3-1 formation in possession, very rarely fielding two strikers at the same time unless his side are in urgent need of a goal.

‌



Gyokeres, who arrived in the summer of 2025, scored 21 goals for the Gunners last season. But the Swede often looked isolated and ineffective up top on his own, with his limitations in the lone striker role seeing him fall behind Kai Havertz in the pecking order this term.

But Gyokeres' compatriot Limpar, who mentored him during his formative years at Brommapojkarna in Sweden, has encouraged the Arsenal boss to deploy a two-striker formation to make the most out of his attacking options. Gyokeres usually plays alongside Liverpool’s Alexander Isak for his country and has scored 10 goals in 11 international games this year.

‌



View 3 Images Viktor Gyokeres has had a tough start to the season (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

"When I see Viktor playing for Sweden, he is much better because he’s playing with two up front, and he was brought up in the Swedish system, playing with two forwards," the former Gunners winger told Betarades. "Playing up front on his own is hard for him because it’s not his game to be a target player.

‌



"He is good going forward, chasing the ball, and he’s a threat on counterattacks, so he needs a player who is a really good target so he can play off them. At the moment, you can see that he’s struggling a little bit when it comes to receiving the ball, to pass the ball around.

"It might be nerves, or that he’s not comfortable coming off the bench. But you should never ever go out in the press saying that you want to leave or that you want to play every game.

‌



"That’s not good for Arteta, that’s not good for him, and that’s not good for the club. I’m pretty sure that all the Arsenal players are squad players."

Limpar added: "If you ask me if I want him to play, then yes, I think he should play as a starter. I think he should be a starter, especially now when Kai has struggled a little bit in the last couple of games, but we have to wait and see who is playing the next game."

‌



Bukayo Saka injury update

View 3 Images Bukayo Saka sustained an injury against Bayern (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

Arteta provided an update on Bukayo Saka after Wednesday night’s game, expressing concern over the severity of his recent injury. The Gunners talisman was taken off after just nine minutes against Bayern, having gone to ground holding his leg in discomfort after playing a pass.

‌



He was replaced by Eberechi Eze, who scored just 15 minutes later. But Arsenal fans will be disheartened by the immediate prognosis for the 25-year-old, revealed by Arteta after the match.

"[The medical staff] are a bit concerned," Arteta told TNT Sports. "A player that has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news. But we have to wait and see. It does not look good at all. It's his quad."

Article continues below

Saka started all seven of Arsenal's Premier League fixtures this season but has suffered several injury absences over the past two years. He missed 15 matches for Arsenal and England last season with various injury issues. In 2024/25, Saka missed 25 games across a total period of more than three months due to a hamstring injury.

Sports.title: Why divisive Julian Nagelsmann would be a huge gamble for Man Utd after Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
There was a time when Julian Nagelsmann was the hottest managerial property in world football. Those times are long gone.

Nagelsmann has come into contention for the Manchester United job during a time when his star has faded. That in itself says something about United's current situation, where Michael Carrick is clinging onto his job after a shambolic performance in Como.

Nagelsmann is still only 39 years old, but he is already on the other side of stints in two dream jobs: Bayern Munich and Germany. He was surprisingly sacked from the first job amid plenty of discontent in the dressing room. He resigned from the latter after a historic defeat by Paraguay at the World Cup.

Now he could be thrust into another spotlight and given a job of epic proportions. Well, that is if United's director of recruitment Christopher Vivell gets his way. Vivell is reportedly at odds with director of football Jason Wilcox over the way forward if Carrick doesn't last. Wilcox is above Vivell in the chain of command at Old Trafford, so it could be that someone with Premier League experience - Eddie Howe, Antonio Conte or Fabian Hurzeler are also on the shortlist - gets the job ahead of him.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Everything Julian Nagelsmann has said about Man Utd as he makes stance clear READ MORE :

Man Utd chiefs SPLIT on Michael Carrick replacement as player row spills into boardroom READ MORE :

If United do turn to Nagelsmann then it will be a bold choice. Carrick was the unifying choice: an ex-United player with a great deal of goodwill in the bank after a strong interim period. Nagelsmann would undoubtedly be divisive.

Like many managers, Nagelsmann is a football obsessive. And like many German coaches, he was heavily influenced by Ralf Rangnick, a man who doesn't have the best reputation at Old Trafford.

But it is Nagelsmann's approach to management which would ruffle feathers at United. If the club chiefs were to ask Matthijs de Ligt about his time at Bayern during their due diligence they would discover a fairly compelling reason against the appointment.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 3 Images Matthijs de Ligt worked under Julian Nagelsmann at Bayern Munich (Image: INA FASSBENDER / AFP via Getty Images)

Nagelsmann's time at Bayern Munich brought a Bundesliga title, yet that is considered the bare minimum in Bavaria. His average of 2.31 points per game is comparable to those who came before him. But it was the way he went about the job which resulted in his downfall.

"Thirty per cent of coaching is tactics, 70 per cent social competence,” Nagelsmann has said of his approach. "Every player is motivated by different things and needs to be addressed accordingly."

‌



The problem is how a manager who is only slightly older than many of his players goes about motivating his players. "I try to explain things thoroughly and keep people informed," he said while Germany boss. "Sometimes I’m not as successful as I’d like to be, and sometimes I am."

View 3 Images Julian Nagelsmann's time at Bayern Munich raises concerns for Manchester United (Image: Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images)

After being sacked by Bayern in March 2023, The Athletic laid bare the extent of the issues in a dressing room packed full of egos. We already knew the stir Nagelsmann's decision to axe goalkeeper coach and Manuel Neuer ally Toni Tapalovic had made, but that was just the tip of the iceberg.

Players had been confused by Nagelsmann's ever-evolving and highly-demanding tactics. They were irritated by his personal intensity and tendency to micro-manage. They were annoyed to be constantly moved in and out of the starting line-up, often with little explanation. He struggled to connect with his players - and that cost him.

‌



That Bayern squad was packed full of elite and experienced players; United's is listless and way short of such quality. His complex methods don't look well suited to a mid-season rescue mission.

Sports.title: Antonio Conte's two demands to take Man Utd job emerge after giving green light
Sports.content:
Antonio Conte's two demands to take Man Utd job emerge after giving green light

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick is under pressure to deliver results and the former Chelsea and Tottenham manager Antonio Conte has been linked with the role

View 2 Images Antonio Conte has been linked with the managerial position at Manchester United

Antonio Conte will make two demands to the Manchester United hierarchy if he is to take over from Michael Carrick. The former Chelsea, Tottenham and Napoli boss has been repeatedly linked with a move to Old Trafford given the club's recent struggles.

‌



‌



Carrick is under increased pressure to deliver results having won just two of their opening 11 games so far this season. The Red Devils boss is set face the music on Friday at his press conference before the clash with Bournemouth this weekend.

‌



As things stand, Carrick is expected to take control of the clash with the Cherries, though reports claim the club have contacted prospective replacements if they decide to part company with the 45-year-old. Reports in Italy claim United have already held talks with Conte about replacing Carrick in the aftermath of the 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League.

‌



It's claimed talks with Conte continued on Wednesday night, with the Italian already expressing a desire to United chiefs to return to the Premier League, but had two clear conditions.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Accoring to La Repubblica, Conte has demanded full control over transfer activity, along with the authority to pick his own backroom staff. The report claims Conte wants the final say on how he builds his squad, identifying players who fit his tactical set-up.

It's claimed that United's hierarchy are currently deciding whether or not to accept these demands, with results set to decide whether or not they part company with Carrick. United reportedly have a shortlist of managers drawn up, with Conte among the names on that list, though Jason Wilcox and Christopher Vivell reportedly don't agree on who should replace Carrick.

‌



The latter of the duo is said to favour Julian Nagelsmann, while Wilcox wants a Premier League proven manager, with Eddie Howe, Fabian Hurzeler, Unai Emery and Conte on his shortlist.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is under pressure at Man Utd (Image: PIERO CRUCIATTI/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



The current United boss says he hasn't given his future any thought despite the club's disappointing run of form, and made his feelings clear about the terrible display in Como.

Speaking after the defeat, Carrick said: "Listen, I've not given my own position any thought. [My thoughts are] for the supporters – I was one of them watching that and I wasn't happy at all."

‌



"It's not about me right now and my feelings in that regard. It's more of as a team and as a football club, what we want to look like, what we should look like.

"And as I said, the results can come and go at times, but you got to do it in a certain way. And that wasn't it."

Sports.title: Man Utd at civil war and Bruno Fernandes criticism leaves Michael Carrick with no way back
Sports.content:
It now feels like a question of when and not if for Michael Carrick.

Manchester United’s humiliating defeat at Como in the Champions League has only sharpened the focus on a growing crisis at Old Trafford which has left Carrick on the brink. The worst start to a league season since 1986 and United crashed out of the Carabao Cup at the first hurdle.

Incredibly, they are closer to the Premier League relegation zone than the top four. But, undoubtedly, the most damaging part of this week might actually be Bruno Fernandes openly questioning the manager and his tactics.

Sadly, you know the game is up when the dressing room begins to turn and no one should underestimate the power and impact of Fernandes’ words after that Como game. That felt like a new low for Carrick even in such a disappointing season where they have now gone six games without a win.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Fernandes openly questioned Carrick’s tactics after the defeat at Como. “It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, but sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confidence,” he said.

When asked if Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes also told TNT Sports: “That's on the manager and staff to see it, not me.”

‌



There is an old saying in football that when a manager loses the fans you are a dead man walking. Maybe that explains why Carrick, at the end of the Como game, went over to the travelling fans before anyone else to effectively apologise for the lame performance and surrender.

But, meanwhile, Carrick is clearly in danger of losing the players anyway which is generally the tipping point for any manager. Without the players fighting for you on the pitch, the manager stands no chance of getting a performance from the players.

It was Erik ten Hag who this week talked to The Athletic about “player power” and a “toxic” environment at Old Trafford during his time in charge.

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes called out Michael Carrick's tactics (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

‌



Dutchman Ten Hag said he had to be the bad cop. Ruben Amorim came in and was probably too honest. Carrick clearly got brilliant results and performances from the players last season to lift the club from mediocrity and into the Champions League places.

Carrick got the players onside but that approach will only work for so long. Being a nice guy in football is probably seen as a sign of weakness and that makes you the No.1 target when you do not get results.

The most obvious thing about United this season has been a lack of intensity, a lack of sharpness and direction. The recruitment has been poor but the opening day defeat at Hull City was more about the team’s lack of fitness. That still looks well below par.

United have not improved and now you have criticism coming from all angles. Last week it was Lisandro Martinez taking aim at the club’s hierarchy and poor recruitment.

‌



Why did they sign Youri Tielemans? He is a good player, but what was the plan? He does not fit into their system. So, why sign him? That’s United’s transfer policy to a tee.

And what on earth did those signings make of those Martinez remarks? That was the first sign of civil war.

Should Manchester United sack Michael Carrick? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick apologised to Manchester United's fans (Image: PIERO CRUCIATTI/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



This week, we have the captain speaking out against the manager. That feels like the point of no return. There is surely no way back for the United manager.

United should, in hindsight, have been bold in the summer and thanked Carrick for steering the club back into the top four and then looked to hire an elite, experienced manager.

Instead, they stuck with Carrick and are now stuck back in a cycle which just mirrors what happened with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. An upturn in results as the dressing room like him, they turn things around - and then run out of steam.

That is what happened with Carrick. It’s rinse and repeat. Carrick has run out of credit with the players. Frankly, after a 4-1 defeat, one of the worst defeats in the club’s proud European history, it would have been no surprise if they had pulled the trigger.

‌



Now it just feels like Carrick is treading water. He stumbles on until Bournemouth on Sunday. He may get until the next international break. Then it will be the next cab off the rank from the ranks of Julian Nagelsmann, Antonio Conte or Eddie Howe.

Conte would get results but present a scorched earth policy. Howe inherited a bigger mess at Newcastle but did a great job. He is free, available and would be keen. But even Howe can only succeed if the structure above is right. And at United, that is the bigger problem.

Sports.title: NFL to the Moon? ‘Everything an option’ as league debuts in Paris
Sports.content:
NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell joked he wouldn’t rule out the moon as he emphasised the league’s commitment to global expansion ahead of its Paris debut this weekend.

In layman's terms, the league has no plans to pump the brakes on its globe-trotting ventures amid a season in which a record nine international games will be played.

France enters the fold as one of three new territories for 2026 alongside Melbourne and Rio de Janeiro when New Orleans Saints face Pittsburgh Steelers at Stade de France on Sunday, live on Sky Sports NFL.

It is the newest extension to a format mirroring Formula 1's reach.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jacksonville Jaguars beat Philadelphia Eagles in London - and the last few minutes did not disappoint!

"It could lead to something else," Goodell told Sky Sports.

"Formula One actually helped me understand. I went to a race in Montreal and was looking at how they're racing, they race every week or two and have a lot of travel, a lot of ability, but also a lot of challenges. It's roughly 23 races, several of those already in the States.

"If we can get to 16 [international games] we're fairly close, it's the same number of markets we're reaching on a global basis.

"At some point we really have to think about it. Would we create an international franchise? Would we create a division? We want to think about that."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jacksonville Jaguars beat Philadelphia Eagles in London - and the last few minutes did not disappoint!

The NFL pushed its boundaries further than ever earlier this season by staging its first game in Australia as San Francisco 49ers beat Los Angeles Rams at the iconic MCG in front of 100,000 fans.

It had the feel of the league's boldest international move yet, though would also prove divisive amid players and coaches involved.

Goodell, though, says the league remains intent on establishing a long-term presence down under. Could the league possibly venture any further?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cam Little made a 57-yard field goal to win the NFL game between Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars.

"We're looking! Everything's an option," joked Goodell of travelling as far as the moon.

"We were thrilled. When you look back at that, when you think about 10am on a Friday morning, 100,000 people coming to the NFL game, it was just remarkable.

"We shut down the town for most of the weekend. It was really, for us, an eye-opener to see something like that, so we were happy.

"We're looking back at it, too. When we play these games, we're thinking long-term. We're not coming into these games to play one game, we want to use it as a launchpad."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Former England cricketer Stuart Broad discusses attending Jacksonville Jaguars against Philadelphia Eagles in London.

Goodell describes the NFL's global ambitions as a "360 challenge" as it continues to explore new markets, and credits the success of London as a host in paving the way for further expansion.

"London was the foundation, really," he said.

"The teams, what was really required, number one, was clearly to make it a successful event. One thing was to make sure the teams had an experience so they can go back and it hasn't completely disrupted their season, that in fact it enhances it.

"We were fortunate that in the first year we had the Giants and Dolphins and neither were playing great, but the Giants went on a run and what contributed to that was that they were here and they came together as a team."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Baltimore Ravens at the Dallas Cowboys from Week 3 of the NFL season.

Sunday's game in Paris arrives on the back of three straight in London across Tottenham and Wembley, while also preceding games in Madrid and Munich in November.

Mexico City returns to the schedule next month, while Asia has emerged as another potential destination.

The league isn't slowing down.

Sports.title: Lewis named on England bench as Ashton replaces Eckersley for France
Sports.content:
England head coach Brian McDermott has made one change to his 19-man squad for Saturday's Rugby League World Cup match against France.

AJ Brimson retains the job at full-back with Jack Welsby again named as an interchange, while Luke Thompson starts at prop in the absence of Morgan Knowles, who suffered an injury in the lead-up to the opening-game defeat to Tonga.

Veteran centre Kallum Watkins is listed among the reserves as he chases a cap at his fourth World Cup, while Mikey Lewis returns to the bench after missing out on a place in the squad last time out.

As per World Cup rules, each side is able to name a six-player bench in each game, but only four of the six players named can be brought on.

Last weekend against Tonga, Welsby and Warrington Wolves winger Matty Ashton were the unused substitutes. Wigan Warriors speedster Zach Eckersley was initially selected to start again, until Ashton replaced him on Thursday.

Sports.title: O'Neill challenges Celtic to 'find a way' to win in Europe
Sports.content:
The 2-1 defeat to Celta Vigo was Celtic's third straight loss in the Europa League; they are second bottom of the table and yet to pick up a point; watch Hibernian vs Celtic live on Sky Sports Football on Sunday from 11am

Martin O'Neill challenges Celtic to 'find a way' in Europe - but are they just not good enough?

Celtic have lost their last four games in European competition

Martin O'Neill wants Celtic to find a way to win in Europe, but after a third straight defeat is the step up from domestic dominance too big for them?

The Hoops are now 35th of 36 teams in the Europa League after a third loss, this time against Celta Vigo. Only Ararat-Armenia are keeping them off the bottom of the table on goal difference.

A 7-1 hammering of Hearts in the Premiership gave some hope that Celtic were on the up. Instead, their European frailties were laid bare once again.

Germany midfielder Mika Baur fired the home side in front just over a minute into the second half and for a short spell it looked like Celtic could go on and get those elusive first three points.

However, Spain international Javi Rodriguez scored twice in three minutes - a header then an unstoppable drive - to leave the Hoops with no points from nine in the league phase with five fixtures remaining.

O'Neill said: "We conceded a free-kick and I thought a second before that we should have had a foul for us.

"They score from the free-kick and it knocks us a little bit. It gave them a bit of momentum.

"If [Liam] Scales' header goes in to make it 2-0, we get the three points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Celtic manager Martin O'Neill believes they can still progress in the Europa League despite Celta Vigo inflicting their third straight defeat in this season's tournament

"We've lost three matches now, remarkably we're still in with a chance [of progressing].

"We've got to win here and got to win away from home.

"We take the lead in the game, if we get the second goal we win the match and it changes the whole dynamic.

"It didn't happen, that's it - we need to try to find a way to win European games."

Celtic looked all but certain to be playing Champions League this season when they took a 4-0 aggregate lead against Austrian champions LASK in the play-off round, only to concede five goals to drop into the Europa League.

Celtic in Europe this season EL - Celtic 1-2 Celta Vigo

EL - Benfica 4-1 Celtic

EL - Celtic 1-3 Ferencvaros

CL play-off - LASK 5-1 Celtic

CL play-off - Celtic 3-0 LASK

O'Neill's side have lost their last four European matches while shipping 14 goals.

Goalscorer Baur admits Celtic are simply struggling at Europa League level at the moment.

"The focus is performing every three days in the league. That's first and then performing in Europa League or international football as well," he said.

"At the moment, maybe we are not capable to win these games. But in two weeks, that's the next one, against Besiktas, home again. Hopefully a good atmosphere. We need the points.

"But, absolutely disappointing.

Image: Mika Baur opened the scoring for Celtic

"The first half was absolutely okay, it was an open game.

"Then we scored, then we had 10, 12, 15 minutes where we controlled it and dominated it, and then they scored, and at that moment the momentum switched completely and we were not capable to switch it again.

"We had no control. We made mistakes, they pushed us in our own half, around our box.

"It's not getting easier now but there's still five games ahead. What else should we do then but believe?

"As I said, five games ahead and the chances are there. We need points."

Sports.title: Rugby League World Cup 2026: Latest results and schedule
Sports.content:
The Rugby League World Cup runs until November 15; England men play Tonga, France, and PNG in the group stages; England women play Wales, Australia, and Samoa in the group stages; Australia are the defending champions in both

Latest scores and results from the 2026 Rugby League World Cup, with Australia, New Zealand, and Papua New Guinea playing host to the men's, women's and wheelchair tournaments.

In the men's and women's tournaments, Australia are the defending champions, while England currently hold the title of world champions in the wheelchair competition.

The men's match got the World Cup under way on Thursday October 15, as Australia pulled off a thrilling 24-22 win over New Zealand.

England men suffered a tough opening 30-12 loss against Tonga and will look to bounce back against France on Saturday October 24, with kick-off at 7.35am. England women started their title charge with a huge 70-6 win over Wales. They now face the tough test of Australia on Saturday October 24, with kick-off at 10.05am.

The wheelchair tournament gets going on Friday October 30, when England take on Wales at 4.30am.

Men's Pools - and the unique format

Group A : Australia, New Zealand, Cook Islands, Fiji

: Australia, New Zealand, Cook Islands, Fiji Group B : England, Lebanon, Samoa

: England, Lebanon, Samoa Group C: France, Papua New Guinea, Tonga

The format of the Men's Rugby League World Cup is rather unusual.

The four teams in Group A will face each other. The two teams that finish top of the group will progress to the semi-finals.

However, things are a bit different for teams in Group B and C.

The teams in Group B will play the three teams in Group C and vice versa. They will not play the teams in their own group.

Results from these matches feed into a combined Group B and Group C table with the two-highest-ranked teams going through to the semi-finals.

The team that finishes top of that combined table will face the runner-up in Group A in the last four. The team that comes second will play the winner of Group A.

Sports.title: Wilcox wants Howe if Manchester United sack Carrick; Dortmund fight back against influencers: football news – live
Sports.content:
3m ago 07.47 EDT Ed Aarons Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start Most footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024, the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor. Gross was moving from Brighton to Borussia Dortmund after seven years in the Premier League and reported to his boyhood club for pre-season training days later. 22m ago 07.27 EDT Bundesliga fighting back against influencers View image in fullscreen Borussia Dortmund fans get behind their team at Signal Iduna Park before their Bundesliiga fixture against Werder Bremen. Photograph: Hesham Elsherif/NurPhoto/Shutterstock A stadium selfie could soon cost fans of German giants Borussia Dortmund after the club announced plans to reward those who leave their phones alone during the game. Dortmund are offering signed jerseys and gift cards for club merchandise to fans who use an app which measures how often they unlock their phones at its stadium. Arguing that “more and more fans are annoyed by selfies, streaming, and social media in the stands,” Dortmund say supporters can opt to use a “fan mode” in the club’s app, starting Saturday with a home game against Eintracht Frankfurt. The rewards scheme and app are entirely voluntary and there’s no ban on fans using their phones. Fan mode will measure how often the phone is unlocked during the game — not counting the halftime break — and award points to people based on how little they use the device, with prizes on offer for those with the most points. Each time the phone is unlocked, the user loses points. “Over 81,000 people in the stadium, singing, cheering, and holding their breath together: this here and now is irreplaceable,” said Dortmund chief executive Carsten Cramer. The club’s stance is part of a backlash in German football against attempts to turn its stadium atmosphere into social media content, especially by influencers using professional camera equipment. Hertha Berlin said this month it was banning “commercially produced and monetized” video productions from its games, while allowing fans to take photos and videos for personal use. Another club, Dynamo Dresden, said in August it would ban commercial filming for social media, saying it wanted to ensure fans felt comfortable at the game and to protect the club’s TV rights deals. Sports.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
Sports.content:
Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus.

According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”.

All of which offers just the tiniest sliver of insight into an election that – in common with most modern Brazilian elections – has by turns been rancorous, divisive, wildly surreal and littered with contested facts, where the fake news sounds real and the real news often sounds fake. “Brazil is now a dystopian place,” said Renan Santos, one of the presidential candidates defeated in the first round of voting. “People do not talk about public policy. They just create entertainment content about politics.”

View image in fullscreen Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign has been using the Brazil shirt. Photograph: Douglas Shineidr/AFP/Getty Images

And this being Brazil, of course, it has been an election indelibly inflected by the ultimate entertainment content: football, its symbols and tropes, its ability both to explain and reflect a country torn along multiple planes. As president, Flávio’s father Jair – a deeply weird ex-military man who refers to his four sons by number – made a concerted effort to politicise the yellow national team shirt, appropriating it as an emblem of his campaign and wearing it at rallies. Numerous footballers – Neymar, Ronaldinho, Rivaldo, Dani Alves, Thiago Silva, Lucas Moura – allied themselves explicitly or tacitly to his cause.

In part this can be explained by the wider appeal of the Bolsonaros within Brazil’s evangelical Christian community, from which 20 of the 26 players in Brazil’s World Cup squad this summer came. Many are followers of neo-Pentecostalism, a highly commercialised brand of evangelism fuelled by 24-hour TV preachers, megachurches and vast ostentatious displays of material wealth, in which the individual is cast as the architect of their own fate.

The disaffected young urban men from which both Bolsonaros draw their base have little use for the minimum wage increases or welfare programmes established by current president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. They dream not of union membership but entrepreneurialism and influencer clout, conceive of society not as a collective struggle but as a game with winners and losers, where the aim is not to build order but to conquer the chaos.

View image in fullscreen Richarlison has a tattoo on his back featuring a portrait of himself, Neymar and former Brazil striker Ronaldo above a Brazilian favela. Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images

In this world Neymar – currently whiling away the last of his fading light at Santos – is not a cautionary tale, a potential all-time great footballing career that essentially disintegrated into frivolity and waste. In this world Neymar is an aspirational hero, a man who accumulated wealth and celebrity status beyond his wildest dreams, and did it all with a defiant wink, by apologising to nobody. Neymar has, of course, publicly backed the younger Bolsonaro before this election.

But the real footballing battleground of this election has been not the players, but the clubs. Last month Lula incited fury within Brazilian football by imposing a ban on sports betting in a country where an estimated 7% of the population are problem gamblers. Online gambling is also one of the sport’s major sources of revenue: 14 of Brazil’s 20 top-division clubs advertise online betting sites on their shirts. Star players such as Neymar and Vinícius Júnior make a handsome living endorsing gambling companies. “How am I going to pay for [Lucas] Paquetá?” the Flamengo president, Luiz Eduardo Baptista, complained on a podcast. Bolsonaro has criticised the ban and suggested he may be open to reversing it if elected.

And in a sense the dividing lines in this election are also the very same questions with which football has been grappling for decades. Is this a team game or a vehicle for individual volition? Is it all about the scent of triumph, the cold hard certainties of winning and losing, the reaping of accolades and capital, the haptic thrill of crushing enemies underfoot? Or can it also be an expression of collective will, civic and regional pride, representation and inclusivity, the pursuit of a goal larger than the self?
