Sports.title: Vergil Ortiz Jr. Faces Keith Thurman With Little Upside
Sports.content:
Vergil Ortiz Jr. gives the December 5 Benavidez–Cieslak DAZN pay-per-view another fighter fans want to watch. Whether Keith Thurman gives them another fight worth buying is a harder sell.

The former unified welterweight champion brings name recognition to the Glendale, Arizona card. His victories over Shawn Porter and Danny Garcia give promoters something familiar to advertise alongside Ortiz’s knockout record. But those wins offer little evidence of what Thurman can produce against an unbeaten puncher at this stage of his career.

Thurman, 37, enters off a sixth-round stoppage loss to Sebastian Fundora in March. He has not fought since. There is no rebuilding victory between that defeat and another dangerous opponent, leaving buyers to judge his chances largely on a performance in which he was thoroughly beaten. premierboxingchampions.com

That is the weakness in presenting Ortiz–Thurman as a major reason to purchase the event. Adding recognizable fighters improves a poster. Adding uncertainty about who wins improves the argument for paying.

Thurman’s best chance would appear to involve making Ortiz work for clean openings: moving, changing direction, and landing counters before getting away. Trading with the younger fighter would invite the kind of sustained punishment Thurman needs to avoid.

Fundora and Ortiz present different challenges. Fundora’s unusual height and reach helped him control Thurman, so that defeat does not establish exactly how this fight will unfold. Ortiz, however, brings his own pressure through body punching, combinations, and the ability to punish an opponent who stays within range.

The concern is whether Thurman can maintain the movement and concentration that approach requires. Doing it for a few early rounds is one thing. Keeping Ortiz from wearing him down over 12 is another.

The announcement also lists this as a middleweight bout, despite Ortiz’s recent work at 154 pounds. That detail deserves attention, although the release does not specify the contracted weight.

For Ortiz, the clearest benefit is finally getting back into the ring after stopping Erickson Lubin in November 2025. A place beneath David Benavidez also puts him in front of an audience that could follow him into bigger fights.

“Overall I’m just happy to be active again,” Ortiz said in the announcement.

That explains accepting a fight. It does less to establish Thurman as the right opponent for a fighter who has already beaten Serhii Bohachuk, Israil Madrimov and Lubin.

Oscar De La Hoya’s sales pitch was revealing: “Keith Thurman is a crafty, experienced fighter who has been in there with the very best and will give Vergil some good rounds.”

“Good rounds” is a modest promise for a pay-per-view co-main event. It sounds like preparation for a bigger fight rather than the bigger fight itself.

Ortiz also faces an uneven reward. A quick stoppage would be expected against an older opponent coming off a stoppage defeat. A difficult night would invite unfavorable comparisons with Fundora. Thurman’s name would go onto Ortiz’s record, but beating him now would add less than beating him during his championship years. Ortiz–Thurman can contribute action, familiarity, and the possibility of another Ortiz knockout.

Some buyers will value that addition. Fans still deciding whether Benavidez–Cieslak deserves their money, however, need a stronger reason to believe the co-main event will be competitive. Thurman’s last performance makes that belief difficult to sell.

Sports.title: Bob Arum Calls Shakur Stevenson’s $15 Million Price Unviable
Sports.content:
Bob Arum believes paying Shakur Stevenson $15 million per fight makes no financial sense unless outside funding covers what the event cannot earn. His explanation for the Zuffa split puts the focus on the price attached to Shakur rather than the difficulty of finding him an opponent.

Arum argued that a promoter has reason to walk away when a fighter’s purse cannot be supported by the business his fights produce.

“If you can get out of that contract, you get out of it,” Arum said to Fight Hub TV. “Did it cost them any money to get out? I don’t know.”

Arum described a $15 million-per-fight arrangement, although his comments do not establish the terms of Shakur’s contract. He also linked the split to what he believes is a reduction in Saudi funding, without providing documentation for that claim.

“To pay Shakur 15 million … financially, it’s not viable,” Arum said.

That is a hard argument for Shakur’s next promoter to avoid. A fighter can ask for any number, but someone has to cover the guarantee. If ticket sales, broadcast income and sponsorship cannot support it, the promoter needs another source of money or accepts a loss.

Arum applied the same reasoning to the failed Devin Haney negotiations. In his view, the amounts promised to both fighters exceeded what their proposed fight could justify.

“The money didn’t exist in the fight that they would have,” he said.

He considered Shakur–Haney a good fight that would interest fans. He still questioned whether that interest would produce enough revenue to cover the costs.

Shakur’s next deal will test whether another promoter sees a business at that price. Arum’s position leaves little room for sentiment: boxing ability can help sell a fight, but a $15 million guarantee still needs paying.

In MMA, Dana White controls athlete compensation tightly to guarantee promotion profitability. Handing out a reported $15 million guarantee for a fighter who historically struggles to sell out arenas outside of Newark or move domestic pay-per-views directly contradicts how Zuffa operates.

Without third-party subsidies covering the spread, Zuffa was looking at absorbing massive, multi-million-dollar losses per event. Once the Haney clash disappeared, Zuffa attempted to switch to realistic opponents that fit the market. When options like Jose “Rayo” Valenzuela were tabled with reduced, market-corrected money around $7 million, Shakur held firm on his premium valuation.

A promoter cannot keep a fighter active when the athlete demands A-side megastar money for B-level volume fights that the public will not buy on pay-per-view. Shakur’s defensive masterclasses appeal to purists, but casual ticket buyers and mainstream sports fans have never embraced that style.

Promoters are willing to swallow astronomical purses for high-risk, high-action punchers who generate viral knockouts and massive live gates. Shakur’s risk-averse, distance-control approach inside the ring made it impossible for Zuffa executives to justify treating him like Canelo Alvarez or Gervonta Davis at the box office.

Sports.title: Hearn Calls Out Haney and Teofimo for Playing Promoter on Other People’s Money
Sports.content:
The Matchroom promoter questioned how much financial responsibility fighters take on when they become promoters. His criticism targets arrangements that give a boxer company recognition and some control while leaving someone else to fund the show.

“What that means is they’re not willing to put one penny into the show, but they want a logo on the poster and they want to hear their name on the announcements and they want to have some input, which is fine,” Hearn said to the media.

Hearn named Haney and Teofimo while discussing their arrangements with DAZN. He suggested their wish to operate promotional companies helped explain how those deals came together quickly.

There are benefits for a fighter in that position. Having a company involved can give him more influence over his career and a share of revenue that might otherwise go to an outside promoter. It also creates a business identity that could continue after retirement.

But putting a logo on a poster is the easy part. Funding purses, selling tickets, employing staff, and absorbing losses require something beyond a company announcement. If another organization handles those responsibilities, the fighter’s role is different from that of a promoter financing an event.

Shakur Stevenson’s stated plans to start his own promotional company make the subject relevant to his next move, too. That does not establish how his business would operate or whether he intends to invest in shows.

Hearn’s comments also leave a question about the arrangements he criticized: he did not supply financial terms showing what Haney or Teofimo contributes or receives.

A fighter can negotiate a better deal without building a promotional operation. The real test comes when his company stages events, signs other boxers, and accepts the possibility of losing money. Until then, the announcement tells us less than the work that follows.

Hearn is telling an inconvenient truth about the current landscape, even if his motives are entirely self-serving.

From an operational standpoint, he is dead on. There is a massive distinction between being a licensed promoter who takes actual financial exposure and operating a vanity boutique. Sticking an LLC graphic in the corner of a promotional graphic, negotiating a co-promotional fee, or demanding that Jimmy Lennon Jr. say a company name in the ring is basically just an athlete branding exercise.

Real promoting is ugly business: underwriting seven-figure guarantees, absorbing production shortfalls, paying sanctioning fees, moving tickets through grassroots footwork, and taking the bath when a gate flops. When DAZN, Matchroom, or Top Rank fronts the operating capital and takes the hit on red ink, the fighter is still an employee with a boutique label attached to their check.

At the same time, Hearn’s frustration is transparent. Traditional promoters used to control fighters by owning the apparatus: the venue deals, the broadcast pipeline, and the financial leverage. Haney, Lopez, and potentially Stevenson are bypassing that old dynamic by exploiting platforms willing to buy content directly.

From a boxer’s perspective, skipping the financial downside while still extracting extra broadcast money and retaining career independence is simply good leverage. If a network or investor allows them to claim promotional clout without putting up escrow, only a fool would voluntarily volunteer their own cash to absorb risk.

The rubber only meets the road when a fighter tries to build an actual stable. Floyd Mayweather backed up Mayweather Promotions because he eventually signed outside talent, staged shows without being the headliner, and cut checks from his own accounts.

Until guys like Haney or Lopez write checks to support younger prospects on untelevised undercards and stomach a six-figure loss on a slow night, Hearn has a valid point: they are prize fighters with vanity logos, not genuine fight promoters.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Gets His Chance Against Emanuel Navarrete
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie Foster isn’t agreeing to a slugfest just because Emanuel Navarrete wants one. With three super featherweight titles available Saturday in San Antonio, Foster intends to make Navarrete fight on terms that suit him.

Their comments at Thursday’s press conference supplied an edge to a fight week that has struggled for attention despite the stakes. Navarrete brings the WBO and IBF belts to Frost Bank Center, while Foster puts his WBC title into the unification.

“What I don’t want is an entire night where we’re just jabbing each other to see who can land more jabs. I think people want to see a good fight. They want to see a war,” said Navarrete.

That request benefits Navarrete. A fight fought at close range would give the Mexican champion more opportunities to put his power and unconventional punches to work. Foster has little reason to volunteer for that when his chances depend on making Navarrete miss and pay.

“I don’t fight to other people’s advantages. Whatever he brings to the table, I’ll adjust,” Foster said.

Foster also questioned whether Navarrete would follow through on his own invitation once punches started coming back.

“He don’t really like getting hit, in my opinion,” Foster said. “He’ll trade with you, but we’ll see. If he does that, it’ll be a great night for me.”

The challenge for Foster is turning that confidence into enough clean work to win rounds. Making Navarrete miss alone won’t do it if the more aggressive champion keeps producing the more noticeable offense.

Navarrete said his camp included changes to nutrition and preparation. Saturday will test whether those adjustments help him maintain the pressure needed to keep Foster from controlling the distance.

Foster says he has chased this fight for almost three years. He finally has the opponent he wanted, with the chance to leave holding three belts.

Navarrete generates awkward leverage from every conceivable angle, and trying to trade hook-for-hook with him is exactly how fighters end up getting broken down and stopped. Foster’s entire game relies on reset steps, shoulder rolls, and controlling distance with the jab. The moment he plants his feet to trade, he throws away his only distinct tactical advantages.

In past fights, Foster has shown flat spots down the stretch, letting rounds slip away because he takes his foot off the gas or looks physically soft around the midsection. When fighters carry extra weight between camps, the late rounds invariably expose it.

Against a tireless volume puncher like Navarrete, that physical drop-off is fatal. Navarrete might look unorthodox and technically sloppy, but his output does not decline in rounds nine through twelve. If Foster gets arm-weary or his legs get heavy from carrying that extra padding into the second half of the fight, Navarrete will pin him against the ropes and drown him in punches.

DAZN’s main broadcast begins at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT. Albert Gonzalez faces Edward Vazquez in the featherweight co-feature, while Frank Martin meets Tarik Zaina at light welterweight.

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Advances Talks For Frank Sanchez Defense
Sports.content:
Filip Hrgovic’s next fight is moving toward a mandatory defense against Frank Sanchez, leaving the IBF heavyweight champion facing a difficult opponent without the payday he had hoped to secure against Daniel Dubois or the Anthony Joshua–Tyson Fury winner.

Mike Coppinger reports that Hrgovic and Sanchez are in advanced talks for a fight in Croatia during the first quarter of 2027. A date and venue have yet to be announced.

Hrgovic won the vacant IBF belt by stopping Moses Itauma, but Sanchez brings a different test. The Cuban is more likely to make Hrgovic work for openings than give him a stationary target for his right hand.

That could make this an awkward homecoming. Hrgovic will have the crowd expecting him to take charge, while Sanchez has reason to slow the action, move and force the champion to keep finding him. Hrgovic would need to apply pressure without spending rounds following the challenger around the ring.

Sanchez previously accepted a step-aside agreement that allowed Hrgovic’s title fight against Itauma to proceed. His opportunity now appears closer, with the two camps discussing a fight that would settle the champion’s mandatory obligation.

For Hrgovic, the danger is looking beyond the opponent directly in front of him. Dubois remains an obvious target because of their previous fight, which handed the Croatian his only professional defeat. Getting another chance at Dubois would offer Hrgovic something a routine title defense cannot: an opportunity to reverse that result.

Sanchez has his own reason to interrupt those plans. A victory in Croatia would give him the IBF belt and put him into the unification discussions Hrgovic wants to pursue.

The homecoming would belong to Hrgovic. Whether he leaves with the same options he brought into the fight would depend on getting past Sanchez first.

Hrgovic absorbed heavy punishment from Itauma before the youngster ran out of gas in the second half of the fight. Sanchez does not carry that flaw. He is a seasoned Cuban amateur with hundreds of rounds in the bank, excellent pacing, and no inclination to sprint early or blow his engine looking for an early knockout.

Stylistically, Sanchez is built to give Hrgovic nightmares. Hrgovic thrives against heavyweights who plant their feet and let him set up his straight right hands. Sanchez will not stand there. He circles, counters, keeps the tempo slow, and relies on slick upper-body movement.

If Hrgovic approaches this the way he did against Dubois or in the early rounds with Itauma, he risks getting picked apart from the outside while walking into sharp counter hooks. The business side makes it even worse.

A stadium fight in Croatia against Sanchez will not generate the massive purse or international buzz of a Dubois rematch or a major Riyadh Season headliner. Yet a loss completely derails Hrgovic, strips away his title, and hands all his leverage in the division straight to Sanchez.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Expects Conor Benn To Leave Zuffa
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn doubts Conor Benn will fight for Zuffa again, suggesting the price of his comeback could lead to a disagreement over the opponent.

The Matchroom promoter believes Zuffa will want Benn to accept a difficult fight to justify his purse. However, Hearn admits he does not know whom the company intends to offer, making this his forecast rather than evidence of a breakdown between Benn and his promoter.

“He’s got a comeback fight. Watch who they try and make him fight for that comeback fight,” Hearn told reporters. “I don’t believe he’ll fight for Zuffa again.”

Hearn referred to a $15 million payment to Benn while discussing fighter pay, but did not provide contract details establishing what Benn would receive for his next appearance.

Asked to identify the opponent, Hearn made clear he was describing what he expects to happen.

“I don’t know, but what they’ll do is they’ll give him an opponent he doesn’t want to fight because he’s on a lot of money for a comeback fight,” he said.

That is the potential difficulty with an expensive comeback. The fighter may want an opponent who allows him to rebuild, while the promoter wants a bout that earns back some of its investment. Finding someone who satisfies both sides becomes harder when the purse is already high.

Demanding a tough fight hardly proves Zuffa wants rid of Benn. Any company committing serious money can reasonably expect a competitive contest. Benn’s actual reaction will come down to the exact opponent, the financial terms, plus what his contract requires.

Hearn’s critique must also be weighed against the source. As a competing promoter who spent much of the conversation taking aim at Zuffa’s boxing footprint, his forecast carries an obvious commercial angle.

Concrete matchmaking offers will give this situation substance. For now, Hearn has put his name to a blunt forecast, betting Benn’s negotiations end with him walking away rather than returning to the ring for Zuffa.

Handing Conor Benn a soft touch on a massive guarantee is financial malpractice for an outfit trying to establish a foothold in boxing.

Zuffa is not running a charity or operating like an old school promoter willing to absorb red ink just to build a fighter’s confidence. If they are cutting an eight-figure check or anything close to it, they need eyeballs, gate revenue, and platform buzz to offset the layout. A walkover against an unranked body does none of that.

Benn has spent years fighting sporadic rounds, dealing with layoffs, and avoiding the elite tier at 147. His ring identity was built on aggressive matchmaking against aging veterans rather than proven, prime operators.

Even pulling an elite light welterweight up to a catchweight or a soft 147 presents a nightmare. Fighters like Subriel Matias, Richardson Hitchins, or Gary Antuanne Russell possess the precision, hand speed, and technical discipline to exploit Benn’s reckless attacks inside six rounds.

The welterweight division may be transitional, but throwing Benn in with someone like Brian Norman Jr., Richardson Hitchins, or even a rugged veteran who can take a shot means Benn is live to get completely exposed.

If Benn’s camp expects a showcase fight while cashing an elite purse, the negotiations are doomed from the jump. Zuffa’s natural move is to demand a real fight where the outcome is genuinely in doubt. The moment they slide a dangerous name across the table, Benn either has to take the gamble of his life or walk away from the payday entirely.

Sports.title: Denzel Bentley Loses Appeal To Bypass Yoenli Hernandez
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley’s November 7 fight against Shane Mosley Jr. now threatens his hold on the WBO middleweight title after the sanctioning body rejected his appeal and ordered him to face Yoenli Hernández next.

The ruling leaves Bentley’s planned Zuffa Boxing debut in conflict with his mandatory obligation. If he intends to keep the WBO championship, the committee’s decision requires Hernández to come first.

The WBO announced Thursday that its Complaint and Grievance Committee had denied Bentley’s appeal and upheld the mandatory order.

“Both parties have been ordered to confirm their intention to proceed within 24 hours of service of the Award.”

That deadline concerns whether Bentley and Hernández intend to proceed. It does not mean they must complete negotiations or fight within 24 hours. Nor does the announcement say Bentley has already been stripped.

Still, Bentley has lost the appeal he hoped would allow him to retain his championship while taking the Mosley fight. He previously argued that he should be permitted a voluntary defense before meeting Hernández. The WBO has refused to approve that route. talksport.com

Bentley’s team booked Mosley while the title issue remained unresolved. That decision now puts pressure on the November 7 plans, with the WBO insisting its mandatory challenger cannot be made to wait through another opponent.

The financial side helps explain Bentley’s reluctance. The mandatory fight already went through purse bids, with the WBO’s official minutes recording a $200,000 bid. That is the total bid for staging the contest, rather than Bentley’s individual purse. wboboxing.com

A better-paying opportunity elsewhere may appeal to Bentley, but it does not remove Hernández’s right to challenge for the belt. Allowing a champion to book another fight and then postpone his mandatory would leave the challenger paying the price for a deal he had no part in making.

Bentley can decide which opportunity he wants to pursue. What he cannot currently count on is taking the Mosley fight with the WBO’s approval while Hernández waits. The appeal was his attempt to keep both options available. Thursday’s ruling closes that route unless the sanctioning body subsequently changes its position.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia vs Floyd Mayweather: Is It Good Or Bad For Boxing?
Sports.content:
Boxing fans received an unexpected announcement as the reigning WBC welterweight world champion Ryan Garcia (26-2, 21 KOs) claims he and boxing legend Floyd “Money” Mayweather (50-0, 27 KOs) have agreed to a fight.

On October 21st, Ryan Garcia posted the breaking news on all of his social media platforms. Garcia claims his bout with Mayweather will be a real match, and the WBC strap will be at stake.

“Trust me at first I thought this was bull***,”Garcia said. “But it’s real Floyd and I agree to a fight 147 for the WBC welterweight championship of the world 50-0 vs The current champ.”

Garcia doubled down on the claim as he posted another message on his Instagram account, and this message included a photo of Garcia and Mayweather in what appears to be a FaceTime call.

“Talking about fighting- it’s real, and he wants to do a real fight 147. He and I both agreed to post this! Let’s Rumble.”

When you glance at the tale of the tape, Ryan Garcia is 28 years old, and in four months Floyd Mayweather will be 50. That along with a few other red flags make boxing fans question why Garcia is interested in this bout?

Garcia blames Mayweather for changing the fight game in the worst way due to the fact that boxers in Garcia’s era try to mimic Mayweather by protecting their 0. It would be satisfying for Garcia to put the blemish on Mayweather’s record.

This bout is good for Mayweather because a fight against Garcia guarantees a big payday. Also, a victory over Garcia would take down Bernard Hopkins’ record, and it would make Mayweather the oldest boxer in history to win a world title.

This fight is good for boxing because a Mayweather vs. Garcia bout would grab the attention of the casuals. Casual fans will be intrigued by the star power and the fact that this bout will feature boxers from two different eras.

This potential fight is bad for boxing because some boxers have been fighting and clawing their way up the rankings trying to position themselves for a title shot. If the Mayweather vs. Garcia bout takes place, it means Floyd skipped the line.

Floyd Mayweather hasn’t fought a legitimate boxer since his bout against Andre Berto back in 2015. If the WBC approves Mayweather’s bid to skip the line, it would be egregious.

Speaking of the sanctioning body, as of now the WBC hasn’t approved this proposed Mayweather vs. Garcia bout. The news of this matchup is trending, but it may end up being clickbait.

It’s puzzling why Garcia wants this fight. Garcia could have matchups against Teofimo Lopez, Devin Haney, or Isaac “Pitbull” Cruz, but yet he wants to box an opponent who is 11 years removed from legitimate competition.

For Ryan Garcia, this appears to be a losing situation. If Floyd Mayweather beats him, it’s kind of embarrassing considering the circumstances. If he defeats Mayweather, he won’t receive the credit because by the time the fight takes place, Mayweather will be 50 years old!

This Ryan Garcia vs Floyd Mayweather situation has a few pluses, but it has a number of minuses. In the coming days and weeks, boxing fans and boxing pundits will give their opinions as it relates to the question, is this potential bout good or bad for boxing?

Ghana News.title: AG recommends prosecution of NDC’s Ashie Moore for alleged theft of a Singaporean businessman’s property
Ghana News.content:
Nii Ashie Moore

The Office of the Attorney-General has recommended that the Greater Accra Regional Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Emmanuel Nii Ashie-Moore, be charged with stealing, following allegations that he removed a Singaporean businessman’s luggage and personal belongings while the businessman was in police custody.

A document cited by Myjoyonline in connection with the case indicates that the Attorney-General’s Office considers the evidence gathered sufficient to support a charge against Mr Ashie-Moore under Section 124 of the Criminal Offences Act, 1960 (Act 29).

The document refers to an investigation docket containing witness statements, CCTV footage from Fiesta Residences and a cybercrime analysis report.

It identifies Mr Ashie-Moore as the first suspect and says the evidence suggests that he removed the complainant’s belongings from the hotel while the businessman was in police custody.

“Upon careful review of the entire docket, including the statements of the complainant, the 1st suspect, investigating officers, the CCTV footage from Fiesta Residences, and its accompanying cybercrime analysis report, it is my considered view that there is sufficient evidence to support a charge of stealing against the 1st suspect, Emmanuel Nii Ashie-Moore,” the document states.

According to the document, the CCTV footage corroborates the alleged removal of the luggage by Mr Ashie-Moore and other unidentified persons.

It also raises questions about how Mr Ashie-Moore came to possess the complainant’s medication and how the businessman’s passport was deposited at the High Court Registry.

The document says these circumstances suggest that Mr Ashie-Moore had control over the complainant’s property and support an inference that the belongings were dishonestly appropriated without lawful justification.

It consequently advises investigators to charge him with stealing, obtain a statement from him and forward it to the Attorney-General’s Office for prosecution.

“Your Special Investigation Unit (SIU) duplicate case docket with R.O. No.204/2025 is hereby retained for prosecution,” the document adds.

The recommendation does not, in itself, amount to a criminal conviction.

Background to the US$800,000 ECG contract allegations

The case is linked to allegations by Singaporean businessman Toh You Kang, who accused Mr Ashie-Moore of taking US$800,000 in connection with purported contracts with the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) for the supply of electric cables.

In a human rights action filed at the High Court in 2025, Mr Kang alleged that he paid the money after Mr Ashie-Moore represented that he could help secure contracts with ECG.

Mr Kang also accused the NDC regional chairman of violating his rights, including through his alleged detention and the seizure of his personal belongings. The claims formed part of a wider legal dispute between the two men.

Mr Ashie-Moore, through his lawyer, Gideon Tettey Tetteh, denied receiving the US$800,000 and rejected the allegations against him.

His legal team instead accused Mr Kang of defrauding Mr Ashie-Moore and his business partners.

The allegations remain subject to the relevant legal processes.

Ghana News.title: Obuasi SHTS abuse allegations: Otiko Djaba urges Vice-President to visit alleged victims
Ghana News.content:
Former Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection Otiko Afisah Djaba has urged Vice-President Prof Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang to visit students allegedly sexually abused at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), saying that calls for the law to take its course are not enough to address their immediate needs.

Speaking in an interview with JoyNews about the allegations against the school’s headmaster, Ms Djaba questioned what was being done to protect the affected girls while investigations continued.

Her comments follow a statement by the Vice-President describing the allegations as a serious national concern and calling for the law to take its course.

Ms Djaba said the Vice-President should demonstrate her commitment to the welfare of the students by engaging directly with them and ensuring they receive the necessary support and protection.

“While the law is taking its course, what's happening to the children?” she asked.

“I would have expected by now that she herself would go there,” she added.

Ms Djaba said her appeal was not about restricting the Vice-President’s responsibilities to women’s issues because of her gender. Rather, she said, the country’s first female Vice-President had an opportunity to demonstrate leadership on matters affecting women and children.

Recalling the Vice-President’s appeal for women’s support during the election campaign, she said the significance of having a woman in the country’s second-highest political office should be reflected in action on issues affecting their welfare.

“It's not about gender boxing,” she said.

“Nobody is saying that because you are a woman and you are a vice; only focus on women.”

She added: “When you have been given this huge opportunity, to whom much is given, much is expected.”

Ms Djaba also questioned the handling of the allegations, arguing that an earlier intervention could have prevented further harm to students.

Read also: Let the law take its course in Obuasi SHTS abuse exposé – Vice-President Opoku-Agyemang

Referring to April 2025, she said the failure to address the matter decisively at the time had allowed the situation to worsen, with the number of alleged victims reportedly reaching 19.

“The law, as we have seen, has failed us. The system has failed the girls,” she said.

“If this thing had been addressed in April of 2025, do you think we would be talking about 19 girls? No, it wouldn't have gotten to that. It wouldn't have.”

She further argued that an earlier intervention by the Vice President could have prevented other girls from allegedly being assaulted.

“If she had interfered, intervened in 2025, would we be talking about 19 girls? We would have avoided all these other girls being assaulted,” she said.

“And that is my pain,” she added.

Ms Djaba also criticised what she considered an inadequate public response from President John Mahama, urging him to speak clearly on the allegations and demonstrate that protecting children and upholding the law take precedence over political considerations.

“And the President of Ghana, what has he said? He's the father of all of us,” she said.

Acknowledging that the person at the centre of the allegations was a member of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC), she said political affiliation should not prevent the President from addressing the matter.

“Yes, the person is a member of his party. But even if it is your child who has committed a crime against Ghana, you must speak up and let the people of Ghana know,” she said.

“If you spoke, I don't think the police and these other institutions would be dilly-dallying and fooling around with what they are doing,” she added.

Ghana News.title: CPA marks 20 years without consumer protection law in Ghana, urges passage of bill by December
Ghana News.content:
The Consumer Protection Agency (CPA) has renewed calls on the President and Parliament to pass Ghana’s long-awaited Consumer Protection Bill before the end of 2026, warning that the absence of a comprehensive law continues to leave consumers vulnerable to unfair business practices, substandard products and poor services.

In a statement issued on Friday, October 23, to mark its 20th anniversary, the agency described the failure to enact the legislation, first drafted in 2006, as the country’s biggest setback in protecting consumer rights.

The CPA said the bill remained at the Ministry of Trade and Industry despite years of advocacy, petitions, national forums and stakeholder engagements aimed at securing its passage.

It warned that the lack of a dedicated legal framework had become particularly concerning amid the growth of e-commerce and the circulation of fake, unregistered and inferior products on the Ghanaian market.

The agency called for the passage of the bill and the establishment of a well-funded Consumer Protection Authority with the mandate and resources to enforce consumer rights and hold businesses accountable.

Two decades of consumer advocacy

Founded and funded by Kofi Kapito in 2006, the CPA was launched by the late Vice-President Alhaji Aliu Mahama to provide consumers with a platform to seek redress over goods and services.

Over the past two decades, the agency has campaigned against poor telecommunications services, called for sanctions against underperforming operators and advocated the use of fines imposed on them to fund consumer education.

It also organised what it described as Ghana’s first Off Phone Day protests against telecommunications companies over poor service delivery.

In the retail sector, the CPA campaigned against the use of “olonka” and other unapproved measuring containers in markets, advocating certified weighing scales to protect consumers from unfair measurements.

The agency said it had also worked with regulatory bodies, including the Food and Drugs Authority (FDA), Ghana Standards Authority (GSA) and Public Utilities Regulatory Commission (PURC), on initiatives to improve product safety and consumer welfare.

Over four million fake diapers removed from market

The CPA cited its interventions against fake and unregistered baby diapers as one of its notable achievements, claiming that more than four million pieces had been removed from the Ghanaian market through enforcement activities.

It also highlighted its involvement in addressing complaints about sanitary towels, saying the re-testing of registered products confirmed that they were safe for use.

The agency further listed its advocacy for reductions in electricity tariffs among its efforts to ease the burden on consumers.

It said fake, unregistered and substandard products continued to pose health and financial risks while threatening the survival of locally manufactured goods.

The CPA disclosed that it was collaborating with the Ministry of Finance and other stakeholders to develop a policy to address the influx of such products into the country.

Agency establishes mediation and arbitration centre

The CPA identified its contribution to making consumer protection a national issue as one of its major achievements, noting that media organisations and other institutions increasingly seek its assistance in resolving consumer complaints.

It also announced the establishment of what it describes as Ghana’s first Consumer Arbitration and Mediation Centre, which provides an alternative dispute resolution mechanism for consumer-related disputes.

According to the agency, cases referred to the centre can be resolved within one month, potentially offering consumers a faster alternative to lengthy court proceedings.

Four demands to strengthen consumer protection

As part of its anniversary statement, the CPA outlined four key measures it wants the government to implement to strengthen consumer protection.

They are:

Pass the Consumer Protection Bill: The agency wants the President and Parliament to ensure the bill is passed before the end of 2026.

Establish a Consumer Protection Authority: It is calling for a well-funded institution with the capacity to enforce consumer rights and hold businesses accountable.

Standardise market measurements: The agency wants certified weighing scales adopted across markets to prevent unfair trading practices.

Tackle substandard imports: It is urging the development of a clear policy to curb the importation and circulation of fake, unregistered and inferior products.

The CPA also raised concerns about funding for its operations, saying its work over the years had depended largely on the resourcefulness of its chief executive officer and support from benevolent institutions.

It expressed appreciation to individuals and institutions that had supported its consumer advocacy work over the past 20 years.

The statement was issued by Nana Prempeh Okogyeabour Aduhene, Executive Director for Mediation and Arbitration at the CPA.

Ghana News.title: Ghana, 2 others offer vehicle assembly growth in Sub-Saharan Africa – Fitch Solutions
Ghana News.content:
Outside South Africa, Ghana and Kenya offer the strongest near-term vehicle assembly growth in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA).

According to Fitch Solutions, Ghana are best positioned to attract new assembly investment over the medium term in Sub-Saharan Africa.

“Ghana's automotive industry remains smaller in scale but continues to benefit from supportive policy measures. The Auto Policy and local assembly incentives are encouraging investment, while improving consumer confidence should support demand growth”, it said.

“We forecast production to rise from around 4,700 units in 2025 to approximately 4,900 units in 2026. Although the expiry of the VAT exemption on locally assembled vehicles presents a near-term challenge, continued policy support should help increase local content and support gradual growth in assembly activity”, it added.

The UK-based firm said recent developments also highlight growing confidence in Ghana's assembly sector.

In September 2026, Zonda Tec expanded its Tema assembly facility, increasing annual production capacity to 12,000 passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles and EVs and creating an estimated 1,000 jobs.

While Ghana's manufacturing base remains relatively small, Fitch Solutions said the expansion demonstrates continued investor willingness to scale production capacity in the market.

Regional Integration Could Become Important

It added that regional integration could become increasingly important for both markets because supplier networks remain relatively underdeveloped.

“AfCFTA's [Africa Continental Free Trade Area] automotive framework creates scope for countries to participate in automotive value chains through components, materials and supplier industries rather than relying solely on final vehicle assembly. This should support gradual growth in local manufacturing activity as regional trade links deepen and sourcing becomes more integrated across African markets”.

Neither market, it said, is likely to emerge as a major export hub over the medium term, but both should play a growing role in regional vehicle assembly.

Ghana News.title: “I forgive you” – Koku Anyidoho tells Asiedu Nketiah
Ghana News.content:
Former Deputy General Secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Samuel Koku Anyidoho, says he has forgiven National Chairman Johnson Asiedu Nketiah, reflecting on their troubled political relationship as a 21-year era at the party’s headquarters draws to a close.

In a post on X on Thursday, October 22, Mr Anyidoho recounted how Mr Asiedu Nketiah was elected General Secretary in 2005, replacing the late Dr Nii Armah Josiah Aryeh, and went on to become the party’s longest-serving General Secretary before rising to the chairmanship.

Mr Anyidoho, who served as his deputy, recalled that their relationship deteriorated after he challenged his boss for the General Secretary position, despite what he said was an assurance that Mr Asiedu Nketiah would not seek another term.

“He knows, and most people know, I contested because he had assured me that he would not contest again. As it is, the rest is history,” he wrote.

He also alleged that Mr Asiedu Nketiah unilaterally announced his suspension after the contest, a decision he insists was invalid. Mr Anyidoho maintained that he remains a bona fide member of the NDC.

Despite their differences, he said he had chosen to move on and focus on the positive aspects of life rather than dwell on past grievances.

“I honestly had no issues whatsoever working with him as his Deputy,” he stated, adding that he was taken aback by the fallout following his decision to contest him.

Mr Anyidoho further alleged that he was deliberately provoked in an attempt to make him resign from the party, but said he refused to take the bait.

“Ultimately, you wanted me to get angry and say I have resigned from the NDC, but because I was your Deputy and know your modus operandi, I did not fall for your bait,” he wrote.

He said a chance meeting with Mr Asiedu Nketiah at Kumasi airport about two months ago offered a reminder that their differences did not erase their shared history. The two exchanged greetings, shook hands, joked and later chatted briefly on the same flight to Accra.

“I believe that there is more that unites us than divides us,” he said.

Mr Anyidoho also acknowledged Mr Asiedu Nketiah’s contribution to the NDC and Ghanaian politics, while alluding to his reported ambition to become the party’s presidential candidate.

“He has certainly written some history politically within the NDC and Ghana. I thank God He did not create me with a petty mind nor petty heart so I say to Johnson Kwadwo Asiedu-Nketiah, Ayekoo,” he wrote.

Concluding his message on a note of reconciliation, Mr Anyidoho said he had moved on and wished the NDC National Chairman well as he navigates the next phase of his political career.

“I have moved on in life and wish you well as you also move on in life. Shalom,” he added.

Ghana News.title: Fake business listings: How Ghanaians can check who they are paying
Ghana News.content:
A customer searches for a business online, finds a phone number, discusses a booking and sends a deposit. Later, the business says it never received the money. The person who answered the call was pretending to work there. Ghana’s Cyber Security Authority (CSA) has warned that fraudsters are placing fake business listings on search engines and online maps.

In an alert issued in April, it said 54 such cases had been reported between January 1 and April 26, 2026, with losses totalling GH₵266,195. Cybersecurity governance and risk specialist Valerie Arko-Adjei says customers should verify who they are dealing with before sending money.

Finding a business online, she explains, does not mean the contact number beside its name belongs to it. The scam works because the first steps feel ordinary. Many people use a search result or a map listing to find a phone number without giving it much thought.

A fraudster can use the name and address of a real business, then substitute a number they control. Once a customer gets in touch, the conversation may sound much like a genuine booking or sale. Knowing the price of a service does not prove that the person answering is legitimate.

Prices, photographs and descriptions may already be public. Before agreeing to pay, customers should check whether the number they called appears on the business’s own website or on a social media account they know belongs to it. If the details do not match, they should contact the business through a different, independently verified channel. Arko-Adjei also urges customers to pay attention to sudden changes in payment instructions.

Someone might say the usual mobile money number is temporarily unavailable or ask for a deposit to be sent to a personal account. There may be innocent reasons for a change, but customers should confirm it with the business using contact details they found separately. Calling the number that sent the new instructions only takes them back to the person whose identity they are trying to establish.

The CSA says some people responding to fake listings have been directed to forms asking for their phone number, mobile network, transaction amount, and mobile money PIN. A request for a PIN, one-time code, or banking password should end the conversation. Customers should leave the form or chat and contact their payment provider or the business through a number they have verified themselves.

If a payment has already been made, acting quickly matters. Contact the payment provider, explain what happened, and ask what steps are available for that transaction. Keep screenshots of the listing and conversation, along with the phone number and payment reference. Anyone who shared a PIN or code should secure the affected account immediately and report the incident. These records may help the provider and authorities investigate.

Arko-Adjei says businesses must make it easier for customers to check they are dealing with the right people. Those that accept online bookings or deposits can make their official contact numbers and payment channels easy to find. A clear notice explaining how payments are requested, and stating that staff will never ask for a customer’s mobile money PIN or one-time code, gives people something to check against when a message feels wrong.

Business owners should also search for their own names and check the phone numbers shown in map results. If they find an impersonator, they can report the listing to the platform and warn customers using their genuine accounts. Staff should know how to handle a report from someone who may have paid a fake account, including gathering the listing details and directing the customer to their payment provider.

The warning comes ahead of Ghana’s National Cyber Security Awareness Month in October. At the campaign’s September launch, the CSA said it had recorded 3,876 cybersecurity incidents between January and July 2026, with online fraud making up about 47%.

That figure covers online fraud generally; it is not a count of fake business listings. Arko-Adjei says the answer is to pause when a search result turns into a request for money: check the contact number, confirm any change in payment details, and keep PINs and security codes private. A short check before paying could spare a customer a far more difficult conversation afterwards. Suspicious listings and cybercrime incidents in Ghana can be reported to the CSA by calling or texting 292, sending a WhatsApp message to 050 160 3111, or emailing report@csa.gov.gh.

Valerie Arko-Adjei is a cybersecurity GRC (Governance, Risk, and Compliance) Professional with a background in behavioural science, focused on helping businesses and individuals understand risk and build stronger security habits through human-centred cybersecurity. She can be reached via adjeiv2@yahoo.com.

Ghana News.content:
Finance Minister Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson has announced that the government has paid over GH¢4.40 billion to the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) and for the settlement of Second-Tier Pension obligations.

According to him, the payments would help protect workers’ pensions and demonstrated the government’s commitment to managing public money responsibly and meeting its obligations.

“Government has paid over GH¢4.40 billion to SSNIT and for Second-Tier Pension obligations,” Dr. Forson stated.

“This helps protect workers’ pensions and shows our commitment to managing public money responsibly and meeting our obligations.”

The announcement follows a similar disclosure by the Minister that the government had released GH¢24.8 billion to statutory funds since January 2026.

Those payments were made on time and in full to support schools, healthcare, roads and local development.

The Minister said timely releases ensure that the funds have the resources needed to deliver essential services to Ghanaians.

Forms Capital Limited has been adjudged Marketing-Oriented Finance House of the Year, 2025 at the Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana (CIMG) 37th Annual National Marketing Performance Awards, in recognition of the company's excellence in strategic marketing and its commitment to creating value for customers and delivering strong business results.

The award was presented at the ceremony on Saturday, 17 October 2026, at the Labadi Beach Hotel in Accra. The recognition highlights Forms Capital's strategic approach to marketing, including the use of market insights, effective marketing programmes and customer-focused initiatives to support business growth and strengthen its position in Ghana's financial services industry.

For Forms Capital, the recognition represents an important milestone in its commitment to making financial services more accessible, relevant and impactful for individuals, businesses and communities.

Commenting on the achievement, Ishmael Abbey, Head of Business Development at Forms Capital Limited, said: "We are honoured to receive this recognition from the Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana. It affirms our belief that marketing goes beyond promoting products and services; it is about understanding people's needs, creating meaningful value and building lasting relationships with customers”.

“At Forms Capital, we continue to pursue innovative and customer-focused approaches that connect our financial solutions to the aspirations of individuals, entrepreneurs and businesses. This award is an encouragement to keep challenging ourselves, deepening customer trust and contributing to the growth of the communities we serve. We are grateful to our customers, partners and dedicated team members whose continued support and commitment make achievements like this possible”, he added.

Advancing Customer-Centred Financial Services

Forms Capital Limited continues to strengthen its approach to financial services through customer-focused solutions, strategic partnerships and initiatives designed to respond to evolving financial needs. Its marketing philosophy centres on connecting customers with relevant financial opportunities while building trust, improving engagement and supporting sustainable business growth.

As the company advances its growth ambitions and prepares for its next phase of development in Ghana's financial services sector, the CIMG award provides further motivation to deepen its commitment to innovation, customer experience and responsible business growth.

The company recognises that sustainable success is built on a combination of strong strategy, customer understanding, effective execution and the collective efforts of its people. This achievement therefore belongs to the entire Forms Capital team, alongside the customers and partners who continue to be part of its journey.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
