World.title: France tightens security in anticipation of weekend protests
World.content:
Gatherings banned and curfews extended as cities lock down in bid to avert more unrest.

French authorities have announced tightened security measures in a bid to prevent a repeat of violent unrest during protests last weekend.

President Emmanuel Macron was due to hold a meeting on Friday with his defence council, made up of top ministers and officials, and to meet security forces, as cities across the country confirmed limits on gatherings and public transport.

Macron’s announcement on Thursday that only union demonstrations would be authorised at the weekend has prompted harsh criticism from student groups whose demonstrations in recent weeks against conditions in schools were joined by groups denouncing high living costs and other grievances.

More than half a million people gathered across France last Saturday for demonstrations that spiralled into violence and looting.

Paris has extended a nighttime curfew until Monday, while Marseille and Lyon have banned gatherings, introduced curfews, and restricted public transport for this coming Saturday.

Police deployments will also be increased by 20 percent compared with last weekend, after the government was accused of being blindsided by the scale of the unrest.

Macron, who has blamed “seditious” ultra-left groups for the unrest, is due to announce “additional decisions” following the defence council meeting, his office said.

‘Trampling on freedoms’

Despite the restrictions, France’s main student union, UNEF, has called ⁠⁠for rallies on Saturday. The Yellow Vest movement, an anti-establishment force that first emerged in 2018 and re-entered the French political consciousness last weekend, has filed plans for a march through central Paris.



Macron was due to meet student representatives later on Friday to discuss their plans, but UNEF said their rallies would go ahead.

“Macron is trampling upon the freedom to protest in our country, and is spitting on the values of the republic he claims to defend,” UNEF said.

Shops and businesses in major cities have been urged to close. The Louvre and the Louis Vuitton Foundation will be closed on Saturday, while the Paris edition of the Art Basel fair will end on Friday, two days ahead of schedule.

Since last Saturday’s violence, 2,700 people have been arrested, according to the Ministry of Justice.

World.title: South Korea invites North for military talks over border
World.content:
The proposal comes days after Pyongyang says it moved new military units into ‘firing positions’ along the border.

South Korea has proposed holding military talks with North Korea in a bid to calm rising tensions over their heavily fortified border.

Seoul said on Friday that it had invited Pyongyang to discuss restoring communication channels. The offer was made as military activity on the border increases.

Talks with North Korea would aim to “mutually confirm” the precise location of the land Military Demarcation Line (MDL), “discuss ways to restore military communication lines and prevent accidental clashes in border areas”, Kim Hong-cheol, deputy minister for national defence policy, told reporters.

“Specific dates and locations could be discussed through Panmunjom,” Kim said, referring to the symbolic truce village on the North-South border where soldiers from both Koreas stand face to face.

He added that the South was open to three-way talks involving the United States-led United Nations Command and hoped for “a positive response from North Korea”.

It remains unclear whether North Korea would agree to talks. Leader Kim Jong Un has taken a hardline approach towards Seoul and suspended virtually all dialogue and cooperation with the South in recent years.

Meanwhile, Pyongyang has raised its military activity along the border and continues to do so.

On Wednesday, Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of the North Korean leader, announced that new military units have been moved into “firing positions” along the border.

Mines, barbed-wire fences, tactical roads, antitank walls and other fortifications have also been added to one of the world’s most heavily armed borders.



Tensions have worsened since last month when three South Korean soldiers were injured by explosions near the military demarcation line in the western section of the Demilitarized Zone, the buffer zone that runs between the Koreas, commonly known as the DMZ.

The South blamed the blast on landmines laid by the North and demanded an apology. Pyongyang has fiercely rejected the accusation.

Seoul’s Ministry of National Defence said on Friday that it was difficult to predict “what further incidents could occur if this situation is allowed to continue unaddressed”.

The ministry noted that a proposal for talks last year did not receive a response from Pyongyang.

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung has called for the North to return to dialogue. However, Kim Yo Jong responded by slamming the suggestion of bilateral talks as “the climax of the farce”.

World.title: New electronics reach Iran, but prices soar as gov’t fees, US sanctions hit
World.content:
Latest smartphones are finding their way into Iran despite sanctions and trade restrictions, but many can’t afford them.

Tehran, Iran – When the latest iPhone 18 lineup was released by Apple in the United States on September 18, it only took a couple of days for the new models to go on sale in downtown Tehran.

That is despite Apple not having a physical presence in Iran due to years of international sanctions, and the ongoing months-long US naval blockade of Iran’s southern ports, through which the bulk of the country’s imports previously entered.

“These things can’t stop a mobile phone seller,” a phone and accessories trader in Tehran’s Charsou Mall, a major electronics hub, told Al Jazeera, asking to remain anonymous for security reasons.

But he explained that the process of bringing in phones has become much more complicated, time-consuming and costly, due to both external pressures and domestic conditions imposed by the Iranian government.

Many electronics manufactured internationally are imported into Iran via Dubai in the United Arab Emirates, but the nearly eight-month-long war with the US and Israel has disrupted trade through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has also repeatedly attacked the UAE throughout the conflict, and the UAE also announced a halt to trade, commercial exchanges and financial transactions with Iran on August 19.

Some Iranian traders then pivoted to using passengers coming in from Oman to bring in phones and other items. But after US sanctions on all Iranian airlines – and anyone who provides services for them – came into effect in September, few flights are landing in the country.



“Most of the phones are now smuggled into the country. Many go to Sulaimaniyah and then come in by land,” the trader said, referencing the northeastern city in the Kurdish region of northern Iraq, which borders western Iran.

A similar story has also been true for many other electronics currently found in the Iranian market, including laptops, graphics and processing units, PlayStation devices and even Starlink terminals.

This week in Tehran, a MacBook Air 15-inch M4 sold for the rial equivalent of more than $1,450, about 6 percent higher than an average retailer in the UAE. A one-terabyte PlayStation 5 Slim disc-edition console was going for about $730, or 11 percent more expensive than some retailers in the US.

‘Registration’ and other fees

Things are much worse when it comes to mobile phones.

Mobile phone service on imported devices only works for 30 days if a registration fee to the Iranian government is not paid.

The fee was introduced nearly 10 years ago, ostensibly aimed at fighting smuggling and corruption. The amount varies depending on the value of the phone, with the government charging import duties of up to 6 percent for phones worth below 600 euros ($673), up to 15 percent for phones between 600 and 900 euros ($673 and $1,010), and up to 30 percent for phones with a value above 900 euros.

After adding other levies and “warranties” from domestic companies, extra charges for some phones can amount to more than half of the total price paid.

But even a registered phone cannot be used to freely access the internet, as the government imposes severe internet filtering and shutdowns, while global payment methods are off-limits to Iranians and international firms refuse many services to Iranian nationals because of US sanctions.

According to the state-linked Tasnim news site, about $1.6bn worth of mobile phones were imported commercially during the previous Iranian year ending in March 2026, up to 20 percent of which were phones priced at more than $600. Phones worth $470m were brought in by aeroplane passengers, most of them higher-spec phones. There are no clear figures for smuggled phones.

In mid-August, customs chief Foroud Asgari told state media that approximately one million phones had been imported during the first five months of the current Iranian year, versus 3.16 million in the corresponding period of a year earlier. He said the import value of the phones had fallen by approximately 70 percent.

The government can also decide to stop the registration of phones whenever it deems necessary.



That was the case between 2023 and 2024 for newer iPhone models, which authorities said could not be registered under any circumstance because they were made by an American company and were gobbling up precious foreign currency reserves for imports. Authorities did not take issue with similarly-priced high-end models.

Skyrocketing government charges and local restrictions are making it harder for Iranian customers to afford new phones at a time when the monthly minimum wage and basic government subsidies for an average married worker amount to the equivalent of just $83 in Iran.

The rial, the country’s national currency, has continued on its downward spiral. It changed hands for about 2.64 million per US dollar in Tehran on Monday, slightly improved from an all-time low reached earlier this month.

Prices have been surging across the board, especially for food and other essentials, as domestic mismanagement, war damage, sanctions and blockade squeeze the Iranian economy and make most of the country’s 90-million population poorer.

Afsaneh, a 27-year-old teacher from Tehran, said she has been thinking about replacing her iPhone 13 with last year’s 17 model, but balks when she sees the prices.

“The only way to get it is to sell my current phone, use my small savings and also borrow from my parents,” she told Al Jazeera.

She pointed out that many among her peers and acquaintances are also forced to keep old devices alive by repairing them or replacing parts, if possible, since they cannot afford to upgrade.

“A lot of people are one failure of a major electronic device away from getting into serious debt,” she said.

World.title: Serbia’s snap election: What’s at stake and can students unseat Vucic?
World.content:
A snap parliamentary vote on October 25 will determine whether a student-led group can loosen Vucic’s grip on power.

Serbia will hold a snap parliamentary election on October 25 .

The vote is seen as a test of whether President Aleksandar Vucic’s Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) can extend its 14-year grip on power and stave off a student-led movement born out of mass anti-government protests.

Here’s what you need to know:

How did Serbia get here?

In November 2024, the collapse of a concrete canopy at a railway station in Novi Sad killed 16 people. What began as demands for accountability over the disaster grew into a nationwide movement against alleged corruption and the government’s handling of the tragedy.

Students emerged as the movement’s driving force, organising some of Serbia’s biggest demonstrations since the overthrow of Slobodan Milosevic. Their campaign has channelled deep frustration with the SNS, which has governed since 2012, and with a conventional opposition seen as fragmented and ineffective.

The parliamentary election was not due until late 2027. But Vucic resigned from the presidency in September, ahead of the end of his second and final constitutional term, and is leading the SNS campaign for prime minister. The manoeuvre has made the parliamentary contest central to his effort to retain political power before a separate presidential election must be held.

Who is challenging the ruling party?

The main challenger is the student-backed Student List–Students Win (Studentska lista–Studenti pobeduju), which brings together candidates with little or no previous political experience, including academics, teachers and other professionals.



It is campaigning on restoring the rule of law, ending corruption and rebuilding institutions, rather than focusing on divisive questions such as Kosovo, European Union membership or relations with Russia.

“The political dynamic has changed from the ground up,” Jelena Vasiljevic, a senior research associate at the University of Belgrade’s Institute for Philosophy and Social Theory, told Al Jazeera.

Young people, long considered the country’s most politically disengaged group, have become the core of its largest social mobilisation in decades, she said.

Some opposition parties have chosen not to run and instead support the student list.

Others are contesting the election but face the prospect of failing to clear the threshold for parliament. As a result, many see the vote as not simply a contest between parties, but a referendum on whether the SNS system should continue.

Why does the election matter?

The outcome will shape whether Serbia attempts to reset institutions that critics say have been hollowed out by years of party control. The SNS rejects allegations of abuse and corruption, but its opponents and rights groups accuse it of putting pressure on independent media, electoral malpractice and using state resources to maintain power.

For Vasiljevic, turnout will be decisive. The SNS retains a disciplined core electorate, supported by a clientelist model of government, in which goods and services are exchanged for political support, she said. The student list must not only unite opposition-minded voters but also mobilise habitual non-voters and the undecided.

A student list breakthrough would also remake the opposition.

Vasiljevic said parliament could contain a large group of politically inexperienced and ideologically diverse student-backed politicians, while traditional opposition parties could be greatly reduced. The result may therefore start a wider reorganisation of Serbia’s political landscape, regardless of who forms the government.

But winning power would be only the beginning.

Srdan Majstorovic, chair of the governing board of the European Policy Centre, said a new government would face the far harder task of rebuilding a democratic system after what he described as 14 years of systematic damage to institutions, the rule of law and public trust, compounded by deep social divisions and rampant corruption.

After years of what critics call a captured-state system, he said, Serbia would need a broad reset of its democratic governance.

What’s at stake for foreign policy?

Serbia’s stalled EU path is a part of the backdrop.



Majstorovic said progress has been blocked by concerns over the rule of law, Serbia’s limited alignment with EU sanctions, including those against Russia, and the stalled normalisation process with Kosovo.

A change in government would not automatically transform foreign policy, he said.

The student movement has avoided detailed commitments, instead treading carefully to unite left, centre and right-leaning voters.

But Majstorovic said democratic reform, judicial independence, free media and tackling corruption could renew cooperation with Brussels and revive the accession process.

Igor Bandovic, director of the Belgrade Centre for Security Policy, said foreign policy remained the biggest unknown in the student list’s programme. Its candidates have taken a hard line on Kosovo, proposed reviewing agreements reached under EU auspices and floated a referendum on EU membership within six months of taking office. They have also signalled continuity in relations with Russia.

Bandovic said a new government would probably face more immediate domestic priorities and the constraints of the Balkans’ security environment. But a referendum on EU membership could slow or halt accession further. If the SNS stays in power, he expects further deterioration in relations with Brussels.

External actors are watching closely.

Bandovic said Moscow has offered explicit support to the government, portraying the protests as a Western-backed “colour revolution”. The United States Congress has voiced concern about democratic standards and Serbia’s ties with Russia, while the US administration has been more restrained.

China, which has commercial interests in Serbia, has avoided public comment but is likely to prefer continuity.

How does the election work?

Voters will elect all 250 members of the National Assembly in a single nationwide constituency.

One ballot is cast for a party or coalition list, with seats allocated proportionally.

Electoral lists generally need at least 3 percent of votes to enter parliament, while recognised minority lists are exempt from the threshold.

The list or coalition able to command a majority in the 250-seat assembly will form a government.

But with the result expected to be close and the campaign taking place amid deep mistrust, the legitimacy of the process may prove as consequential as the final seat count.

Polls will close on Sunday at 8pm local time. Preliminary results are expected about two hours later.

World.title: NBA’s Irving praises Al-Shaair’s ‘selfless act’ after Hind Rajab fine paid
World.content:
NBA star Kyrie Irving has opened up about his decision to pay a fine for American football player Azeez Al-Shaair, who was penalised in September for wearing the name of Hind Rajab, a Palestinian girl killed by Israeli forces in Gaza.

“Azeez is a friend of mine,” Irving told reporters, after suffering an opening night 128-110 defeat with Dallas Mavericks in the match against Houston Rockets late on Wednesday.

“He’s a brother that I consider in this revolution this generation is building. It’s a selfless act when you can show up for others who don’t necessarily have a voice for themselves,” said Irving, who has been vocal in his support for Palestine.

Al-Shaair has used his social media accounts and his eyeblack, a tape worn by athletes to reduce glare, to bring attention to the killings of Palestinians in the three years of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

The Black American Muslim player began his current NFL season by wearing Rajab’s name on September 13. The five-year-old girl was killed in Gaza after Israeli soldiers opened fire on her family’s stranded car on January 29, 2024.

For that, Al-Shaair was handed a fine of $11,941 by the National Football League (NFL). Shortly after the fine was announced by an NFL reporter on X, Irving responded to the tweet by saying he would “take care” of it.

“I think we assume that most of us know what’s happening around the world globally,” Irving said on Wednesday. “There are a lot of innocent people who have lost their lives, children especially.



“Us here in America, we get the luxury of going to bed at night in our nice bedrooms, things paid for, but when our tax dollars are going towards other things that we don’t necessarily agree with, then you have to stand up.

“I think small instances of revolutionary acts like wearing people’s names or wearing a child’s name like Hind Rajab on your face and taking a fine and stepping up to the plate, it just shows how much you’re a selfless person, how much you’re willing to sacrifice,” Irving said.

“This mission is bigger than me and Azeez and we know that, but our strength and solidarity and how connected we are and how united we are in our efforts.”

Al-Shaair honours Palestinian children for fifth straight week

Despite being fined and reportedly threatened with removal from games, Al-Shaair has remained undeterred.

When asked, he brushed off the fine regarding Rajab, saying: “It’s bigger to me; what’s a life worth? Is a life worth $11,000? No, I think it’s priceless.”

He has continued to raise awareness about the slain children by wearing a name, or combination of names, every Sunday.

After honouring Rajab, Al-Shaair took the field against the Cincinnati Bengals wearing the name of Wafa Akila, an eight-year-old who was killed along with her father in an Israeli attack in western Gaza as they were making their way home.

In Week 3 against the Indianapolis Colts, Al-Shaair’s eye black had the names of sisters Lana and Bana Ahmad on it. The 12- and eight-year-old girls were killed along with their family in an Israeli air attack in September.

The Houston Texans’ linebacker then wore the name of Amal Abu Khater, 10, who died from gunshot wounds after Israeli forces fired on her in Khan Younis in August.

Al-Shaair’s latest tribute was to slain Palestinian toddler Maryam Ghanem, a two-and-a-half-year-old girl in Gaza who was forced to watch her mother burn alive after an Israeli strike hit their home in the Remal neighbourhood of Gaza City earlier this month.

World.content:

For Israeli teenagers, military life ordinarily kicks off in school. Al Jazeera’s Ava Warriner spoke to Israeli students about the influence the military has on education.

World.title: Pulaku: The two faces of Nigeria’s vigilantes
World.content:
Adamawa State, Nigeria - The night they came for Daniel Musa*, the dogs were barking.

At about 11:30 pm on May 23, 2023, Musa looked out of a window overlooking the gate of his home in Adamawa State, northeastern Nigeria.

The intruders wore all black, like the night. Their faces were uncovered.

Musa, 49, usually left his dogs loose in the compound at night. But the men who had climbed over the fence drove them back into their cage and locked it, clearing a path to the house.

Then they broke the padlock on a smaller gate and moved towards the main door. There, they began trying to force it open with a digger.

Musa, a local pastor, knew they were coming in. Rather than wait for them to break down the door, he opened it himself; he didn’t want any trouble.

He had already told his wife and his then 13-year-old daughter to stay in their bedroom. The men entered his home, pointed a gun at him, and ordered him to sit on the floor.

One went into his bedroom and took money and phones. Another walked to the fridge and helped himself to bread, milk, and water.

Then, at gunpoint, they led Musa out of his home; he did not struggle. He feared that if they did not take him, they might take his wife or daughter instead.

For six hours, Musa walked blindfolded with his captors through bushland, crossing shallow streams until they reached the mountains. There, he heard the familiar voice of his neighbour and discovered he had also been abducted.

He would remain in captivity for three days.

By then, negotiations with his relatives over ransom were under way. The kidnappers demanded 15 million naira (about $11,256 at the time) for his release. But after contacting Musa's family members, they switched off their phones. The family could only reach them when the kidnappers chose to make contact, leaving them unable to negotiate a lower ransom.

Musa, whose name has been changed to protect his identity, says he remained blindfolded throughout his captivity. His only drinking water came from a river, and even then, his captors allowed him just a few sips at a time, whenever they chose.

The captives, still blindfolded, were warned by their abductors that if they detected police officers or vigilantes approaching, they would kill their hostages before attempting to escape.

At about 4am on Friday, gunfire erupted.

For roughly 15 minutes, shots rang out around the camp.

Musa lay on the rocky ground between two other captives, urging them not to move. They could hear voices approaching but had no way of knowing whether they belonged to their abductors or the people trying to rescue them. Were the kidnappers returning? Had the security forces found them? Or were they about to be killed, as their captors had threatened?

“We were confused. We didn’t know who was coming, so I told the others not to move,” he said.

The voices told them not to be afraid, as they removed their blindfolds. Several men stood before them; he can’t recall how many, all dressed in olive-green uniforms.

They belonged to Pulaku, a predominantly Fulani vigilante organisation fighting kidnapping and cattle rustling in northeastern Nigeria. Musa had heard of the group, but this was his first encounter with its members.

The kidnappers had fled, leaving behind food, phones and other belongings. Musa recalled that the rescuers also discovered what appeared to be a national identity card belonging to one of the suspects.

The captives then made their way down the mountain with their rescuers before the police took them to headquarters in Yola, the Adamawa State capital. There, Musa was reunited with his wife and daughter.

He recalls being filled with joy when he saw them again. He credits Pulaku with making that reunion possible.

“They saved my life,” says Musa. His church would later present Pulaku with an award, recognising its work in the community.

But the group’s growing role in fighting kidnapping has also brought the organisation under scrutiny. While some residents credit its members with saving lives, others accuse them of serious abuses. One man says they held him for more than two months and beat him so badly that he lost consciousness.

The two accounts reveal the uneasy place occupied by armed community vigilantes in a region where formal security forces have struggled to contain kidnapping and cattle rustling.

World.title: Hamilton calls for Palestine and DR Congo freedom as Rwanda takes F1 spotlight
World.content:
Rwanda’s controversial Formula One GP leads Lewis Hamilton to call for freedom for DR Congo, while renewing Palestine plea.

Seven-time Formula One champion Lewis Hamilton has renewed his call for freedom for Palestine when pressed on the controversial decision to award a Grand Prix to Rwanda.

The 41-year-old is the only Black competitor in the motorsport and said an African race would make people more aware of the continent, but recognised there were concerns and used the issue to expand on his stance on humanitarian issues across the world.

Human rights campaigners Amnesty International recently accused Formula One of hollow words and offering Rwanda a “sportswashing prize” – an accusation levelled at countries perceived to be using sport to improve a tarnished image abroad.

Hamilton, who was speaking before Sunday’s US Grand Prix, has long called for a Gaza ceasefire amid Israel’s genocidal war and returned to the matter – as well as other conflicts – when asked about a Grand Prix in Rwanda.

“I think we need to make sure we’re pushing to free Congo, free Sudan, free Syria, free Palestine,” Hamilton said.

“There’s a lot of peace that I’m hoping we get to at some stage.”

Rwanda in the spotlight after Formula One GP award

Rwanda President Paul Kagame has been accused of repressive methods to keep his grip on power, with opponents dying in prisons, independent media muzzled, and other abuses.

Neighbouring Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) joined the criticism of Formula One’s decision to award a race to Rwanda, which is accused by the DRC, the United States and United Nations experts of backing the M23 rebels fighting in the DRC.



“Of course, I don’t get to choose where we go,” Hamilton continued.

“Naturally, there are problems all over the world today, so I’ve seen many of the stories. But I think we really have to approach it with humility.

“Of course, going there doesn’t mean that you neglect the things that are happening there.

“So hopefully many people start to educate themselves a little bit more about what is happening there and what has happened there for hundreds of years. I hope that does spark the conversation.

“Growing up in England, they never taught us anything about Africa. It needs to be on the curriculum.

“A lot of the problems they have there are still results of colonialism and the West intervening.”

Formula One’s return to Africa has been Hamilton’s dream

Hamilton said a race in Africa was a dream that could keep him going longer in the sport now that Formula One has done a deal with Rwanda for a Grand Prix in the early 2030s.

The Ferrari driver will be 42 in January and has a contract for 2027. Fernando Alonso, the oldest active F1 driver, is 45 and recently signed up for another season with Aston Martin.

“I’m now forced to stay a lot longer because we have a race in Africa, and that’s been my dream, to be able to race in Africa,” Hamilton said on Thursday in a news conference alongside championship leader Kimi Antonelli.

“I have to keep fighting to try and stay fit. If I can still punch out good results over the next year, we’ll keep it going.”

Antonelli, who replaced Hamilton at Mercedes last season and is still only 20 years old, encouraged him: “You got to do at least the first one.”

Hamilton, the sport’s first and only Black champion, has long campaigned for a race in Africa – a continent that last hosted a race at South Africa’s Kyalami circuit in 1993 – and spoke of his efforts.

“Countless meetings with the stakeholders, so many meetings with (F1 CEO) Stefano (Domenicali) at his office in London, but also on race weekends, countless calls: ‘What’s happening? Where are we going? Who are you meeting with?’

“Many meetings with different presidents from different countries. Lots of phone calls with different presidents from different countries within Africa,” he recalled.

“I think for me, it’s a place that deserves to have a Grand Prix. It’s about more than just one country. It’s about the continent itself.”

World.title: Ukraine says Starlink still restricted after Trump says limits lifted
World.content:
Ukraine is still recording issues with the Starlink network, sources within the defence ministry say, after Donald Trump said limits on the satellite uplink had been reversed by Elon Musk.

The sources told the BBC that instances of drones experiencing connection loss at speeds of 161km/h (100mph) were being recorded, hampering military operations.

The US president had denied instructing the tech billionaire to restrict connectivity to Starlink's military-grade counterpart, Starshield, before saying on Thursday that Musk had "put it back".

Musk previously said he was not behind the slowdown, which affected Ukraine's ability to use attack drones and co-ordinate defensive operations.

The Ukrainian defence ministry sources said the military was constantly monitoring the performance of both the Starlink and Starshield networks.

They added that there was "currently no confirmation that these restrictions have been lifted".

Last week, Kyiv said uplink speeds to the low Earth orbit satellites had been restricted, affecting the speed at which drones could travel. Any drone travelling faster than 100mph lost its connection, officials said.

Shortly after, Musk said that Starshield, which Ukraine uses for some of its operation, was controlled by the US military and suggested that the Pentagon could be behind the issues.

The White House has since repeatedly denied deliberately placing limits on the network in Ukraine.

Trump refused to say whether he had called Musk to ask him to lift restrictions to the service when asked about reports to that end on Thursday, but said: "Bottom line, he put it back."

World.title: Five Israelis wounded and two suspected Palestinian attackers killed in West Bank shooting
World.content:
Five Israelis have been wounded and two suspected Palestinian attackers killed by Israeli security forces following a shooting in the occupied West Bank, Israeli officials say.

Footage verified by the BBC shows an intense gun battle between soldiers and the gunmen, at a military checkpoint at the entrance to the city of Hebron.

In response, Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he had ordered the military to prepare for a full lockdown of the West Bank, beginning later on Friday.

The attack comes at a time of high tensions, with extremist Jewish settlers targeting Palestinians during the annual olive harvest, and Israel's general election taking place in four days time.

The two injured Israelis are in critical condition, according to Israel's ambulance service.

The Israeli military said it had found a large quantity of ammunition in the attackers' vehicle, and that they believe the gunmen had intended to carry out a much larger attack on the nearby Route 35, but ran into the checkpoint - so instead decided to open fire there.

Unverified CCTV footage shows two gunmen exit a car armed with what appears to be a handgun and an assault rifle and start firing on soldiers at the checkpoint, before coming under return fire.

The Israeli military said it had begun raids on the homes of the attackers, while far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said he had ordered the demolition of several Palestinian buildings adjacent to the site of the attack.

It is common practice for Israeli forces to demolish the homes of Palestinians who are suspected of carrying out attacks on Israelis.

Netanyahu, who has built his election campaign on promising security for Israelis, said that his Likud party would cancel campaign events for the morning.

The West Bank was already expected to be placed under lockdown for the election on Monday and Tuesday, according to Israeli media.

At least 96 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers in the West Bank since the start of the year, according to the UN.

Four Israelis, both security forces and civilians, have been killed by Palestinians there over the same period, the UN says.

World.title: Hundreds of flights cancelled as Typhoon Champi shuts Taiwan
World.content:
Hundreds of flights in the East Asia region were cancelled on Friday as powerful Typhoon Champi roared close to Taiwan's north-east coast.

Schools and offices in Taiwan were shut as Champi neared the island. While it is uncertain if it will make landfall, the storm was forecast to bring 90cm (35in) of rain and strong winds to the north-east until Saturday.

One person died after being swept away by waves, authorities said. The storm also injured 171 people and forced 1,000 others to evacuate.

Champi is the latest in a string of intense typhoons as a Super El NiÃ±o heats up the Pacific Ocean and fuels storms. At its peak earlier this week, it was the planet's strongest storm of the year so far.

On Friday afternoon, Champi was packing wind gusts of 191km/h (119mph) .

After passing Taiwan's north-eastern tip and the Okinawa islands in southern Japan, Champi is expected to hover over the waters off China's eastern coast, before curving farther to the north-east to Japan's main island.

Weather agencies in Taiwan, Hong Kong and Japan forecast that the eye of the storm is expected to pass without making landfall in Taiwan.

However, a forecaster in Taiwan's Central Weather Administration told Reuters that they could not rule this out completely - especially if the storm "stalls, loops or wobbles from side to side" as it approaches.

World.title: At least one dead and four injured in Paris suburb shooting
World.content:
One person has been killed and at least four others injured in a Parisian suburb, in what police are treating as a "terrorist incident".

French Prime Minister SÃ©bastien Lecornu said the "very serious events" happened in Trappes, to the west of Paris, adding that the suspected attacker had been "apprehended and placed in police custody".

The National Anti-Terrorist Prosecutor's Office (PNAT) said it had taken on the investigation into the incident, which appeared to be "murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise".

Reports in French media suggest the number of injured may be higher and that a 12-year-old child may be among them.

The Mayor of Trappes, Ali Rabeh, said that "an individual fired shots from his vehicle at several people he encountered" on Friday morning.

World.title: Cyprus police open investigation into financial affairs of Roman Abramovich
World.content:
Police in Cyprus have opened an investigation into the financial affairs of Roman Abramovich, following revelations by BBC Panorama that accountancy firm Deloitte helped in falsifying documents to hide his wealth and evade tax.

Serious questions about the integrity of some of Abramovich's professional advisers were raised earlier this month in a joint report from the BBC and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism (TBIJ).

A Cypriot Ministry of Justice official told MPs this week that the report's findings would be looked at as part of a new investigation by the police's Financial Intelligence Unit.

Lawyers for Abramovich have said that he denies evading tax or concealing his fortune. Deloitte Cyprus said it acts "in compliance with applicable laws".

The police investigation was announced at a parliamentary committee meeting in the Cypriot capital, Nicosia, held to discuss the combating and prevention of money laundering.

The Ministry of Justice official told MPs the police would try to determine whether any criminal acts had been committed.

Last week, the report from the BBC and TBIJ detailed how accounts signed off by Deloitte in Cyprus in 2006 meant assets such as superyachts, mansions and private jets worth $672m (Â£508m) vanished from Abramovich's company accounts.

Deloitte, which is the world's largest accountancy firm, also appears to have advised on a scheme to evade a huge tax bill on the oligarch's wealth, through the falsification of documents.

World.title: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds
World.content:
The attacks culminated in an RSF raid on 8 June. Hospital staff were taken by surprise - many of them escaped over the back wall as the RSF fighters entered the building, says Dr Mustafa Ahmed, a pharmaceutical specialist.

But the director general of the hospital, surgeon Izzeldin Ahmed Dawaud Asow, encountered a group of the paramilitaries outside his office.

They did not know he was a doctor, he said, but denounced him with ethnic slurs.

"There are no citizens here. You are Falangi," they said, using a derogatory term implying that non-Arab Sudanese are foreigners.

Dr Asow says he was beaten with rifle butts and lost consciousness at one point. Ultimately, he saved himself by pretending to be dead.

"They put their hand on my chest, and I stopped breathing. And they said: 'Leave him, leave him. The rubbish has died. Leave him.' They left me."

That same day the RSF was driven out by the Sudanese military and its allies and Dr Asow returned to find the bodies of several patients and the surgical equipment in his operating room thoroughly destroyed, he said.

The hospital closed and later fell into RSF hands when the army retreated.

Dr Nugud, a prominent Sudanese surgeon who has joined the RSF-backed civilian government as health minister, insisted the South Hospital was being used as a military base.

According to international law, hospitals can lose their protection if they are used by a party to the conflict to commit an "act harmful to the enemy".

In an interview with the BBC, Dr Nugud declared that missile launchers were set up on the grounds and shared a video showing remains of weapons filmed more than a year after the hospital closed, which he said supported his claim.

He also showed us what he called maps of landmines planted around the Teaching Hospital, which is located next to Sudanese military headquarters.

Doctors told us the hospital was not incorporated into the base and said they visited it to pick up medical equipment during the war.

The BBC has found no independent evidence of Dr Nugud's allegations. And the government of the Darfur region categorically rejected the charges.

After the South Hospital shut, its staff and remaining equipment were moved to the Saudi Maternity Hospital in the west of the city, where the army had its main bases.

Within days the pace of attacks on the facility picked up. At this stage the medical charity MÃ©decins Sans FrontiÃ¨res (MSF) sounded the alarm.

"We do not know if hospitals are being intentionally targeted, butâ¦ the belligerents are not taking any precautions to spare them," it said in a statement.

However, in the course of our investigation we spoke to six doctors who described a pattern of systematic targeting.

They told us how Saudi Hospital was repeatedly struck - on some days up to 25 times, with a mix of shelling and drones, the latter "intelligent rockets" with precision-guided attacks.

Smaller medical facilities also came under fire. The BBC's timeline records the steady closure of private hospitals and neighbourhood clinics.

Furthermore, when some of these healthcare buildings shifted locations, the alternate venues were also attacked.

The Specialised Children's Hospital, which shut down at the beginning of the war along with the Teaching Hospital, moved to two other locations, both of which were then shelled and forced to close.

Similarly, the main dialysis centre was struck and then attacked again after it relocated.

World.title: Woman with Ebola in Nigeria confirmed as wife of Swiss diplomat
World.content:
She returned to Nigeria on 3 October after spending about two and a half weeks in Uganda.

The patient did ânot travel to DR Congo, the Swiss âgovernment told Reuters news agency on Friday, contradicting accounts from Uganda.

She developed symptoms four days after arriving in Abuja and sought treatment at two private health facilities before testing positive for Ebola on 20 October.

Health officials are now investigating whether she may have crossed paths with a Kenyan man who died from Ebola and had travelled through Uganda's main airport on the same day.

Investigators are examining whether they could have been exposed through shared equipment or other contact, the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) said on Thursday.

Dr Wessam Mankoula, the agency's head of emergency preparedness and response, said this was "one of the possible scenarios", but stressed that no link had been established.

The Kenyan man had travelled from DR Congo through Uganda before arriving in Nairobi on 3 October. He died shortly afterwards, becoming Kenya's first recorded Ebola death.

Kenya has since confirmed eight other cases of Ebola.

The WHO said it was too early to determine where the woman in Nigeria became infected.

"The source of exposure is still not known. The travel history of the patient is still being pieced together," said Dr Patrick Otim, a WHO emergency response official.

He said investigators had struggled to obtain a complete account of her movements because opportunities to interview her were limited while she remained in hospital.

Nigeria's Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said it was carrying out genomic sequencing, which could help establish whether her infection is linked to other cases. However, it has been confirmed that she has the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, the same one which has caused the outbreak in DR Congo.

"The investigation is reconstructing the full travel and exposure history. Genomic sequencing is given a high priority," said Dr Pavel Ursu, the WHO's representative in Nigeria.

Ugandan health officials previously said the woman had travelled to eastern DR Congo for business.

However, the WHO, Africa CDC and Nigeria's health ministry said they had not received verified information confirming that she had visited the country.

Uganda has maintained that it has no confirmed active Ebola cases and says the woman's travel through the country does not necessarily mean she contracted the virus there.

Meanwhile, Nigerian authorities are tracing more people who may have been exposed to the woman, beyond the 44 contacts initially identified.

Kenya's Health Director-General Dr Patrick Amoth said all nine confirmed infections were linked to the first patient, with no evidence of wider community transmission.

He urged the public to remain vigilant and not panic but warned: "We are not out of the woods".

He said the surviving eight patients were still in isolation and responding well to treatment.

The developments have renewed concerns about the movement of infected people across international borders, particularly between DR Congo and neighbouring Uganda, where thousands cross daily for trade, work and family visits.

Dr Otim warned that the long and porous border between the two countries made it difficult to screen everyone entering or leaving, as many people used unofficial crossing points.

The WHO's regional director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, called for "regional vigilance" and urged countries to strengthen surveillance, investigate infections and protect frontline health workers.

Ebola is a serious viral disease that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person, or with contaminated objects. It does not spread through the air like flu.

The virus can cause fever, severe weakness, vomiting and diarrhoea, and can be fatal. People are not considered infectious before they develop symptoms.

Health authorities say tracing contacts quickly, isolating suspected cases and providing early treatment are crucial to preventing further transmission.

World.title: Powerful earthquake hits Tibet killing 16 people, reports say
World.content:
A magnitude 7.0 earthquake has hit a mountainous region in Tibet, killing at least 16 people and injuring dozens, according to Chinese state media.

The centre of the quake hit BaqÃªn County in the Nagqu region on Thursday night, Xinhua reported, citing the local emergency management bureau.

The county - located in what China calls the Tibet Autonomous Region after annexing it in the 1950s - is 400km (250 miles) north-east of the region's capital, Lhasa.

Authorities have declared the incident an emergency and deployed rescue teams to the affected area, where 65 others have been injured, including 11 people with severe injuries.

The electricity supply has been cut off and 339 homes have collapsed in the affected region, though by Friday morning there were reports of power restored in some areas.

Local media said more than 12,400 people had been relocated following the earthquake.

Rockfall has forced roads in the region to close, making it more difficult for crews to reach impacted high-altitude areas.

The US Geological Survey (USGS) has recorded seven tremors close to the epicentre, all of which are located in the mountainous region. The largest tremor was recorded at 5.2 magnitude at a depth of 10km.

Shallow earthquakes and tremors closer to the Earth's surface are more damaging than deep quakes.

World.title: Ebola: Nigerian govt urges 15 states to speed up preparedness
World.content:
The federal government has urged 15 states to speed up preparedness as Nigeria steps up measures to contain the country’s first confirmed imported case of Ebola disease.

The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, made the call on Thursday while briefing the National Economic Council (NEC) on Nigeria’s response to the Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

Mr Pate said 21 states had already updated their Ebola response plans, while the remaining 15 states are expected to expedite the establishment of appropriate preparedness and response mechanisms, Voice of Nigeria reports.

The minister identified coordination and governance, detection at points of entry, laboratory testing capacity, logistics for essential medical supplies and personal protective equipment, and effective communication as key components of the national response.

The development comes as the federal government continues to strengthen preparedness following confirmation of an imported Ebola case in Abuja.

States strengthen response

At the NEC meeting, Mr Pate said Nigeria is working to operationalise a robust national response system involving federal and state authorities.

The minister said the government had already informed all state governments about the situation, while most states had response plans developed with guidance from the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC).

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the government is working to ensure that the remaining states strengthened their preparedness.

Mr Pate said the government is coordinating with the World Health Organisation (WHO), Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) and other technical partners.

He also said Nigeria is strengthening its surveillance at points of entry and working to ensure that existing screening capacity, including thermal imaging equipment, was functional.

No restrictions on gatherings

Speaking later on Thursday at a ministerial press briefing in Abuja, Mr Pate said there are no restrictions on large gatherings for now.

He said there is currently no indication to alter the course of planned large gatherings.

“At this moment there is no indication that requires us to alter the course of large gatherings that have been planned,” he said.

He, however, said the government could review the decision if the situation changed.

“But if the situation changes, we would make a determination, we would consult broadly with the right experts and make that determination,” he said.

Mr Pate said such decisions would be based on scientific evidence and public health considerations.

Patient showing improvement

The minister also disclosed that the confirmed Ebola patient was recovering, with laboratory results showing improvement.

He said he had spoken with the clinicians treating the patient and that there was a possibility she would recover.

“Thankfully, that individual is being taken care of and in fact is recovering. Today I spoke to the clinicians and I understand that lab results are showing great improvement and there is a possibility that she will recover from this,” Mr Pate said.

Government urges calm

At the ministerial briefing, Mr Pate urged Nigerians to remain vigilant but said there is no need for panic.

He advised people to follow basic public health measures, including regular hand washing and avoiding unnecessary contact with bodily fluids.

He also urged people experiencing symptoms such as fever, headache and muscle aches, particularly those with a relevant travel history, to isolate themselves and promptly notify public health authorities.

Hospitals have also been directed to prepare isolation beds and strengthen infection prevention and control measures, while private health facilities have been urged to promptly notify public health authorities of suspected cases.

World.title: Seven dead, 11 injured in Gombe road crash
World.content:
Seven people, including three children, have died, while 11 others sustained injuries in a multiple-vehicle accident at Kumo in Akko Local Government Area of Gombe State.

The crash, which occurred at Tashan Magariya Junction along the Gombe–Billiri road at about 5:30 p.m. on Thursday, involved a heavy-duty truck, two Volkswagen Golf cars and five motorcycles.

An incident report by the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) attributed the accident to suspected brake failure, which reportedly caused the truck driver to lose control while travelling from Gombe towards Yola.

The truck subsequently collided with the two cars and five motorcycles, bringing the total number of vehicles involved to eight.

According to the report, the deceased comprised four adult men, two boys and a girl.

The 11 injured victims included four adult men, three adult women and four girls. They reportedly suffered various injuries, including severe fractures, cuts and bruises.

Although the FRSC recorded 25 people as being involved in the accident, the report did not provide details about the condition of the remaining seven individuals.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The agency said its personnel received an emergency call at 5:32 p.m. and reached the scene two minutes later.

The injured victims were taken to the Federal Medical Centre in Kumo for medical attention, while 11 people reportedly received first aid.

The vehicles involved in the crash were subsequently handed over to the Motor Traffic Division of the Nigeria Police Force in Kumo for further investigation and necessary action.

The identities of the deceased and the latest medical conditions of the injured victims were not immediately known.

The suspected mechanical failure that triggered the crash highlights the dangers faulty vehicles pose to motorists, motorcyclists and other road users.

World.title: 2027: Governor Namadi to lead Jigawa APC campaign council
World.content:
The Jigawa State Chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has formally constituted its State Campaign Council as part of strategic measures to consolidate party structures, deepen grassroots mobilisation, and secure victory in the forthcoming 2027 General Elections.

The establishment of the council followed extensive consultations with party leaders across the state’s three senatorial districts and was approved by the APC State Working Committee.

Announcing the composition in a statement, APC Jigawa State Chairman, Ahmed Garba, disclosed that Governor Umar Namadi will serve as Chairman of the State Campaign Council.

To support the chairman and ensure broad-based leadership, four Deputy Chairmen were named: the deputy governor of the state, Aminu Usman; former Governor, Ali Sa’adu Birnin Kudu; former Governor, Saminu Turaki; and the APC State Chairman, Ahmed Garba.

To ensure equitable political representation and effective coordination across all zones, six Vice Chairmen were appointed to represent the three senatorial districts of Jigawa: Jigawa North-East: Muhammad Ibrahim (Vice Chairman I); Ibrahim Hassan Hadejia (Vice Chairman II) Jigawa South-West: Haruna Aliyu Dangyatin (Vice Chairman I) and Farouk Adamu Aliyu (Vice Chairman II) as well as Jigawa North-West: Isa Gerawa (Vice Chairman I) and Hajia Rabi Ishaq (Vice Chairman II).

Also, Lawan Yau Roni has been appointed Director-General of the Campaign Council. In this role, he will oversee the day-to-day coordination and execution of the campaign’s programme across the state.

According to the party leadership, the Campaign Council is tasked with providing strategic direction, coordinating campaign activities, and deepening engagement with supporters across all 27 Local Government Areas of Jigawa State.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Garba emphasised that the team’s composition reflects the APC’s commitment to unity, inclusion, and collective leadership.

He urged all council members, party stakeholders, and loyalists to work with discipline and shared purpose to deliver a decisive victory at the polls.

World.title: El Clásico: UNILAG to host watch party as Barcelona face Real Madrid
World.content:
The University of Lagos (UNILAG) will host a watch party on Sunday for the first El Clásico of the 2026/27 season, as Barcelona look to strengthen their position at the top of LaLiga against arch-rivals Real Madrid.

The watch party organised by StarTimes and Meridianbet will hold at King Jaja Hall begining from 6 p.m., ahead of the 9 p.m. kick-off.

It will feature entertainment, fan activities and giveaways, with supporters expected to attend in their preferred club colours.

StarTimes Nigeria Marketing Director, Oke Umurhohwo, said the event would give supporters an opportunity to watch the match together.

“Football is more exciting when fans experience it together, and few matches generate as much passion as El Clásico. At StarTimes, we want to go beyond broadcasting the game to creating opportunities for fans to connect, celebrate their clubs and enjoy the excitement of football in a memorable atmosphere.

“Our partnership with Meridianbet allows us to bring this experience closer to football lovers at UNILAG, combining live football, entertainment and fan engagement in one exciting evening,” he said.

Sunday’s encounter at Barcelona’s Spotify Camp Nou carries early implications for the LaLiga title race. Barcelona have won all nine of their league matches and lead Real Madrid by six points.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

READ ALSO: Barcelona seal LaLiga title as StarTimes watch party electrifies UNILAG

A victory would extend Barcelona’s advantage to nine points, while a Real Madrid win would cut the gap to three.

Barcelona head into the fixture after their winning run across competitions was ended by Paris Saint-Germain, who beat them 4-2 in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday. The defeat did not affect their perfect league record but adds another test ahead of their meeting with their biggest rivals.

Real Madrid will aim to capitalise on Barcelona’s European setback, close the gap at the top and gain an advantage in the title race.

While entry to the UNILAG watch party is free, the match will also be broadcasted on StarTimes Sports channels.

World.title: Angry youths protest alleged killing of entertainer by police
World.content:
There was outrage in Enugu State on Thursday when several angry youths protested alleged extrajudicial killing of a popular entertainer, Izuchukwu Nnaji, in the state.

The protesters, who carried placards with various inscriptions alleged Mr Nnaji, otherwise known as ‘Stone,’ was killed by operatives of the Anti-Cult Tactical Squad in the state.

PREMIUM TIMES gathered that the late Nnaji was arrested around 3 a.m. on Wednesday at The Bull Hotel in Enugu where he had lodged after celebrating his birthday with friends on Tuesday night.

Some of the youths said Mr Nnaji’s body was later discovered at the morgue of the Enugu State University Teaching Hospital, Parklane, on Thursday, prompting the youths to begin the protest.

Video clips showing the youths protesting have been circulating on Facebook.

In one of the clips, the protesters called for the arrest of the police operatives allegedly involved in the killing of the deceased.

They also demanded an investigation into the killing.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Ogochukwu Nnaji, the elder brother of the deceased, told reporters during the protest that his brother was allegedly arrested and killed without justification.

“My brother celebrated his birthday on Tuesday and thereafter lodged at The Bull Hotel.

“Operatives of the police anti-cult squad invaded his hotel room around 3 a.m. on Wednesday and whisked him away.

“When we could not find him, we went to the hotel, where the management confirmed that operatives of the anti-cult unit came in the night and took him away. We later traced his body to the ESUT Parklane morgue today (Thursday),” he narrated.

Mr Ogochukwu insisted that the deceased was “extrajudicially killed” and that he was neither a cultist nor an armed robber.

“He was a well-known celebrity. We are demanding justice,” he said.

The protesters later marched to the Government House in Enugu, calling for the arrest and prosecution of those involved in the killing of the deceased.

Police silent

The police spokesperson in Enugu State, Daniel Ndukwe, did not respond to multiple calls and a text message seeking his comments on Friday morning.

Not the first time

The latest incident occurred about 24 months after a police inspector killed a popular musician, Chikezie Mba, in Enugu State.

Mr Mba, popularly known as ‘Igbo Jah,’ was shot dead by the inspector at the Anti-Cult Unit of the Enugu State Police Command in October 2024.

The police authorities later identified the inspector as Joseph Ozonwanji, dismissed and arraigned him for killing the musician.

World.title: Minister gives update on Immigration, Civil Defence, Fire Service recruitments, promotions
World.content:
The Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, says more than 27,000 personnel across Nigeria’s four paramilitary services have been approved for promotion.

Mr Tunji-Ojo also said the recruitment portal would open from 28 October to 13 November for candidates who reached the oral interview stage.

He disclosed this in a Facebook post on Friday after a meeting of the Civil Defence, Correctional, Fire and Immigration Services Board (CDCFIB).

The minister said the board had also validated a healthcare policy framework to improve the health and welfare of personnel across the services.

He stated that the federal government remained committed to recruiting 120,000 young Nigerians into the services during President Bola Tinubu’s first term. The current recruitment exercise covers the first batch of 30,000 candidates.

The four services are the Nigeria Immigration Service, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Federal Fire Service and Nigerian Correctional Service.

The latest promotions follow an exercise in December 2025, when the board approved the promotion of 24,202 senior officers across the four agencies. The Correctional Service accounted for 11,426 promotions, the Civil Defence Corps 5,859, the Immigration Service 4,336 and the Fire Service 2,581.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Tunji-Ojo said the latest approval brought the number of personnel promoted across the services since Mr Tinubu assumed office in 2023 to more than 100,000.

He said more than 32,000 officers were promoted in 2023, over 20,000 in 2024 and more than 24,000 in 2025, while over 27,000 were approved for promotion in 2026.

In August 2025, the minister said the government had cleared the backlog of promotions across the services, with more than 50,000 officers promoted within two years.

Read the full statement below.

At the meeting of the Civil Defence, Correctional, Fire and Immigration Services Board (CDCFIB) today, we made far-reaching decisions to improve career progress and welfare of personnel across our paramilitary agencies.

In a historic step to boost morale and recognise meritorious service, the Board approved the promotion of over 27,000 officers across our four services. To further support our workforce, we validated a comprehensive healthcare policy framework designed to promote the health, fitness, and overall well-being of all officers and men.

On recruitment, we reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to enlist 120,000 young Nigerians into our paramilitary services over our first tenure. The process for the first tranche of 30,000 candidates has advanced, with the portal opening from 28th October to 13th November 2026 for those who have reached the oral interview stage.

Apparently, with this latest exercise, total promotions across the paramilitary agencies under the Ministry of Interior since His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR assumed office now stand at well over 100,000 officers. This comprises over 32,000 officers promoted in 2023, over 20,000 in 2024, more than 24,000 in 2025, and the just concluded over 27,000 approved today in 2026.

In the Ministry of Interior, this sustained record reflects the Renewed Hope Agenda’s unwavering commitment to ending career stagnation and building a well-motivated, disciplined, and fit workforce capable of discharging its constitutional responsibilities effectively.

World.title: APC youth leader, wife abducted in Kogi
World.content:
An All Progressives Congress (APC) youth leader in Kogi State, Arome Adaji, and his wife, Justina, have been kidnapped from their residence in Abocho, Dekina Local Government Area.

The incident reportedly occurred around 8 p.m. on Wednesday when armed men stormed the couple’s residence along Ajegwuna Road, shooting and forcing neighbours to flee.

A resident, who identified himself as Ndamodu, said Mr Adaji, also known as Iron Gate, and his wife were at home when gunshots rang out around their residence, Daily Trust reported.

“The sound of gunshots scared residents from coming out, as no one wanted to be caught in either crossfire or stray bullets,” he said.

According to him, residents came out after the attackers had left and discovered that the couple had been taken away.

A community leader, Surveyor Eneogba, said kidnappers had increasingly targeted homes, farms and farm settlements in communities across Kogi East.

He said security operatives, vigilantes and local hunters had intensified surveillance along roads, forcing armed groups to shift their activities to residential areas and farms.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“For weeks now, the armed hoodlums have scaled down activities on roads, focusing on residences and farms or farm settlements where they are abducting people at an alarming rate,” he said.

The latest abduction comes amid reports of other kidnapping incidents in the area.

A few weeks ago, armed men reportedly abducted a woman and her four children as they returned from a burial ceremony.

The victims were later released after a ransom was paid, according to accounts from the community.

Related incidents

The abduction also comes weeks after the reported kidnapping and death of Rosemary Adukwu, a councillor representing Ogugu Ward III in Olamaboro Local Government Area of Kogi State.

READ ALSO: Three sentenced to death for kidnapping Catholic priests

Ms Adukwu was reportedly abducted on 30 September while travelling to Onitsha, with gunmen intercepting the commercial vehicle in which she was travelling around the Oji River axis, near the Enugu-Anambra boundary.

Olamaboro Local Government Chairman Ameh Williams later announced that she had died while in captivity.

Her death and the latest abduction have heightened concerns about the safety of residents and travellers in parts of Kogi State.

When contacted for comment on the abduction of Mr Adaji and his wife, the spokesperson for the Kogi State Police Command, Saliu Oyiza Afusat, responded, “Noted.” She did not provide further details.

World.title: Three sentenced to death for kidnapping Catholic priests
World.content:
An Adamawa State High Court has sentenced three men to death for kidnapping two Catholic priests in February 2025.

Christopher Mapeo delivered the judgement on Thursday, convicting Taledo Demiel, Namomai Medan and Mikaila Yusuf over the abduction of Reverend Fathers Matthew Dutsemi and Abraham Sauman.

The defendants were found guilty of offences including criminal conspiracy to commit kidnapping, kidnapping, conspiracy to commit armed robbery, armed robbery, harbouring a kidnapped person and negotiating to receive ransom for the priests’ release.

The priests were abducted from their residence in Gwaida-Malam, Numan Local Government Area of Adamawa State, in the early hours of 22 February 2025.

The police confirmed the abduction at the time and said the state Commissioner of Police had directed security operatives to rescue the victims and apprehend the kidnappers.

The State Security Service (SSS) said the judgement brought to seven the number of death sentences secured by the service in 2026.

According to reports on the SSS statement, the latest judgement followed several other capital convictions secured in different states this year in cases involving kidnapping, terrorism and other serious offences.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

On 20 May, an Ekiti State High Court sentenced Ibrahim Abubakar and Abdullahi Abubakar to death for kidnapping.

On 3 June, a Federal High Court in Abuja sentenced four men to death by hanging over their involvement in the June 2022 attack on St Francis Catholic Church in Owo, Ondo State, which killed scores of worshippers.

A Katsina State High Court sentenced Hauwa’u Mukhtar to death on 15 June, while a Kogi State High Court sentenced Jibrin Halilu to death the following day for kidnapping and murdering his neighbour.

On 22 June, a Sokoto State High Court sentenced three men — Muhammed Yusuf Sallau, Jabbi Ahlaji Yale and Kabiru Muhammed — to death for terrorism-related offences and transporting arms.

On 28 September, another Sokoto State High Court sentenced Ibrahim Usman, also known as Dan Iyali, to death over his involvement in the killing of three kidnapped persons.

The Adamawa judgement adds to the growing number of capital convictions recorded in Nigeria as security agencies pursue prosecutions over kidnapping and other violent crimes.

World.title: Kane edges out Yamal to win award 3 days ahead of Ballon d’Or ceremony
World.content:
Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has beaten Barcelona youngster Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé to emerge as the best player of the 2025-2026 season in Spanish newspaper Marca’s annual Top 100 Players ranking, just few days to the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony.

Kane claimed the top spot in the ranking released on Friday, three days before the Ballon d’Or ceremony, with Yamal finishing second and Mbappé taking third place.

The annual ranking, Marca’s Top 100 Players, was compiled with input from a panel of more than 200 former players, journalists and analysts from around the world, who assessed performances for club and country throughout the season.

Manchester City midfielder Rodri finished fourth, followed by Paris Saint-Germain winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in fifth place.

Inter Miami captain Lionel Messi occupied sixth position, ahead of Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Fabián Ruiz, who came seventh.

Bayern Munich’s Michael Olise finished eighth, while his France teammate Ousmane Dembélé, also of PSG, placed ninth.

Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsí completed the top 10.

Bellingham finishes ahead of Vinícius

Real Madrid’s leading players were spread across the ranking, with England midfielder Jude Bellingham finishing 15th, ahead of Brazilian forward Vinícius Júnior, who placed 22nd.

Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois came 28th, while Turkish midfielder Arda Güler finished 47th.

Portugal captain Cristiano Ronaldo, who plays for Saudi Arabian club Al-Nassr, secured 33rd position, while his teammate João Félix finished 70th.

Barcelona stars feature prominently

Barcelona had several players among the top-ranked performers, with Brazilian winger Raphinha finishing 13th and Spanish midfielder Pedri occupying 14th place.

Ferran Torres came 17th, while Dani Olmo finished 21st.

Barcelona goalkeeper Joan García placed 42nd, with defender Eric García coming in at 55th.

Paris Saint-Germain also recorded a strong showing, with three players in the top 10: Kvaratskhelia, Fabián Ruiz and Dembélé.

Moroccan defender Achraf Hakimi finished 20th, while Vitinha, Nuno Mendes, João Neves, Marquinhos and Willian Pacho also featured in the ranking.

The list included players competing outside Europe’s major leagues, with Messi representing Inter Miami in Major League Soccer and Ronaldo featuring for Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia.

Kane’s position at the top of the ranking places the England international ahead of several high-profile contenders for individual honours as attention turns to the Ballon d’Or ceremony on Monday.

Marca’s Top 10

1.Harry Kane — Bayern Munich

2. Lamine Yamal — Barcelona

3. Kylian Mbappé — Real Madrid

4. Rodri — Manchester City

5. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia — Paris Saint-Germain

6. Lionel Messi — Inter Miami

7. Fabián Ruiz — Paris Saint-Germain

8. Michael Olise — Bayern Munich

9. Ousmane Dembélé — Paris Saint-Germain

10. Pau Cubarsí — Barcelona
