Taiwan — typhoon closures · transport halt Japan — flight cancellations · inflation pressure South Korea — tech sell-off · risk aversion China — market anxiety · disaster response North Korea — threat signalling · silence

Asia’s temper on Friday is one of forced pause and defensive calculation, as a typhoon shuts down Taiwan’s air links and schools while investors retreat from technology and artificial-intelligence valuations. The region is not expanding or asserting itself today; it is battening down, counting cancellations and waiting for the next data point or official word.

The register is administrative and precautionary: Taiwan’s transport ministry lists cancelled flights, Japanese carriers warn of multi-day disruption, and central banks and markets speak through numbers rather than declarations. Leaders are managing exposure to weather, to rate expectations, to North Korean signalling, with the clipped language of logistics and risk control.

The through-line is vulnerability made visible: a storm exposes the fragility of East Asian connectivity, while falling technology shares expose the region’s dependence on an artificial-intelligence investment cycle that no longer feels assured. What leaders fear today is not a single adversary but the compounding of small disruptions into a broader loss of confidence.

Key Facts —Taiwan transport. Typhoon Champi cancelled 262 domestic and more than 350 international flights on 23 October. —Japan flights. More than 100 flights were cancelled between 22 and 25 October, affecting over 11,000 passengers. —South Korea equities. South Korean shares fell more than 2 per cent on 23 October as technology losses extended. —Japan inflation. Japanese inflation data released on 23 October strengthened expectations of another Bank of Japan rate increase. —China market. The CSI 300 entered a bear market after falling more than 20 per cent from its June peak.

Taiwan: The Storm As A Stress Test

Typhoon Champi has prompted Taiwan to close schools, offices and financial markets while cancelling more than six hundred flights in a single day. For a US reader, the closures are a reminder that Taiwan’s outsized role in semiconductors and global logistics rests on an island exposed to severe weather. The storm is weakening and not forecast to make direct landfall, yet the precautionary shutdown still ripples through regional aviation and cargo schedules.

Japan: Inflation Anxiety Meets Weather Disruption

Japan is absorbing a double pressure: more than one hundred flight cancellations linked to Champi and inflation data that revived expectations of another Bank of Japan rate increase. The yen gained as investors sought safer assets, a sign that the market is pricing tighter policy even as the economy copes with weather-related friction.

The mood is one of reluctant adjustment, where households and businesses must manage both immediate logistical inconvenience and the prospect of higher borrowing costs. Japanese carriers are warning that disruption may continue through the weekend, which keeps the focus on resilience rather than recovery.

South Korea: Technology Anxiety Without A Political Script

South Korean equities fell more than 2 per cent on Friday as technology shares extended their losses, deepening the sense that the artificial-intelligence trade is losing momentum. The sell-off has not drawn a clear government or central-bank response, leaving investors to read the market alone.

That silence matters: South Korea’s growth model is heavily tied to semiconductors and hardware, and a sustained technology retreat would quickly become a political problem. The absence of an official voice today suggests either confidence that the move is temporary or uncertainty about what to say.

China: Market Losses And Disaster Response

China’s CSI 300 entered a bear market after falling more than 20 per cent from its June peak, with technology and artificial-intelligence valuations leading the decline. The combination of financial unease and disaster response puts Chinese authorities in a defensive posture, managing both investor confidence and emergency relief. For Washington, the bear-market signal is a reminder that China’s domestic demand and equity sentiment remain fragile even as official messaging emphasises stability.

North Korea: Signalling Into A Void

North Korea has continued making threats while South Korea’s presidential office remains silent, according to Japanese reporting. The dynamic is familiar: Pyongyang tests the perimeter of attention, and Seoul withholds the reaction that might escalate or legitimise the provocation.

The lack of a South Korean official response does not mean the threat is ignored; it means the government is choosing not to feed the cycle. For a US reader, the silence is a form of discipline, but it also leaves allies and markets to infer the level of concern from what is not said.

What This Means From Latin America

Typhoon-related closures in Taiwan and Japan could temporarily disrupt air cargo and maritime logistics connecting East Asia with Latin American markets, particularly for electronics, components and time-sensitive goods. The confirmed cancellation of more than six hundred flights in Taiwan alone is enough to delay shipments and raise freight costs on trans-Pacific routes.

The technology sell-off also matters for Latin American commodity exporters, since weaker Asian industrial and equity sentiment can translate into softer demand for copper, lithium and agricultural inputs. No same-day trade impact is confirmed, but the linkage runs through the region’s dependence on Asian manufacturing and investment cycles.

The decision and statement will clarify whether inflation data have shifted the Bank of Japan’s tightening path.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did Taiwan close schools and markets on 23 October?

Taiwan closed schools, offices and financial markets because Typhoon Champi brought torrential rain and strong winds, prompting authorities to cancel 262 domestic and more than 350 international flights. The storm was weakening and not forecast to make direct landfall, but the precautionary shutdown aimed to limit risk across the island.

How is Typhoon Champi affecting Japan?

More than 100 flights operated by Japan Airlines, All Nippon Airways and Skymark were cancelled between 22 and 25 October, affecting more than 11,000 passengers. The storm was expected to move towards southern Japan, and carriers warned that disruption could continue through the weekend.

Why are South Korean shares falling?

South Korean equities fell more than 2 per cent on 23 October as technology shares extended losses amid anxiety over artificial-intelligence valuations. The decline reflects the country’s heavy exposure to semiconductors and hardware at a time when investors are reassessing the sector’s near-term prospects.

What is the Bank of Japan expected to do next?

Japanese inflation data released on 23 October strengthened expectations of another Bank of Japan rate increase, while the yen gained as investors sought safer assets. The Bank of Japan’s next interest rate decision is scheduled for 29 October, with the policy rate forecast to remain at 1.25 per cent.

World.title: Cabo Verde Eases Early Voting Rules
World.content:
Photo: Ji-Elle / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

Cabo Verde has made it easier for patients in hospital and prisoners to vote early in the presidential election on Sunday, 15 November 2026. They no longer need a notary to certify the copy of their identity document, according to the Cabo Verde election updates we keep on this vote.

The National Elections Commission (CNE), the state body that runs elections, adopted the change on Wednesday, 21 October 2026. Cabo Verde, also written Cape Verde, is a stable island democracy off West Africa, and our Cape Verde presidential election 2026 guide explains the wider race.

Key Facts What changed: Hospital patients and prisoners may now apply for early voting with a simple copy of their ID.

Hospital patients and prisoners may now apply for early voting with a simple copy of their ID. Who decided: The election commission voted unanimously on Wednesday, 21 October 2026, in a plenary meeting.

The election commission voted unanimously on Wednesday, 21 October 2026, in a plenary meeting. Why: The commission says the change makes voting easier for people who cannot reach a polling station.

The commission says the change makes voting easier for people who cannot reach a polling station. Election day: First round on Sunday, 15 November 2026; runoff, if needed, on Sunday, 29 November.

First round on Sunday, 15 November 2026; runoff, if needed, on Sunday, 29 November. Prediction markets: Polymarket gives José Maria Neves 84.0% to win, as of 8:01 a.m. ET on 23 October 2026.

This story is part of our coverage of the Cape Verde presidential election 2026. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide.

In Plain English Early voting: a vote cast before election day by people who cannot attend, here patients in hospital and prisoners.

a vote cast before election day by people who cannot attend, here patients in hospital and prisoners. Notarised copy: a photocopy stamped by an official to prove it matches the original.

a photocopy stamped by an official to prove it matches the original. Runoff: a second round between the top two candidates if nobody wins more than half of the valid votes.

Commission Drops Notary Step

The commission approved Deliberation No. 32 on the presidential elections unanimously at its plenary on Wednesday, 21 October 2026. The Cabo Verdean newspaper Expresso das Ilhas reported the decision on Thursday, 22 October.

Under the text, a request for an early vote can now come with a simple copy of the voter's identity document. That removes the authentication formality set out in Article 215(1) of the Electoral Code.

The identity document is still required, but the rules are generous about which one. Voters can use an identity card or passport, even if it has expired, or the national identification card or its original receipt, as long as it confirms who they are.

The commission said the aim is to simplify the process and raise participation among these voters. It did not say how many patients or prisoners are expected to use the procedure.

How the Vote Works

Cabo Verde votes for its president on Sunday, 15 November 2026. Cabo Verde time is UTC−1, so from 1 November, when US clocks go back, it runs four hours ahead of US Eastern Time.

A candidate needs more than half of the valid votes to win outright. If nobody does, the top two go to a runoff on Sunday, 29 November 2026.

The official campaign runs from 29 October to 13 November, with the final day before the vote kept for reflection. Candidates can withdraw until 13 November by writing to the president of the Constitutional Court.

Six Candidates in the Race

The Constitutional Court first admitted five candidacies on 21 September, then admitted a sixth, Loisito Tavares de Sousa, on appeal on 24 September (reported on 27 September). The six are Gilson João dos Santos Alves, Joana Gomes Rosa Amado, José Maria Pereira Neves, Antero Lúcio Lopes Francês Tavares, Casimiro Jesus Lopes de Pina and Loisito Tavares de Sousa.

The best-known are the incumbent, President José Maria Neves of the PAICV party, and Joana Rosa, a former Justice Minister. After announcing his candidacy, Neves stepped aside from presidential duties under the Electoral Code, and parliament speaker Janira Hopffer Almada is interim head of state.

What It Means for US Readers

The change is small, but it shows an election authority smoothing the rules two and a half weeks before a vote. For Americans who follow African democracies, that fits Cabo Verde{Q}s record as one of the continent{Q}s steadier political systems.

Investors and travellers can read it as a sign of orderly preparation. Cabo Verde has recently drawn attention for its IMF growth outlook and its tourism economy.

What Is Not Known

No reaction from opposition parties, civil-society groups or the courts to the new rule has been reported. The number of eligible hospital patients and prisoners is not public in the reports we found.

No named, dated opinion poll from the last 48 hours was available. The official results page stays empty until voting has taken place.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Cabo Verde change for early voting?

Hospital patients and prisoners can now request an early vote with a simple copy of their identity document. The notary authentication step is dropped, but the document is still required.

Who decided the change and when?

The National Elections Commission approved it unanimously at its plenary on Wednesday, 21 October 2026. It is Deliberation No. 32.

When is the Cabo Verde presidential election?

The first round is on Sunday, 15 November 2026. A runoff, if no one wins more than half of valid votes, follows on Sunday, 29 November.

Who is running for president of Cabo Verde?

Six candidates were admitted by the Constitutional Court, including President José Maria Neves and former Justice Minister Joana Rosa. The others are Gilson Alves, Antero Tavares, Casimiro de Pina and Loisito Tavares de Sousa.

What do prediction markets say about the race?

Polymarket gave Neves 84.0% as of 8:01 a.m. ET on 23 October 2026, with about US$34,000 traded. These are bets, not polls.

Africa’s temper on Friday is a mixture of epidemiological alarm, border anxiety and combustible social tension. Nigeria has confirmed its first Ebola case, Kenya is absorbing displaced Ethiopians after gunfire near Moyale, and South Africa is confronting a fatal anti-immigrant mob attack in Durban. The region is not experiencing a single coordinated crisis, but it is being pulled simultaneously by disease, displacement and public anger.

The register is one of defensive control and urgent mobilisation. Nigerian authorities are expanding airport screening and contact tracing, Kenyan police and the Red Cross are managing cross-border arrivals, and South African investigators are responding to a killing that has deepened fear among foreign nationals. Leaders are speaking the language of containment and order, while ordinary people absorb the consequences of contagion, regional instability and xenophobic violence.

The through-line is the collision between mobility and fear. A virus travels through an aviation hub, civilians cross a border to escape gunfire, and a crowd turns migration into a lethal grievance. Governments can screen passengers, register displaced families and open murder investigations, but they cannot quickly erase the underlying anxieties that make movement itself a source of danger and suspicion.

Key Facts —Nigeria Ebola. 44 contacts identified after a woman tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain, confirmed on 20 to 21 October. —Kenya border. Hundreds of Ethiopians crossed into Moyale after gunfire began around 5:50 a.m. on 22 October. —South Africa killing. A foreign national was beaten to death by about 50 people in Durban on 23 October. —Kenya inflation. Consumer prices rose to 6.8 per cent in September, the highest since January 2024. —Nigeria rate cut. The Central Bank of Nigeria reduced its benchmark rate by 350 basis points to 23 per cent in September.

Nigeria: Vigilance Moves To The Airport

Nigeria’s first confirmed Ebola case has shifted the national mood from distant concern to immediate defensive vigilance. Africanews reported this week that the patient, a woman who travelled from Uganda to Abuja, remains isolated and that 44 contacts had been identified for monitoring. The fact that the Bundibugyo strain reached West Africa through a major aviation route has made airports and contact lists the new front line of public anxiety.

A US reader should see this as a warning that epidemic risk in Africa is now inseparable from global air travel. Nigerian health authorities are expanding screening and tracing, but the psychological effect is broader: a single imported case can turn routine movement into a perceived threat. The response will test whether Nigeria’s surveillance system can contain the virus before fear outruns the science.

Kenya: Border Anxiety And Humanitarian Response

Kenya is absorbing the human consequences of instability across its northern border. Africanews reported that hundreds of Ethiopians crossed into Kenya through Moyale, with crossings starting on Wednesday 21 October and gunfire heard on the Ethiopian side from about 5:50 a.m. on Thursday 22 October. The Kenya Red Cross said its initial response would reach 1,000 households, signalling both the scale of displacement and the strain on local services.

A US reader should read this as a reminder that Ethiopia’s internal frictions are not contained by its borders. The multiple crossing points used by arrivals, including Sessi, Kore and Biashara, suggest that the movement is broad and difficult to regulate. Kenya’s challenge is to manage a humanitarian response while preventing the border area from becoming a new zone of insecurity.

South Africa: Migration Becomes A Lethal Grievance

South Africa’s social mood is combustible and exclusionary after a foreign national was beaten to death by a crowd of approximately 50 people in Durban. The AllAfrica aggregation published on Friday reported that police were investigating and that the victim’s identity and motive remained unclear, but the killing followed violent anti-immigrant protests in Durban and Soweto. Migration is functioning as a vessel for broader frustration over security, jobs and state capacity.

A US reader should understand that this violence is not an isolated criminal incident but a symptom of deeper social strain. The separate arrest of a 46-year-old Nigerian national during a raid on an alleged brothel in Mpumalanga, reported by The Citizen on Friday, shows how immigration status is being folded into law-enforcement narratives. The danger is that public anger hardens into organised xenophobia, making foreign nationals permanent scapegoats.

Regional Economy: Divergent Pressures, Shared Unease

The economic mood across Africa is uneven but increasingly anxious. BusinessDay reported on Friday that inflation rose in eight of 16 African economies in September, reversing the previous month’s trend, with South Africa, Kenya, Ghana, Uganda, Mauritius and Tunisia recording increases. Kenya’s rate climbed for a third consecutive month to 6.8 per cent, its highest since January 2024, while Nigeria, Egypt, Angola and Botswana recorded declines.

A US reader should note that this divergence complicates any single regional monetary story. Nigeria’s central bank cut its benchmark rate by 350 basis points to 23 per cent in September, a dramatic easing that contrasts with Kenya’s renewed price pressure. The policy gap reflects different domestic calculations, but the shared vulnerability to energy costs and geopolitical uncertainty means that external shocks could quickly narrow the divergence.

What This Means From Latin America

Nigeria’s imported Ebola case is a direct warning for Latin American aviation and health authorities, because the virus moved through a major international hub before being detected. The South African anti-immigrant violence offers a sobering parallel for Latin American societies grappling with irregular migration, asylum backlogs and public-order politics. Both developments show how quickly mobility can become a security issue when fear and economic pressure collide.

The regional inflation divergence also matters for Latin American trade and commodity exposure. Higher energy costs and geopolitical uncertainty are affecting African importers and exporters in ways that mirror pressures on Latin American economies, particularly those dependent on food and fuel imports. Kenyan President William Ruto’s call at the COMESA summit to mobilise more than US$4 trillion in African domestic financial assets echoes Latin American debates about development banks and regional financial autonomy.

What We Are Watching

Friday 23 October onward: Nigeria Ebola contact tracing — The 44 identified contacts will be monitored for symptoms. Any new confirmed case would mark a significant escalation of the outbreak in West Africa.

— The 44 identified contacts will be monitored for symptoms. Any new confirmed case would mark a significant escalation of the outbreak in West Africa. Immediate: Moyale border security — Watch for further Ethiopian arrivals, Kenyan border restrictions or a formal bilateral response after the reported gunfire of 22 October. The humanitarian situation could deteriorate if displacement continues.

— Watch for further Ethiopian arrivals, Kenyan border restrictions or a formal bilateral response after the reported gunfire of 22 October. The humanitarian situation could deteriorate if displacement continues. Immediate: South African anti-immigrant violence — Watch for arrests, official condemnation or further attacks following the Durban killing. The government’s response will signal whether it can contain xenophobic mobilisation.

— Watch for arrests, official condemnation or further attacks following the Durban killing. The government’s response will signal whether it can contain xenophobic mobilisation. Thursday 29 October, 4:30 a.m. ET: Zambia inflation rate — October data is due with a forecast of 6.3 per cent against 6.1 per cent. A rise would add to cost-of-living pressures in a key Southern African economy.

— October data is due with a forecast of 6.3 per cent against 6.1 per cent. A rise would add to cost-of-living pressures in a key Southern African economy. Thursday 29 October, 12:00 p.m. ET: Egypt interest rate decision The decision will signal how Cairo is balancing inflation and growth under fiscal pressure.

The decision will signal how Cairo is balancing inflation and growth under fiscal pressure. Friday 30 October, 4:00 a.m. ET: Kenya inflation rate — October data is due with a forecast of 7 per cent against 6.8 per cent. Another rise would intensify pressure on the central bank to respond.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Ebola situation in Nigeria?

Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case on 20 to 21 October, identifying 44 contacts after a woman tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain. Nigerian health authorities isolated the confirmed Ebola patient and identified 44 contacts for monitoring.

Why are Ethiopians crossing into Kenya?

Hundreds of Ethiopians crossed into Kenya through Moyale, with crossings starting on Wednesday 21 October and gunfire heard on the Ethiopian side from about 5:50 a.m. on Thursday 22 October. Most arrivals were women, children and young people fleeing tensions between the Oromia and Somali regional administrations.

What happened in Durban, South Africa?

A foreign national was beaten to death by a crowd of approximately 50 people in Durban on 23 October 2026. The killing followed violent anti-immigrant protests in Durban and Soweto, and police were investigating the victim’s identity and motive.

What did Kenya’s inflation rate reach in September?

Kenya’s inflation rate rose for a third consecutive month to 6.8 per cent in September 2026, its highest level since January 2024. The increase was part of a broader regional pattern in which eight of 16 African economies recorded higher inflation.

Embraer, the Brazilian aircraft maker, said on Friday that its order backlog hit a record US$35.7 billion at the end of September. That is up 3% from the previous record of US$34.5 billion in June and up 14% from US$31.3 billion a year earlier, according to its filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.

The figure matters beyond Embraer, because it is one of the biggest names in Brazil’s economy. It trades in New York as EMBJ and on the São Paulo stock exchange as EMBJ3.

In Plain English Backlog: firm orders not yet delivered. E175 and E195-E2: Embraer’s regional airliners. KC-390: a military transport jet. Phenom 300EV: a light business jet.

Where the Orders Came From

Embraer received 36 firm orders and 30 purchase rights or options for its E2-family airliners in the quarter. Over nine months it has booked 72 firm E2 orders.

Deliveries Are Ahead of Plan

Embraer delivered 66 aircraft in the third quarter, against 65 in the second and 62 a year earlier. That was 22 airliners, 41 business jets and three military aircraft.

In nine months it has delivered 175 aircraft, compared with 153 a year ago. Airliners and business jets together stand at 167, about 67% of the midpoint of its 240 to 255 aircraft target for 2026, against a five-year average of 59% at this point.

US airlines hold a large share of the order book. American Airlines, SkyWest and Republic Airways still await 66, 63 and 26 E175 regional jets, and Avelo Airlines is due 50 E195-E2 jets.

For shareholders, a record backlog points to years of sales, but it is not profit, and orders can slip or be cancelled. Embraer’s financial results will show how much of it turns into earnings.

How big is Embraer’s order backlog?

Embraer’s backlog was US$35.7 billion at the end of the third quarter of 2026, a record. It is up 3% from US$34.5 billion in the previous quarter and 14% from US$31.3 billion a year earlier.

World.content:
A Spanish-language “Yo Voté” (“I Voted”) sticker given to voters in the United States (file photo, October 2012; Photo: sarachicad, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Key Facts

Early Vote Total: More than 20 million ballots had been cast early by Thursday, 22 October, according to data from 46 states.

More than 20 million ballots had been cast early by Thursday, 22 October, according to data from 46 states. Election Date: The US midterm elections are scheduled for Tuesday, 3 November 2026, with poll closing times set by state and locality.

The US midterm elections are scheduled for Tuesday, 3 November 2026, with poll closing times set by state and locality. Current Majorities: Republicans hold narrow majorities: 218 to 214 in the House (plus one independent and two vacancies) and 53 to 47 in the Senate.

Republicans hold narrow majorities: 218 to 214 in the House (plus one independent and two vacancies) and 53 to 47 in the Senate. Democratic Target: Democrats need a net gain of four Senate seats for a majority; 218 seats make a House majority.

Democrats need a net gain of four Senate seats for a majority; 218 seats make a House majority. Prediction markets: Polymarket gives Democrats 92.5% to win the House and 67.5% to win the Senate, as of 23 October, 7:22 a.m. ET.

Early Voting Surpasses 20 Million

More than 20 million Americans had already voted early by Thursday, 22 October, according to data compiled by The Associated Press from 46 states. The cumulative count comes less than two weeks before the 3 November election and represents the clearest hard fact distinguishing the campaign at the close of 23 October.

This story is part of our coverage of the 2026 US midterm elections. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide. Latest: US Democrats Lead House Race by 8 Points

Our US midterms 2026 dossier tracks the race.

The figure is not a forecast of final turnout and not a reliable measure of which party is ahead. Party registration, the availability of early voting, and the eventual Election Day vote vary substantially by state.

Polling And Market Snapshot

The newest specifically dated poll result located was an AP-NORC poll reported on 22 October, which found roughly eight in ten voters surveyed said lowering the cost of living should be one of Congress's highest priorities. Roughly seven in ten said ending the war in Iran should be a top priority, while about two in ten wanted Congress to prioritize supporting President Donald Trump's agenda.

In named races, a St. Anselm College poll conducted 19–20 October put Democrat Stefany Shaheen at 46% and Republican Anthony DiLorenzo at 42% in New Hampshire’s 1st Congressional District. In Florida's 25th Congressional District, Democrat Jared Moskowitz led Republican Scott Singer 47% to 42% in a Public Policy Polling survey conducted 21–22 October for the Democratic-aligned House Majority PAC.

A Republican internal poll had Singer ahead 49% to 42%.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, House 2026: Democrats 92.5%, Republicans 7.5% (US$20.6 million traded).

Polymarket, Senate 2026: Democrats 67.5%, Republicans 32.0% (US$8.6 million traded).

Kalshi, balance of power: Democrats sweep both chambers 66.0%, Republicans sweep 8.7%. Kalshi is regulated in the US by the CFTC.

Prices are bets, not polls, and are as of 23 October, 7:22 a.m. ET. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely.

We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Campaign Developments

The most prominent same-day campaign controversy concerned an Ohio Republican  featuring the estranged mother of Democratic candidate Amy Acton. President Trump defended Republican candidate Vivek Ramaswamy and urged him to keep the  running, while Republican Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine called it “deeply, deeply troubling” but kept his endorsement.

Trump was also campaigning in Iowa on Thursday night for Republican Senate candidate Ashley Hinson, who had called for the Ohio  to be removed. The episode has produced bipartisan criticism, although Trump and Ramaswamy have continued to defend the spot.

In Texas, Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico reported raising US$17.6 million during the first two weeks of October, according to new Federal Election Commission filings. Total advertising spending in that contest, including the primary, was reported at more than US$500 million.

What Is Not Known

The early-vote total does not establish the final turnout, the partisan composition of those ballots, or the result in any chamber.

Polling remains a snapshot, and the cited national margins differ by poll and methodology. The number of ballots still to be cast on 3 November, the final congressional balance, and which close races will determine control remain unknown.

What It Means for US Readers

For US readers, the early-vote milestone is a concrete signal of engagement but not a predictor of outcome. Party registration and state rules make early ballots an unreliable indicator of which side is ahead.

The narrow Republican majorities in both chambers mean a relatively small shift in seats could change control of Congress. Prediction markets currently assign Democrats a high probability of taking the House and a solid chance in the Senate, though they are bets and not forecasts by officials.

Polls Show Tight Race

The freshest named-institute poll available is from Ipsos, published 22 October and based on 3,624 respondents. It was commissioned by the ruling list and put SNS at 47.4% and the Student List at 40.0%.

The Socialist Party-led list had 3.2%.

A separate NSPM poll published 20 October, surveying 1,050 people by telephone between 25 September and 5 October, showed a different picture among decided voters. It put the Student List at 44.5% and Vučić's United Serbia list at 42.7%, with 18.3% of respondents undecided.

The PolitPro aggregate as of 23 October gives SNS 45.0% and the Student List 42.5%. The poll gap is narrower than the Ipsos figures suggest.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, winner of the election: Vučić’s United Serbia list 69.5% (US$3.2 million traded).

Polymarket, Student List vote share: 40–45% at 29.5%, 35–40% at 28.0%, 45–50% at 23.0%.

Polymarket, United Serbia vote share: 45–50% at 37.0%, 40–45% at 32.5%.

Prices are bets, not polls, and are as of 23 October, 7:22 a.m. ET. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely.

We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Final Rally and Arrests

On Thursday evening, 22 October, tens of thousands of people attended the Student List's final campaign rally in Belgrade, and the independent Archive of Public Gatherings estimated about 150,000. The movement grew out of student protests following the November 2024 Novi Sad railway-station canopy collapse, which killed 16 people.

On Wednesday, 21 October, police arrested six people on suspicion of plotting violence and attacks on election day, according to the Higher Public Prosecutor's Office. The available reports do not establish whether prosecutors filed indictments, whether the suspects remain detained, or whether authorities linked the alleged plot to a particular political organization.

What Analysts Are Watching

Political scientist Dušan Vučićević of the University of Belgrade said the result was difficult to predict but expected the student movement to exceed 40%, which would be unusually strong for an opposition list under SNS rule. SNS and the Student List both claim to be ahead.

The Republic Election Commission (RIK) registered the Student List with 250 candidates, one for each parliamentary seat. Serbia's electoral system uses a single nationwide constituency and proportional allocation; most lists must obtain at least 3% of the vote, while recognized minority lists are exempt.

What It Means for US Readers

For US readers, the election is a test of whether a grassroots student movement can unseat a dominant ruling party in a European democracy. The contest has drawn comparisons to broader global debates about youth mobilization and institutional trust.

Traders on Polymarket put the odds of Vučić’s list finishing first at about 70%. Polling averages and the official count remain the primary measures of the contest.

What Is Not Known

Whether the Student List's apparent polling surge will translate into enough seats to form a government remains unknown. The final seat distribution and coalition arithmetic cannot be determined from vote-share polls alone.

How undecided voters will break, particularly the 18.3% recorded by NSPM, is not known. Whether smaller lists below the 3% threshold will win representation is also unclear.

Whether the arrests over alleged election-day violence will produce charges or affect the vote has not been established. Whether allegations of intimidation, media imbalance, surveillance, and cyberattacks will be substantiated through official investigations or independent observation is also unknown.

Related Reading

Serbia Votes Sunday After Student Protests

When do polls close in Serbia's election?

Who are the main contenders?

The ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), led by former president Aleksandar Vučić, who is now its candidate for prime minister, faces the student-backed 'Student List – Students Win'. The SNS has been in government since 2012.

What do the latest polls show?

World.title: France Deploys 70,000 Police for Protests
World.content:
Police officers on motorcycles at a crossing in Guatemala City, pictured in an undated file photo. The photo does not show Sperisen or the 2006 operation. Photo: tian2992 / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

FRANCE · PROTESTS

Published Friday, 23 October, 7:40 a.m. ET (1:40 p.m. Paris) · Source: Franceinfo, Public Sénat, Sud Radio

France will put 70,000 police and gendarmes on the streets on Saturday, 24 October, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said at a Friday press briefing. The aim is to stop a repeat of the looting that followed the France protests of 17 October.

Nuñez promised, “We will be absolutely intransigent” (« intraitables »), with troublemakers. The turmoil is part of why France is in crisis, with unions also planning a nationwide strike on 5 November.

Key Facts What happened: Nuñez says 70,000 police and gendarmes will be on duty across France on Saturday.

Nuñez says 70,000 police and gendarmes will be on duty across France on Saturday. Who decided: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, announcing the plan at a press briefing on Friday.

Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, announcing the plan at a press briefing on Friday. The numbers: Police sources expect 10,000 to 15,000 counter-protesters in Orléans.

Police sources expect 10,000 to 15,000 counter-protesters in Orléans. What happens next: Orléans march starts 10:30 a.m. Saturday in France (4:30 a.m. ET).

Orléans march starts 10:30 a.m. Saturday in France (4:30 a.m. ET). Why it matters for US readers: Travel plans, French markets and a NATO ally’s stability are all in play.

Travel plans, French markets and a NATO ally’s stability are all in play. Prediction markets: Polymarket 7.0% for a French state of emergency by 31 October; Kalshi 10% by 1 November (7:15 a.m. ET, 23 October).

This story is part of our coverage of the why France is in crisis. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide. Latest: France Boosts Security for Saturday Protests

In plain English France has had a week of protests over living costs and politics, and some ended in looting. The government is now sending far more police and banning many marches that unions do not organize.

How Big Is the Police Operation

Nuñez announced 70,000 police and gendarmes (the military police force that works alongside city police) for Saturday. He gave the figure at a press briefing reported by Franceinfo, the public broadcaster.

The minister said many helicopters would fly over Paris and other big cities, and that “Centaure armoured vehicles are everywhere on national territory”. He also warned of “calls on social networks” to loot, and promised officers would act “with great firmness” against troublemakers.

File photo: a burnt-out car in Paris after the 17 October unrest.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on France in Turmoil Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Where Protests Are Banned or Allowed

Nuñez said prefects, the state’s local officials, judge each march by the risk of public disorder. “Everything is evolving,” he added.

Franceinfo reports bans or restrictions on gatherings in Lyon, Rouen and Grenoble. In Paris a union march from Bastille to Nation is allowed, as earlier reporting showed.

Marseille is a surprise. The Bouches-du-Rhône prefecture said that one union march is authorised there “as an exception”, the only one in the department, after it banned all gatherings the day before, as we reported on Thursday.

Orléans Is the Main Flashpoint

The National Rally, the conservative party of Marine Le Pen, opens its congress in Orléans on Saturday and Sunday. It is the official launch of its presidential campaign, with about 5,000 activists expected Saturday and 10,000 Sunday, according to Sud Radio.

About 50 organizations have called a counter-mobilization, and police sources expect 10,000 to 15,000 people. A march “against racism, fascism and imperialism” leaves the cathedral square at 10:30 a.m. local time (4:30 a.m. ET) on Saturday.

Nuñez told a senator on 21 October that he expected “several tens of thousands” of people in Orléans on Saturday, according to Public Sénat. Orléans’ conservative mayor, Serge Grouard, said the city “must not become what we saw in Paris, Marseille or Rennes” on 17 October.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket puts the chance that France declares a state of emergency by 31 October at 7.0%, with about US$281,000 traded. Kalshi, regulated in the US by the CFTC, prices it at 10% before 1 November (7:15 a.m. ET, 23 October).

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for US Readers

Americans in France should expect closed streets, transport changes and police checks in big cities on Saturday. Check the local prefecture’s notices before travelling, especially in Paris, Lyon, Marseille and Orléans.

For investors, the test is whether a large show of force keeps Saturday calm ahead of the 5 November strike. Our France travel safety guide tracks the latest advice.

What Is Not Known

Turnout, arrests and damage on Saturday are unknown, as are the final crowd sizes in Orléans, where estimates range from 10,000 to “several tens of thousands”.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many police will France deploy on Saturday?

Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said 70,000 police and gendarmes will be on duty on Saturday, 24 October.

Where is the biggest counter-protest?

Orléans, a city south of Paris, where the National Rally party opens its congress on Saturday. About 50 organizations called a march at 10:30 a.m. local time (4:30 a.m. ET) from the cathedral square.

Are protests banned in France on Saturday?

Many are. Franceinfo reports bans or restrictions in Lyon, Rouen and Grenoble, and Paris allows a union march from Bastille to Nation.

Is France declaring a state of emergency?

Not so far. Nuñez said it is not needed, and traders on Polymarket put the odds at 7.0% by 31 October.
