The court clarified that the enquiry would continue in accordance with the law.

World.title: 'Won't tolerate vote theft': Anti-SIR protesters try to march to EC HQ, many detained
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Delhi Police detained several protesters on Friday as a march against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls headed towards the Election Commission (EC) headquarters in central Delhi.

Authorities imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), banning mass gatherings, sources said.

The demonstration was called by the Delhi Coordination Committee of People Against SIR, a people's collective, and drew students, youth, farmers and activists carrying the national flag and banners of the group.

The Krantikari Yuva Sangathan (KYS) and the Students' Federation of India (SFI) also extended their support, with activists from Delhi, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh joining the march.

Amid slogans such as âGyanesh Kumar, resignâ, âHalt SIRâ and âWonât tolerate vote theftâ, the protesters were joined by senior CPI(M) leader Brinda Karat and members of the All India Democratic Women's Association (AIDWA) and the All India Democratic Students' Organisation (AIDSO), among others.

The march began near Gole Dak Khana, at the intersection of Kalibari Marg and Bhai Vir Singh Marg, and proceeded towards the ECI headquarters.





When police stopped the protesters, they sat down and held a 'People's Parliament', as announced by the organisers.

âThe protest has begun! We won't let go our right to vote and the right to protest for it! Our's is a democratic country and we will ensure that spirit remains alive!â the All India Students' Association (AISA) said in a post on X.

âThis is not about reclaiming Jantar Mantar; this is about saving democracy and the country,â a protester said, as cited by PTI.

Another protester said that since Jantar Mantar had been denotified as a protest site, every street in the country would become a Jantar Mantar, pointing to several organisations announcing demonstrations across India.

Protests planned across 88 cities

People Against SIR has launched a website providing information about demonstrations being held in different cities. According to the collective, protests have been planned in 88 cities across 18 states, involving 145 organisations.

The collective has listed demonstrations scheduled for Friday, with programmes extending until November 1 as part of its campaign against the SIR exercise. Organisers have appealed to farmers, workers, youth, women and people from different sections of society to participate while carrying the national flag.

The organisers said the Delhi march would remain peaceful and conclude with the adoption of resolutions and the singing of the national anthem.

The SFI has also called for solidarity protests in central Delhi and at district headquarters on Friday.

Security tightened, traffic diversions in place

Security was tightened in central Delhi, with Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel deployed in large numbers.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Traffic diversions were enforced in parts of central Delhi from 1 pm and were scheduled to remain in place until 5 pm. Congestion was expected around Bangla Sahib Gurudwara, Connaught Place, Parliament Street and Jantar Mantar.

The Delhi Traffic Police advised commuters to avoid unnecessary travel along the affected stretches, plan their journeys and follow instructions issued by traffic personnel.

The protest comes amid concerns raised by opposition parties and various organisations over the SIR exercise and the alleged deletion of voters from electoral rolls.

World.title: Punjab polls: Badal praises SAD-BJP rule as Amit Shah’s NDA pitch fuels reunion buzz
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Speculation over a possible reunion between the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) gathered pace on Friday after SAD chief

said his party was open to an alliance with parties that agree with its ideology and programmes, a day after Union home minister Amit Shah predicted an NDA government in Punjab in 2027.

Badal, however, ruled out any understanding with the Congress and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), calling them the âtwo biggest enemies of Punjabâ.

"During the SAD-BJP rule, peace prevailed in Punjab, and the state witnessed development, be it in infrastructure, industry, or the state becoming power surplus," Badal told reporters on Friday, according to PTI.

"Whether we form the government or not, we will continue to fight for the people of Punjab.

In our view, the Congress and Aam Aadmi Party are the two biggest enemies of Punjab, and we can never have understanding with these parties. There are many other parties besides these and those who agree with the Akali Dal's ideology and programmes; we are open (for a tie-up)," he said.

The remarks came a day after Union minister Amit Shah said Punjab's people had decided that an NDA government would come to power in the state in the 2027 assembly elections.





He also predicted that the ruling AAP would be wiped out in the polls.

Shah's statement reignited speculation about the BJP and SAD joining hands again, although Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon denied that any alliance decision had been taken.

"We have nothing on an alliance as of now. We are prepared for all 117 seats and will contest on all of them," Dhillon told TOI, adding that the BJP referred to its government at the Centre as an NDA government and would do the same in Punjab.

A senior Punjab BJP functionary, however, said the political signal was clear despite Shah not naming the Akali Dal. The functionary also felt the two parties should have announced an alliance earlier, given the limited time before the elections. Any formal announcement would have to come from BJP national president Nitin Nabin, the functionary said.

Why a SAD-BJP reunion matters

The SAD and BJP were long-time allies in Punjab before the regional party ended their 24-year-old alliance in September 2020 over the now-repealed farm laws.

SAD MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal, Sukhbir Singh Badal's wife, had also served as a Cabinet minister in the Narendra Modi government before the split.

The former allies contested elections together for years, but their political fortunes were limited in the 2022 Punjab assembly polls. The BJP won two seats, while the SAD secured three in the 117-member Assembly.

In recent months, several Punjab BJP leaders had maintained that the party was preparing to contest all 117 assembly seats independently.

Dhillon reiterated that position on Friday, even as Shah's remarks and Badal's openness to an alliance renewed questions about the parties' electoral plans.

Badal made the comments after leading an SAD delegation to meet Punjab governor Gulab Chand Kataria on Friday. The delegation submitted a memorandum over the killing of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa and demanded, among other measures, the dismissal of Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Badal accused the AAP government of mishandling Punjab's affairs and said the state's law and order situation had deteriorated. He also blamed the Congress and AAP governments for what he described as the worsening situation in the state.

With the 2027 assembly elections approaching, the public statements have revived the possibility of a realignment between the former allies. However, neither party has announced a formal agreement, and the BJP's Punjab leadership continues to maintain that it is preparing to contest all 117 seats.

World.title: Myanmar arms training case: Court allows US mercenary VanDyke, 6 Ukrainians to stay abroad till Feb 24
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Friday allowed American mercenary Matthew Aaron VanDyke to travel to the United States and extended permission for six Ukrainian nationals to remain outside India until February 24.

Special judge Prashant Sharma passed the order while hearing applications moved by the seven foreign nationals.

VanDyke, along with the six Ukrainians, was arrested by the

in March 2026 for allegedly providing weapons and drone-warfare training to ethnic armed groups in Myanmar.

The court's decision came after the central probing agency submitted that it needed more time to investigate several aspects of the case.

Its counsel, Rahul Tyagi, made submissions to this effect.

Speaking to PTI outside the courtroom, VanDyke questioned the continuation of the case against him.

"There's no reason for it to continue. If not, I'll stay in India. Until this is over," he said.

VanDyke, who was granted default bail last month, had returned to India to appear before the court and seek an extension of the permission granted to him to travel abroad.





In September, the court had allowed him to travel to the US for a month to meet his family, subject to the condition that he return to India and appear before it.

The US national also said he had removed his lawyer due to financial difficulties.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"I don't have any comments on the case. It's all ongoing. Especially now that I'm my own lawyer. I don't want to talk about it. There is a money issue. That's the main issue," he said.

The NIA had alleged that VanDyke and the six Ukrainian nationals entered India on tourist visas, travelled to the northeastern region without mandatory permits and subsequently crossed from Mizoram into Myanmar, where they allegedly trained ethnic armed organisations.

The agency had initially invoked provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), including those relating to conspiracy.

It had also alleged that the accused disclosed details about the network and were involved in assembling equipment and targeting a passenger aircraft in Myanmar.

However, in its charge sheet, the NIA did not invoke the UAPA provisions and instead proceeded under Sections 21 and 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, which provide for offences that can be compounded before the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO).

The agency had earlier indicated that its investigation into the alleged terror-related aspects was continuing and that further allegations could be included in a supplementary charge sheet.

World.title: 'Deafening silence from PM': Congress targets Centre over reported 'face-offs' along Arunachal border
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Congress on Friday accused Prime Minister

of remaining silent on reported face-offs between Indian and Chinese troops in Arunachal Pradesh. The party also alleged that the government had made âconcessionsâ to Beijing and failed to adequately address concerns over border security.

In a post on X, the opposition party criticised PM over his interactions with Chinese president Xi Jinping at the BRICS summit, saying the prime minister was seen joking with Xi even as Indian troops reportedly faced tensions along the border.

"Instead of showing China the "red eye," Narendra Modi was seen joking around with Chinese President Xi Jinpingâat the BRICS summit", it wrote.

The Congress also alleged that reports of clashes with Chinese soldiers had been suppressed since July.

The party's handle shared the video of the ITBP chief and wrote, âModi has abandoned our soldiers every time, betrayed the country, and washed his hands of responsibility. Sometimes giving China a clean chit, sometimes abandoning control of patrolling points and the country's land. He called Prime Minister Narendra Modi a âweak prime ministerâ and accused him of causing immense damage to the country.

The criticism follows remarks by Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) Director General Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor, who said on Thursday that the forceâs newly raised Shaurya commando unit had demonstrated its capabilities during ongoing face-offs with Chinaâs Peopleâs Liberation Army (PLA) at multiple locations in Arunachal Pradesh.





Kapoor said the specialised commandos would be deployed across every border battalion as the ITBP strengthens its combat readiness along the 3,488-km Line of Actual Control (LAC). The force is also expanding its modernisation drive, with greater emphasis on specialised training and emerging warfare technologies.

Meanwhile, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh separately cited media reports about the recent face-offs, questioning the Centreâs silence on the developments.

He alleged that India had made concessions to China and raised concerns over reports of lost patrolling points in Arunachal Pradesh.

âWhile the self-styled Vishwaguruâs calibrated concessions to China continue, the DG, ITBP, has laudedâand rightly soâits performance in recent face-offs with the PLA in Arunachal Pradesh, on which there has been a deafening silence from the PM and his establishment,â Ramesh wrote .

He added that local residents had reported the loss of patrolling points, drawing a parallel with developments in Ladakh.

Ramesh also flagged Chinaâs renaming of places in Arunachal Pradesh and the construction of a reported 60,000-MW dam, arguing that these developments posed risks to Indiaâs ecological and water security.

On the economic front, the Congress leader claimed that Indiaâs trade deficit with China had reached a record $112 billion in 2025-26, compared with $99 billion in the previous financial year.

He criticised the governmentâs Make in India initiative, writing that it had effectively become âImport from Chinaâ, and described the widening trade gap as a threat to economic security.

The Congress also invoked Modiâs June 19, 2020, remarks following the Galwan Valley clash, in which 20 Indian soldiers were killed. Ramesh quoted the prime minister as saying that no one had entered Indian territory and that no Indian post was under another countryâs control.

World.title: 'Lot of pressure on him, happened in just 2 hrs': Robert Vadra on son Raihan’s Bikaner exhibition row
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Businessman Robert Vadra has alleged that pressure was exerted on his son, artist and photographer Raihan Vadra, to remove photographs documenting recent protests in Delhi from his solo exhibition at Bikaner House, with the intervention coming just hours before the scheduled opening.

Calling the episode shocking, Robert said the authorities had received the exhibitionâs PDF a week in advance and had raised no objections until the final hours. He also praised Raihan for proceeding with the exhibition despite the removal of several photographs.

âThere was a lot of pressure on him to remove everything, and this happened just two hours before the opening of his exhibition. It was shocking because the authorities had received the PDF file a week in advance and had been informed about the exhibition,â Robert said.

He said setting up an exhibition required considerable effort and that officials had visited the venue, seen the displays and raised no objections initially. However, the situation changed shortly before the opening, he alleged, without any explanation.

âDespite this, I think he was brave enough to go ahead with the exhibition using whatever remained. As I said, I am proud of him. Everyone who had been invited attended the exhibition because this is also his profession,â he said.





âAll 75 had to be taken downâ

In a separate statement, Robert said Raihan had worked hard on the exhibition, which drew on photographs he took while documenting protests in the national capital.

âI am very proud of my son, Raihan, for the hard work he puts in every time he takes up a subject that is relevant to what is happening around him,â he said.

Robert said Raihan had attended the protests, keeping his friends in mind and considering the support students needed.

He carried his camera to the demonstrations, captured photographs and expressions, and later decided to organise an exhibition on the subject.

According to Robert, Raihan submitted a PDF of the proposed exhibition to Bikaner House officials about a week before the event. He alleged that the authorities did not raise concerns about the material at the time.

However, in the final 24 hours, after Raihan and his team had spent considerable time setting up the exhibition, officials arrived to review the displays, Robert said.

The commissioner of Bikaner House subsequently told them that certain displays would have to be removed.

âWhen Raihan asked how many displays were an issue and offered to remove any that were considered controversial, he was told that all 75 had to be taken down,â Robert alleged.

âNo point in mixing politics with the creative worldâ

Robert also questioned the decision to remove the photographs, saying artistic expression should be allowed in a democracy. He pointed out that Bikaner House comes under the Rajasthan government.

âIf we believe in democracy, there is no point in mixing politics with the creative world. Everyone should be allowed to express themselves,â he said.

The controversy centres on Raihanâs solo exhibition,

No Idea Is Final

, after he alleged that more than 70 photographs documenting recent youth-led protests in Delhi were removed shortly before the exhibition opened. Bikaner House has said certain photographs were inconsistent with its policy, which it said focuses on culture and wildlife, and that the removed images carried political messaging.

World.title: French, British air forces stage first joint nuclear strike simulation
World.content:
French and British air forces have for the first time staged a joint exercise simulating a nuclear strike, the countries' Defence Ministries said in a statement on Friday (October 23, 2026).

Thousands gather in Paris after court lifts protest ban despite fears of new violence

“The exercise, codenamed "Rummy", involved RAF Typhoon fighter jets alongside French Rafale aircraft over the Mediterranean Sea,” it said. “The exercise was conducted in compliance with security procedures, did not involve any actual nuclear weapons and was aimed at enhancing coordination between western Europe's two nuclear powers,” the statement added.

World.title: Top news of the day: Protesters marching to ECI HQ detained; Netanyahu orders West Bank closure; and more
World.content:
Police detain protesters during march to ECI HQ

A march against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was halted by police in central Delhi on Friday (October 23, 2026), as participants sought to head towards the Election Commission of India (ECI) headquarters to protest against the alleged deletion of voters. The march, called by the Delhi Coordination Committee of People Against SIR — a people’s collective — started near Gole Dak Khana, at the intersection of Kalibari Marg and Bhai Vir Singh Marg.

Netanyahu orders West Bank closure as attack wounds Israelis before election

Palestinian militants wounded five Israelis in an attack on Friday (October 23, 2026) before being killed in a shootout with soldiers, leading Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to order a lockdown in the occupied West Bank days before Israeli elections. Militant group Hamas, without claiming responsibility, praised the attack as a “heroic operation” and called for more.

16 killed, 65 injured as magnitude 7 quake hits Tibet; over 12,000 evacuated

At least 16 people were killed, and 65 others were injured after a magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck China’s Tibet Autonomous Region, prompting the evacuation of more than 12,000 residents, authorities said.T he shallow earthquake struck at a depth of less than 10 kilometres in Baqen County in Nagqu City at around 10:33 p.m. (local time) on Thursday (October 22).

Immigrants seeking U.S. citizenship targeted in Trump administration’s illegal voting crackdown

Most of the immigrants targeted by federal authorities in California this week for alleged voter fraud had applied for U.S. citizenship and now face charges related to lying on forms or during interviews. Those charges could lead to years in prison and thwart their efforts to naturalise. Amandeep Kaur, who is among those charged, has lived in the country for eight years and is in the process of becoming a naturalised U.S. citizen, said her husband, Kulwinder Singh.

Greece passes social media ban for children under 15

Greece’s Parliament approved a bill on ​Friday (October 23, 2026) that bans the ‌use of social media ​platforms for children under ⁠15 amid growing concerns over their impact on the health ‌and safety of minors. The ban comes ‌into force on ‌January ⁠1, 2027

World record: Jio Platforms IPO becomes first ever issue globally to receive over 1 crore applications

Jio Platforms Ltd’s initial public offering crossed another threshold on its closing day as the IPO became the first issue globally to receive over 1 crore applications. This surpasses the earlier global record of Waaree Energies, who received 97 lakh applications. Bidding for the $3.2 billion issue continues, with the IPO subscribed nearly 7 times and investors bidding for over 147 crore shares against 19.75 crores offered.

Scrap SIR ‘disenfranchisement exercise’, scientists urge govt. and ECI in petition

A collective of independent scientists has petitioned the Election Commission of India (ECI) and the government to scrap the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. They have demanded the immediate restoration of all eligible voters wrongly excluded. The signatories say they have endorsed the statement in their individual capacities, and that their views are personal and do not represent their institutions.

‘Unusual’ names, details crop up in electoral roll for MLC polls in U.P.; ECI cites software error

Entries such as “Ram ne Yadav ko maara”, “Ram ne Sharma ko maara” as names and “B.Com” in place of a voter’s father’s name have surfaced in the electoral roll for the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council elections, prompting the Election Commission of India (ECI) to issue a clarification over the discrepancies. The discrepancies were found in the Allahabad-Jhansi graduates’ constituency ahead of polling for 11 MLC seats on Friday (October 23)

POCSO survivor cannot be denied compensation solely due to absence of injury marks: Allahabad HC

The Allahabad High Court has ruled that a survivor of sexual assault under the POCSO Act cannot be denied compensation merely because the medical report does not record physical injuries. The court held that the district steering committee’s decision to withhold compensation was contrary to law and the provisions of the scheme.

‘Gem Granites’ Veeramani’s daughter detained from aircraft by SIT

The Special Investigation Team (SIT) constituted to investigate offences under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act against ‘Gem Granites’ owner R. Veeramani detained his daughter Archana Veeramani at the Chennai International Airport on Friday (October 23). Minutes after Ms. Archana boarded a scheduled flight to Singapore, an SIT team got her out of the aircraft with the assistance of the crew and took the 49-year-old passenger into custody, police sources said.

Pakistan refused to accept bodies of its own soldiers killed in Kargil war: India at UN

India slammed Pakistan at the UN, reminding the country that it did not even accept the bodies of its own soldiers killed in combat in the 1999 Kargil war but speaks about faith, religious freedom and burials. The interim report of the Special Rapporteur on freedom of religion and belief, Nazila Ghanea, said that “Reports of systemic denial of funeral rights in the context of individuals killed in security operations in Jammu and Kashmir, India, including denial of return of bodies to families and remote and secret burials

USA to host women’s football Club World Cup in 2028 - FIFA

The United States will host the inaugural women’s football Club World Cup in 2028, FIFA announced on Thursday (October 22). “The decision was taken in view of its experience in organising FIFA tournaments, the maturity of its infrastructure and services and the level of stakeholder interest in women’s football in the country,” world football’s governing body said.

World.title: Government plans colour-coded driving licences for citizens, foreign nationals
World.content:
The Road Transport Ministry has proposed introducing separate colour schemes for driving licences issued or renewed for Indian and foreign nationals, alongside doing away with affidavits sworn before an executive magistrate or notary as proof of age and address.

The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH), in draft amendments to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, has also proposed making it mandatory for driving licences to carry the holder's blood group, mobile number and emergency contact numbers.

"Every driving licence issued or renewed by a licensing authority shall be in the form of a laminated or Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) card in Form 7, and the Form shall contain separate formats for driving licences issued or renewed for Indian nationals and foreign nationals, respectively," the draft notification said.

The ministry also proposed accepting affidavits and life insurance policies as proof of age and address to prevent misuse.

It has proposed raising the qualifying threshold for the safe-driving tutorial assessment from 60-75%, alongside a fee waiver for select online driving licence services completed via Aadhaar authentication.

A senior official said the proposed changes to driving licence rules are aimed at tightening assessment requirements.

MoRTH, in draft amendments to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, has proposed that the safe-driving tutorial should run for at least 30 minutes.

Under the proposal, licensing authorities would have to approve or reject applications to change driving licence particulars, including name and address, within 15 days, with reasons for rejection.

It also proposed removing charges for changes in personal details, including the applicant's name and address.

The draft rules also specify documents that applicants can use as proof of identity, age and residence. The list includes Aadhaar, passport, voter identity card, e-ration card, birth certificate, among other documents.

Under the proposal, every driving licence issued or renewed by a licensing authority will be in a laminated or Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) card in Form 7.

The draft notification invites objections and suggestions from stakeholders within 30 days of publication.

World.title: Coimbatore student death: two classmates arrested for caste-based harassment; headmaster, teacher suspended
World.content:
Two days after a Class XI student belonging to a Scheduled Caste community ended his life in Coimbatore over alleged caste-based harassment in his government-aided school, the police on Friday (October 23, 2026) arrested two of his classmates belonging to different dominant castes.

The two students were produced before the Juvenile Justice Board and later lodged in an observation home for juveniles at Papanaickenpalayam in the city.

A senior police officer said the students were arrested on Friday after investigations revealed they had subjected the deceased A. Akilan (16) to caste-based harassment. Women police personnel collected statements from Akilan’s classmates and the teaching staff. Further investigation was under way into the allegations levelled by the mother of the deceased student against a teacher, P. Vijayakumar, and the headmaster, Arunkumar S.

The mother had accused the teacher of having harassed her son over his eating habits. As per the First Information Report (FIR) in the case, she alleged the teacher made her son and four others, who consume beef, stand up in the classroom two months ago. The two arrested students had been harassing and torturing him since then and the school’s headmaster did not take any action against them, she had alleged.

The officer said Akilan did not leave any note and the police team was investigating all the allegations raised by his parents against the two classmates, the teacher, and the headmaster.

Meanwhile, Akilan’s parents, relatives and members of the DMK, CPI (M), May 17 Movement, Samooga Neethi Katchi, and other organisations gathered at the Coimbatore Collectorate premises, demanding the arrest of all persons, who were accused of having harassed the student and abetted his suicide. They met District Collector Pavankumar G. Giriyappanavar and submitted a petition.

Headmaster, teacher suspended

Meanwhile, the secretary of the government-aided school placed the headmaster and the teacher under suspension on Thursday (October 22). The school management took the disciplinary action after learning about alleged use of caste-related remarks at the workplace. The two persons were placed under suspension to facilitate a fair and impartial inquiry, the orders stated.

(Assistance for overcoming suicidal thoughts is available on the State’s health helpline 104, Tele-MANAS 14416, and Sneha’s suicide prevention helpline 044-24640050.)

World.title: Vaikunta Ekadasi celebrations  to begin on December 9 at Srirangam temple
World.content:
The 22-day Vaikunta Ekadasi festival at the Srirangam Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple will begin on December 9 with the Thirunedunthandagam.

The annual festival is split into ‘Pagal Pathu’ and ‘Ira Pathu’. The Pagal Pathu begins on December 10. The highlight of the festival is the opening of the ‘paramapada vaasal’ in the early hours on December 20 on the holy Ekadasi day when devotees in large numbers are expected to converge at the temple to offer worship to the processional deity Sri Namperumal.

The “Ira Pathu” begins on December 20. As part of the festival, the Thirumangaimannan Vedupari event will be held on the temple premises on December 27. The festival concludes with the “Nammazhwar Moksham” on December 30.

The holy ceremony of ‘Muhurthakaal Naduthal’ (installation of a holy wooden pole) in connection with the Vaikunta Ekadasi festival was held near the thousand pillar mandapam inside the sprawling temple complex on Friday morning.

Elaborate arrangements would be made by the Srirangam temple authorities, the Tiruchi City Corporation and the Tiruchi City police ahead of the festival.

World.title: Airbnb sets down rules to stop hosts from forcing guests to clean homes
World.content:
Airbnb, a company that facilitates travel accommodation agreements between private property owners and visitors, introduced a new rule that restrains hosts from making their guests perform too many household chores before they leave.

Airbnb hosts, as they are called, are allowed to set certain rules and requirements for the upkeep of their homes and apartments. For example, they could require guests to strip the bedsheets after their visit, take their trash to designated areas, do laundry, sweep floors, or run a dishwashing cycle.

Also Read : Airbnb, Tourism Ministry join hands to expand homestays, promote emerging destinations

Airbnb guests and hosts rate and review each other based on their experience, which can affect their standing when hosting future guests or visiting other Airbnb properties.

However, Airbnb guests have for years complained that, on top of being forced to carry out onerous household chores while on vacation, many Airbnb property hosts charge extravagant cleaning fees.

Airbnb has recently settled the debate, by stating in plain language that hosts must be “reasonable” and not use their guests as cleaners.

“For example, hosts are generally not allowed to: Ask guests to complete tasks that require significant effort or time, or would typically be performed by a cleaner, including stripping the bed, taking trash offsite, or washing and putting away dishes,” stated one of the rules in Airbnb’s help centre webpage.

The update has sparked a social media frenzy. Many guests reacted with relief, recounting anecdotes of being forced to do laundry and wash dishes while on holiday—on top of paying a cleaning fee.

Meanwhile, many Airbnb hosts lashed out against the updated rule, pointing out that Airbnb guests could stay at hotels or agree to higher fees if they did not want to do a few light cleaning tasks after their stay. For their part, a number of guests argued that Airbnb prices were almost on par with hotel booking fees—and also required the guest to work while on holiday.

Several hosts found the new rule confusing and felt that more flexibility was required.

“My main issue is it’s letting me ask people to load the dishwasher but I can’t ask them to start it. It’s a weird line to draw when the extra effort is 10 seconds (pop a pod in, press start),” stated one user on a Reddit forum for Airbnb hosts.

Other users pointed out that requiring guests to tidy up as a checkout requirement should not replace professional cleaning or home maintenance services between guests.

“Unless there is a dishwasher, guest should not be doing the dishes. Do you want to eat off dishes that a stranger washed in a hurry?” observed another Reddit user.

On its website, Airbnb also warned hosts not to restrict access to any feature advertised as part of the listing, and also said they could not impose fines or other penalties on guests.

World.title: EPFO, ESIC grievances redress programme to be held in Pollachi and Coonoor on October 27
World.content:
The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) and the Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) will jointly conduct the monthly ‘Nidhi Aapke Nikat 2.0’ grievances redress programme in Coimbatore and the Nilgiris districts on October 27.

In Coimbatore district, the programme will be held at Dr. Mahalingam College of Engineering and Technology, Mackkinaickenpatti, Udumalai Road, Pollachi. In the Nilgiris, the venue will be Stanes Anglo Indian Higher Secondary School, Club Road, Bedford, Coonoor. The programme will be held from 10.30 a.m. to 4.30 p.m. EPF members, ESI insured persons, employers, pensioners and trade unions can visit the venues with details of their grievances.

Individual members and pensioners should provide their Universal Account Number (UAN), Provident Fund account number or insured person (IP) number while submitting grievances.

EPFO-related grievances can also be sent to ro.coimbatore@epfindia.gov.in. Those unable to attend the programme can approach the EPFO district offices in Pollachi, Ooty and Coonoor or the Regional Office in Coimbatore on working days.

World.title: Chevittorma explores environmental and personal loss on stage
World.content:
The Jalam Theatre Company comprising residents of Thuruthippuram in Kerala’s Puthenvelikkara, a district in Ernakulam, brings Chevittorma (A Memoir of the Moribund) to the Ranga Shankara Theatre Festival this year. ‘Chevittorma’ is a practice in some parts of Kerala, where a prayer is whispered into the ear of a dying person unable to say it themself. The play was conceived as a prayer whispered for a community that was being swallowed by the sea, says the organisers.

Ever since the 2018 Kerala Floods disrupted its geography, Thuruthippuram has been hit by tidal waves on a monthly basis and despite the loss of life and property, the occurence failed to register with the government and authorities as a disaster. Its unfailing regularity meant the residents of the area were unable to rebuild their lives or homes, with any assurance for the future.

Director of the play Sreejith Ramanan says, what troubled him the most was not only the physical loss, but also the intangible ones. “When I visited this place, it was full of abandoned homes holding a lifetime of memories. Crumbling walls still had sketches children had drawn on them. Toys and other household items were floating about,” recalls Sreejith.

He continues, “For all of us, our home is one of the most important factors in life and having to give that up is never easy. These images remained in my mind for a long, long time.”

Sreejith was roped in by Equinoct, an organisation working on climate change, to create community-resilience models, one of which was theatre.

“The initial brief was for a street play, but after my visit I realised it wouldn’t make an impact. A unique visual language was needed to carry across the gravity of their situation; that was how the sceneography was developed.”

Conceptualised in 2022 and staged the following year, the cast of Chevittorma comprises the residents of Thuruthippuram. “With the exception of a police officer, a school administrator and a few others, all the cast members are daily wage earners. All of them have had their lives upended by this cyclical disturbance.”

The play is performed in water, and when it was first staged, the cast had no idea it would have such a strong impact on society and governing authorities. As a result, canals were developed between the sea and residential areas to reduce flooding, and now, after several years, cultivation has begun there on a small scale.

Sreejith says experts from Equinoct and others working on this subject, undertook scientific research, community mapping, documentary projects and other initiatives to draw attention to the matter. They believe it was theatre that finally highlighted the issue.

“Until then, it was not deemed a disaster or an emergency, with no financial or other assistance rendered to the victims,” he says, adding, “It has created an awareness that similar incidents are happening all over the world and that environmental justice was the need of the hour.”

Another positive outcome of this project was the creation of Jalam Theatre Company by the people of Thuruthippuram. After its initial staging in Thuruthippuram, Sreejith encouraged the residents to create their own troupe and since then, Chevittorma has been performed by Jalam in other parts of Kerala, in Mumbai and Delhi at various festivals, and now, comes to Bengaluru this weekend.

Sreejith says taking the play to different venues not only gives immense satisfaction, but also has a cathartic effect on the members.

Chevittorma will be staged at Ranga Shankara on October 25 at 7.30pm. Tickets priced at ₹300 on BookMyShow.

World.title: 10 India-sponsored terrorists killed as bid to undermine state's writ in Gwadar foiled: ISPR
World.content:
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Friday that 10 India-sponsored terrorists were killed in separate engagements as security forces thwarted their attempts to “undermine the writ of the state” in Balochistan’s Gwadar district.

In a statement, the military’s media affairs wing said: “On Oct 22, Indian-sponsored terrorists of Fitna al Hindustan attempted to carry out terrorist activities in district Gwadar, in the general areas of the Gabd Border Crossing and Gwadar city.”

The state has designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al Hindustan to highlight India’s role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

“By targeting these locations, terrorists sought to harm the very people they claim to represent and wanted to obstruct the development and prosperity of Balochistan. To protect residents and clear the area, security forces launched clearance operations in and around Gwadar city,” ISPR said.

It said that in separate engagements, security forces foiled the terrorists’ designs and “their bid to undermine the writ of the state and spread their misconstrued agenda”.

“In the ensuing exchanges of fire, ten terrorists, including one female terrorist, were sent to hell. During the terrorist attacks one civilian embraced shahadat (martyrdom) and [a] few vehicles were damaged. Operations were concluded without any loss to security forces, restoring order and writ of the state,” it said.

The statement further said that the coercion of a Baloch woman into the attack was “a crime not only against the state but against the hurmat (respect) of Baloch women”.

“It exposes the terrorists’ cynical exploitation of Baloch women as an instrument of propaganda, intended to inflame public sentiment and lend false sanctity to their campaign. Such tactics are contrary to Baloch and Islamic traditions, which hold women in the highest honour. The people of Balochistan have consistently rejected those who shed blood in their name, and they will see through this deception as well,” it said.

The statement said that the counterterror campaign would continue at full pace.

“Security forces and law enforcement agencies remain resolute in eliminating foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country,” it said.

The ISPR statement comes a day after security sources said that security forces killed three terrorists and foiled an attack on an unoccupied construction company camp in Gwadar.

Balochistan has witnessed an increase in terrorist activities in recent years, prompting security forces to intensify counter-terrorism operations.

Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir said earlier on Friday the armed forces will continue the counterterrorism campaign against Indian-sponsored terrorist groups “to the fullest”, vowing to “hit them hard wherever they are”.

Earlier this week, ISPR said an army major was martyred and four terrorists were killed during intelligence-based operations in Balochistan.

The number of terrorist attacks in the province increased by seven per cent from 83 in July to 89 in August , according to data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS).

As per the report, Balochistan was declared the province “most affected” by terrorism.

Following the latest operations by security forces in Gwadar, President Asif Ali Zardari commended the security forces for foiling the terrorists’ attempts.

“The president also expressed deep sorrow and grief over the martyrdom of a citizen in a terrorism incident,” the statement issued by the Presidency said.

It further quoted President Zardari as saying that efforts to disrupt peace and stability in Balochistan could not shake the people’s resolve for development and prosperity in the province.

He stressed the importance of peace for the protection of the rights and interests of people of Balochistan and said that “using the honour of Baloch women for political interests is condemnable”.

World.title: DPM Dar meets Turkish FM ahead of R-4 bloc, European diplomats’ meetings
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Friday met with Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, ahead of a meeting of R-4 foreign ministers and a meeting between the R-4 and European diplomats, the Foreign Office (FO) said.

The R-4 group, comprising Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, emerged in March and has been focusing on regional security and mediation efforts between the United States and Iran.

In a post on X, the FO said that Dar thanked Fidan for hosting the meetings and that the pair discussed bilateral relations and regional developments, particularly the situation in the Middle East and Palestine.

“They expressed concern over threats to regional stability and underscored the importance of dialogue, diplomacy and coordinated efforts to promote regional peace and security,” the FO post said.

Additionally, Dar and Fidan strongly condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed their commitment to close coordination on regional issues, including under the Makkah Defence Agreement.

“Both leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the longstanding bonds of friendship and brotherhood between Pakistan and Turkiye, and to deepening cooperation across all areas of mutual interest, both bilaterally and in multilateral fora,” the FO added.

Dar left for Istanbul earlier in the day and is attending the meeting at the invitation of Fidan.

In a post on X, the FO said that upon his arrival, Dar arrived in Istanbul and was received by Director General of the Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs Cihad Erginay and Pakistan’s Chargé d’Affaires Shaiq Ahmed.

The FO added that during his one-day visit, Deputy Prime Minister (DPM) Dar would participate in the R-4 and R-4-plus meetings with France, Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom. Dar would also call on Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts, the FO said.

Earlier, FO said that the ministers will participate in a meeting with counterparts from the European E-3 bloc — UK, France, and Germany — following the R-4 meeting.

The E-3 group comprises three European powers that established the grouping more than 20 years ago to advance diplomatic coordination on Iran’s nuclear programme. Italy will also be a part of the meeting, FO had added.

“This will be the first meeting of the seven countries in this format,” FO said.

“The meetings will focus on key regional developments and explore coordinated diplomatic approaches to address shared challenges and advance regional peace and stability,” FO added.

DPM Dar is also set to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts during his visit as well.

“Pakistan’s participation reflects its continued commitment to constructive diplomacy, regional cooperation and the peaceful resolution of disputes,” FO said.

Talks to revolve around Hormuz, Saudi Arabia

British foreign minister Ed Miliband’s office said the talks would essentially revolve around “the Strait of Hormuz and the situation in Saudi Arabia”.

It said Miliband “will advocate for a diplomatic solution to the (Hormuz) crisis that restores full navigational rights and freedoms”.

He will also stress “how Iranian tactics are being replicated across the region, with attacks on Saudi Arabia further destabilising the region and increasing pressure on vital waterways and global chokepoints, such as Bab El-Mandeb and the Suez Canal”, it added.

France confirmed the talks on “the Iranian crisis in its various ramifications”, hailing it as a first “in this format… against a backdrop of extreme instability and uncertainty in the region.”

The meeting will aim to “strengthen coordination between Europeans and Middle Eastern countries in the face of crises that we did not choose and that affect us all,” the French foreign ministry said.

A Turkish diplomatic source also told Reuters a day earlier that the seven countries would meet in the R-4+E-3 format for the first time at Turkiye’s initiative as wars involving Iran , Yemen and Ukraine threaten shipping routes and regional security.

Fidan is expected to emphasise the need for a diplomatic solution to the war between the United States and Iran, the importance of freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb, and reiterate Turkiye’s support for Saudi Arabia’s security against attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement signed by Islamabad, Ankara, and Riyadh, the sources said.

World.title: At least 12 killed, 22 injured in road accident near Zero Point in Balochistan’s Uthal
World.content:
KHUZDAR: At least 12 passengers were killed and around two dozen injured when a minibus and a passenger coach collided head-on near Zero Point in Uthal on the Quetta-Karachi Highway in Balochistan on Friday, police said.

According to police, the coach was travelling from Gwadar to Karachi, while the minibus was heading from Bela to Karachi.

“The tragic incident took place near Bela when the passenger coach hit the minibus,” the officials said, adding that seven passengers were killed on the spot, while five others succumbed to their injuries in hospital.

In-charge of the Edhi Centre in Bela Abdul Hakeem Lasi said around 22 injured passengers were shifted to hospital by Edhi workers before being taken to Karachi for treatment.

He said seven injured passengers were in serious condition. Most of the casualties occurred in the minibus, he added.

The accident occurred two days after 10 people were killed and 44 others injured when a passenger bus overturned after hitting a road divider in Rajanpur district’s Rojhan tehsil on the Indus Highway on Wednesday.

A similar accident occurred last month when two people were killed and 15 others injured in a head-on collision between a passenger coach and an LPG bowser near Balochistan’s Kharkhera Customs on the main National Highway in Winder.

In February, five people, including a local journalist, were killed in two separate road accidents in Winder and Khuzdar districts.

In January, four people were killed and several others injured in a road accident near Wadh in Khuzdar district on the Quetta-Karachi National Highway.

World.title: Insulin product in short supply after German manufacturer halts supplies, NA told
World.content:
An insulin product used by patients with Type 1 diabetes is in short supply in Pakistan after its German manufacturer halted supplies while upgrading its products, Parliamentary Secretary for Health Nelson Azeem said on Friday.

Responding to a matter raised by MNA Syeda Amna Batool in the National Assembly, Azeem said there had been no shortage until June, with stocks available until September. However, supplies from Germany were disrupted in October, leading to the current shortage.

“The impact of the shortage is being felt not just here, but across Asia, as well as in Australia and Europe,” Azeem said. “The product will be available as soon as international supplies are restored.”

The secretary further said alternative insulin products with the same dosage and mode of action were readily available in Pakistan and that patients could switch to them on their doctors’ recommendation.

“The product is manufactured in Germany. It is an issue that we are trying to resolve,” he said.

However, Batool expressed concern about the difficulties patients could face in switching treatments. She said the alternatives were at least 20 per cent more expensive and that many patients did not have access to doctors.

“Currently, around 34.5 million people in Pakistan have Type 1 diabetes, including children,” she said. “Alternatives are not readily available. Has the health ministry or the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (Drap) ensured their easy availability?”

Azeem asserted the German manufacturer had previously supplied 3,500 kits, but supplies had now fallen to 1,000 kits and could decline further during the year-long upgrade process.

He said the health ministry had asked distributors importing the product to arrange supplies, but acknowledged that this would be difficult because the manufacturer had halted production.

On Tuesday, authorities had denied reports of a widespread insulin shortage in the country, saying that only one brand was unavailable.

“Insulin glulisine (Apidra, Sanofi) is currently unavailable due to international supply constraints. Alternate rapid-acting analogues within the same pharmacological class, specifically insulin aspart (NovoRapid, Novo Nordisk) and insulin lispro (Humalog, Eli Lilly), are readily available nationwide,” health ministry spokesperson Sajid Shah had said, adding that all other primary insulin classes remained fully accessible across Pakistan.

In August 2025, the Pakistan Medical Association raised alarm over “an unprecedented” and severe shortage of essential medicines across the country and warned that the crisis threatened the lives of millions of patients.

According to the association, at least 80 important medicines were unavailable, with 25 having no substitutes. These drugs included life-saving medications for diabetes, cancer, Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, heart disease and psychiatric disorders.

World.title: ‘Hit them hard’: CDF Munir vows to continue campaign against Indian-sponsored terrorist outfits
World.content:
Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir has said the armed forces will continue the counterterrorism campaign against Indian-sponsored terrorist groups “to the fullest”, vowing to “hit them hard wherever they are”, the military’s media wing said on Friday.

CDF Munir made the remarks during a visit to the Corps Headquarters in Peshawar, where he was briefed on the security situation, ongoing counterterrorism operations, border management measures and the operational preparedness of formations deployed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said.

Upon arrival at the headquarters, CDF Munir was received by the Peshawar Corps commander.

During his visit, he lauded the morale and professionalism of the armed forces and directed them to maintain “vigilance and the highest standards of operational readiness to effectively counter threats”.

ISPR added that CDF Munir vowed that the armed forces would “continue the campaign against Indian-sponsored terrorist outfits to the fullest and hit them hard wherever they are”.

He also paid tribute to the martyred security personnel, affirming that “with the support of the people, Pakistan will surely inflict total defeat on the terrorists and their perverted ideology”.

A day earlier, CDF Munir attended a meeting of KP apex committee held at the Governor House, where the province’s overall security situation was reviewed. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif who chaired the meeting, said that the federal government, which now runs KP under governor’s rule, would make every effort possible to “bring back” progress to the province.

According to a recent report from the Centre for Research and Security Studies, Pakistan recorded a sharp 83 per cent increase in violence-linked fatalities during the third quarter of 2026, reversing a declining trend reported in the first and second quarters as terrorism and counter-terrorism deaths surged nationwide.

Balochistan and KP remained the epicentres of violence, jointly accounting for 98pc of all fatalities during the period. Balochistan recorded 829 deaths, nearly 59pc of the national total, while KP reported 556 fatalities, accounting for more than 39pc. The increased terrorist activity has prompted security forces to intensify counter-terrorism operations.

A day earlier, four policemen, including two officials, were martyred and two terrorists were killed during an exchange of fire in KP’s Karak.

On October 19, an army major was martyred and four terrorists were killed during intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan.

A day before that, security forces killed eight “India-sponsored” terrorists during IBOs conducted in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts of Balochistan.

World.title: State counsel cross-examines prosecution witnesses in security breach case against Imaan, Hadi
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: A state-appointed counsel on Friday cross-examined all prosecution witnesses in a security breach case against lawyers Imaan Zainab Hazir-Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha.

Imaan and her husband, Hadi, are facing a jail trial in a 2024 case pertaining to the alleged disruption of an international cricket team’s security route and incitement to public unrest.

The couple, accused of removing barriers from the route, was indicted on Oct 7.

Anti-terrorism court Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra presided over the hearing held inside Adiala jail on Friday, during which state counsel Atif Mehmood cross-examined a prosecution witness.

On Saturday, the court will provide Imaan and Hadi with questionnaires under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) to record their statements.

In a hearing on Thursday, the court appointed Mehmood as the state counsel to cross-examine the prosecution witnesses, replacing Taimoor Janjua, who was dismissed over his past conduct.

The court had ruled to appoint the state attorney after the defence counsel failed to cross-examine the prosecution witnesses.

During the last hearing, Imaan informed the court that she and Hadi did not need a state counsel as they already had their own lawyers.

Hadi explained that their lawyers were frequently occupied with other cases at the Islamabad High Court (IHC), while the trial court had scheduled daily hearings at Adiala, making it difficult for them to attend every proceeding.

The court had directed the prosecution witnesses to appear again on Friday, affirming that the cross-examination would proceed without further delay.

Imaan and Hadi’s rearrest

The lawyer couple has been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the IHC and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association president. The arrest prompted criticism by rights bodies, politicians and journalists, who stressed the couple’s right to a fair trial.

Just a day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) in the controversial social media posts case.

The convictions were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts .

On Sept 17, following months of litigation before the courts , the Supreme Court suspended their sentences in the case. The SC ordered their release pending the Islamabad High Court’s final verdict on their appeals against the trial court’s decision.

However, the reprieve was short-lived as hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with another case and produced them before an ATC, which sent them to jail on judicial remand.

The fresh case in which the two were arrested was registered at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station on March 22 last year on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio.

Imaan and Hadi were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads and were nominated by name in the FIR. However, at the time of registration of the case, no section of the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA) had been added.

The FIR included sections 188 (disobedience of an order lawfully promulgated by a public servant), 341 (wrongful restraint), 506 (punishment for criminal intimidation), 353 (assault or use of criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging their official duty) and 186 (obstructing a public servant in the performance of official duties).

World.title: Lahore tops global pollution ranking as air quality turns ‘hazardous’
World.content:
Lahore ranked as the world’s most polluted city on Friday, with its air quality classified as “hazardous”, according to air quality monitoring platform IQAir.

In the past few years, air pollution has become one of the most pressing public health and environmental crises facing Pakistan. Various cities of the country, most notably Lahore , deal with smog, especially in the winter months. The phenomenon is attributed mainly to industrial emissions, vehicular pollution , stubble burning and air movement .

Lahore topped the list of the world’s most polluted cities on Friday morning, with an air quality index (AQI) of 410, according to the IQAir live tracker. The reading fell under the ‘very unhealthy’ category. India’s New Delhi followed with an AQI of 203, while Senegal’s Dakar ranked third at 196.

Figure shows the top ranked polluted cities according to IQAir on Friday morning. — Screengrab via IQAir

The provincial capital was the only Pakistani city to rank among the 20 most polluted cities on Friday morning. Karachi was the only other Pakistani city on the 21-city list, with an AQI of 110.

According to IQAir, in Lahore, “PM2.5 concentration is currently 45.2 times the World Health Organisation annual PM2.5 guideline value”.

PM2.5 refers to fine inhalable particles, with diameters generally 2.5 micrometres and smaller. Of all air pollution measures, PM2.5 pollution poses the greatest health threat, according to IQAir.

According to the website, PM2.5 can enter the circulatory system and even the brain, causing serious health complications if long-term exposure occurs.

A view of the early morning in Lahore on Friday. Photo by Murtaza Ali

For those in Lahore, IQAir recommended avoiding outdoor exercise, keeping windows closed to prevent outdoor air from entering, wearing a mask outdoors and installing an air purifier indoors.

Lahore air quality map. —IQAir

The Punjab government’s air quality monitoring platform, meanwhile, recorded an AQI of 339 for Lahore at 11am on Thursday, classifying the air as ‘very unhealthy’. The reading was based on data from 10 monitoring stations across the city.

The difference between the readings on the two platforms may be due to variations in monitoring stations, averaging periods and methodologies. However, both indicated severe air pollution in the provincial capital.

Human rights activist Sheikh Saqib told Dawn that both his children were suffering from throat infections due to smog. He criticised the government for what he described as empty claims about measures to curb air pollution.

A view of the early morning in Lahore on Friday. Photo by Murtaza Ali

He said school attendance could drop by half as parents stopped sending their children to school amid deteriorating air quality.

Saqib also disputed the chief minister’s claims that smog had been controlled over the past three years, saying he continued to witness crop burning while travelling on motorways towards Islamabad and Karachi.

“Vehicles emitting smoke are still running on Lahore’s roads,” he said, questioning the effectiveness of the government’s measures to tackle air pollution.

On Oct 2, Lahore also topped IQAir’s list of the world’s most polluted cities, with an AQI of 167, classified as “unhealthy”. At the time, CM Maryam said the government was making efforts to address environmental issues.

World.title: China orders 'all-out' rescue after Tibet quake kills 16
World.content:
China ordered an “all-out” rescue effort in Tibet on Friday after an earthquake killed at least 16 people, injured dozens and flattened hundreds of homes, state media reported.

Footage showed rescue workers with torches clambering in the dark through some of the more than 300 houses that Xinhua said collapsed in the 7.0-magnitude quake on Thursday evening.

Diners ran out of restaurants and items fell off wobbling supermarket shelves as the tremor struck, according to clips on state broadcaster CCTV, which said 65 people were injured.

One resident told local media that her family had just gone to bed when her home shook, knocking over objects, and that they “rushed outside without even taking the time to get dressed.”

“My legs were shaking the entire time I was heading downstairs and by the time I reached the bottom, I was so terrified that I burst into tears,” the woman said.

Local residents “are afraid to return to their homes,” she said. “They set up tents along the roadside or spent the night in their cars.”

A man told the Beijing News that the “very strong” quake left his home “creaking and rattling”.

“I was asleep when it hit. Everyone has run outside now and is too afraid to go back in. I’m currently driving to an open area to sleep in my car,” he said.

Broadcaster CCTV also showed emergency personnel with helmets carrying a person and shining flashlights on damaged buildings, some with collapsed roofs.

Tibet is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists and Chinese authorities are the only source of official information.

President Xi Jinping said the tremor caused “significant casualties” and took place at a “high-altitude location” in cold weather.

“(We) must go all-out to carry out search and rescue operations and do our utmost to treat the injured, so as to minimise casualties,” Xinhua quoted Xi as saying.

He called for assistance for residents and rescue equipment to be sent to the area promptly.

The epicentre was in a mountainous area about 190 kilometres east-northeast of Nagqu, and 390 kilometres northeast of the regional capital Lhasa, the US Geological Survey said.

It struck at 10:33 pm (7:33 pm PKT) on Thursday at a shallow depth of around 10 kilometres.

Lhawang Dagpo, a local official in the Maru township, the quake’s epicentre, said it put cracks in the walls of his office, according to Xinhua.

Power and telecoms services were disrupted in the county seat, the agency said.

Baqing County has mobilised more than 1,600 people to help in the relief operation, CCTV reported.

The municipal fire and rescue brigade has dispatched 25 vehicles and 110 personnel, and the Nagqu Armed Police Detachment sent 225 officers and soldiers and 18 vehicles, CCTV said.

As of 4:30 am (1:30 am PKT) on Friday, relief supplies including 1,000 prefabricated houses, 3,239 tents, four generators and 1,000 flashlights had been delivered, it added.

President Zardari, PM Shehbaz extend condolences

President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, in separate statements on Friday, extended their condolences to the Chinese president, the bereaved families and the people of China. Both leaders also reaffirmed Pakistan’s solidarity with China and prayed for the swift recovery of those injured.

In a statement shared by his office, President Zardari “expressed deep sorrow over the loss of lives”.

PM Shehbaz said he was deeply saddened by “the tragic loss of precious lives and injuries caused by the devastating earthquake”.

He added that Pakistan was “ready to extend every possible support”.

Earthquakes in China are relatively common.

In January 2025, a quake in Tibet’s rural Tingri county killed at least 126 people.

The disaster came little over a year after at least 148 people died in a quake in remote Gansu province in northwest China in December 2023, according to state media.

That quake was China’s deadliest since 2014, when more than 600 people perished in the southwestern province of Yunnan.

A massive tremor in 2008 in Sichuan province left about 90,000 people dead or missing, including around thousands of schoolchildren.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers. A practical structure could be a 100 percent tax holiday for the first 10 years, 50 percent for the next 3 years, and 25 percent for the next 2 years. This should apply to CAPEX, OPEX, IPP, and MPP models. A broader 10–20 year tax holiday for renewable energy projects should also be considered.

Bangladesh has a remarkable solar opportunity already waiting on its rooftops. About 7 percent of the country’s land is covered with concrete or other built structures. This means more than 10,000 square kilometres, or about 10 billion square meters of built surface. If only 30 percent is usable, that would give around 3 billion square meters. At 10 square meters per kW, this can create nearly 300 GW of solar potential. Bangladesh’s peak demand is only around 16–18 GW. The opportunity already exists on rooftops, factories, warehouses, schools, hospitals, government buildings, and commercial establishments.

Rooftop solar should therefore be relaunched nationwide with a clear business model. Utility-scale solar also needs support through unused khas land, transparent tendering, and grid readiness. Floating solar, river-based solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage should receive separate policy attention.

The suspended solar projects must also be revisited. A total of 31 solar power projects, with a combined capacity of more than 3,000 MW, were previously suspended or cancelled. Many were being developed by foreign investors, with more than USD 200 million reportedly already invested. If implemented, these projects could save around BDT 10,800 crore annually in energy import costs. They should be reassessed and revived quickly.

Energy storage is another missing pillar. Solar and wind need storage support to become more reliable. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and other storage systems should be reduced to zero. This will help stabilise renewable power and support future grid flexibility.

Electric vehicles can also become part of the solution. In China, Japan, and the United States, EVs are increasingly seen as mobile energy storage systems. A typical EV battery has a capacity of 40–70 kWh, enough to power an average household for 1–2 days. If Bangladesh had 1 million EVs, the country would have 40–70 GWh of distributed storage. This is several times higher than the daily peak demand gap. Solar-powered EV charging, vehicle-to-home, and vehicle-to-grid systems should be included in future energy planning.
